#Swarm User Guide

This guide explains the Swarm system from the ground up: what it is, how to install it on your own PC with your own accounts, how the bots think, and how to use every page of the dashboard. It is written for someone who owns L2Swarm but has never seen our scripts or dashboard.

All screenshots in this guide come from a demo copy of a real running system. Character, party and account names were replaced with demo names (party Aldric, party Borin, party Gromund, party Valerius, party Dravik, solo Quill). Phone shots are 390 x 844, desktop shots 1440 x 900. Yellow numbered circles point at the controls explained in the text.

The same guide as one page with pictures: open index.html in a browser (works offline, also on a phone).

#Rebuilding this guide

Everything here can be regenerated with one command from the install folder:

node docs/guide/tools/make_guide.js

It builds an anonymised copy of your own live data, starts a sandbox copy of the dashboard that cannot reach the game, takes every screenshot with headless Edge or Chrome, regenerates the command reference and index.html, and checks that no real name is left. Details: tools/README.md.

#Getting started

This chapter explains what the Swarm system is made of, what you need, how to install it on your own PC with your own accounts, how to start and stop it, how to update it, how to fix the common problems, and which safety rules to keep. Words you may not know are explained in the glossary.

Contents: 1. What the system is · 2. Requirements · 3. Install on a new PC · 4. swarm.config.json, field by field · 5. Accounts, characters, parties and roles · 6. Scheduled tasks, start and stop · 7. The dashboard · 8. Changing swarm.js: Scripts_dev and deploy · 9. First run checklist · 10. Updating · 11. Troubleshooting · 12. Safety rules

#1. What the system is

The Swarm system has five parts. Only the first one is a product you buy; the rest is in this install folder.

Part What it is Where
L2Swarm The commercial multi-account bot (L2Swarm.exe, a Windows WPF program). It logs every account in, moves, fights and talks to the game server. It has a JavaScript engine (each account runs its own copy of a script) and an MCP server on port 8083 that other programs use to read the bots and send them orders. L2Swarm.exe, Settings\, Data\, Geodata\, Maps\
swarm.js Our script. One copy runs in every account's window. Each copy looks up its own role (tank, healer, destroyer ...) and its party leader, and then behaves as that role. In lead mode the party leader decides everything; the members follow, assist, defend, rest, rebuff and resurrect. See Concepts. Scripts\swarm.js (live copy) and Scripts_dev\swarm.js (the copy you edit)
The dashboard A small web server (Dashboard\server.js, Node.js) on port 8090. It shows every party live (map, HP, what each character is doing) and lets you give any order from a PC or a phone. Dashboard\
Data files Game data and your own choices that the bots read: hunting zones, dungeon rooms, field areas, raid boss data, gatekeeper menus, routes, gear preferences, sell list, party tactics. Most of them are read live, so a change works without restarting anything. Scripts\data\
Tools PowerShell and Node.js tools: setup, start/stop/memory watch, deploy, account creation, data generators. SETUP.cmd, SETUP.ps1, docs\plan\tools\

Two more things are optional:

  • Claude Code. An AI assistant can drive the bots through the same MCP server. CLAUDE.md in the install folder is its operating guide. You do not need it to run the system.

#1.1 How the parts talk to each other

 phone / PC browser ──HTTP──> Dashboard\server.js (port 8090) ──MCP──> L2Swarm.exe (port 8083) ──> game server
                                   │   reads Logs\swarm_state_<Name>.json            │
                                   │   writes Scripts\data\*.json (your choices)      │ runs swarm.js once per account
                                   └── Logs\cmd\inbox.json (backup channel) <─────────┘
  • Every swarm.js window writes its state to Logs\swarm_state_<Name>.json every few seconds. The dashboard reads these files to draw the pages.
  • An order from the dashboard goes to L2Swarm through MCP. A party order is sent as party chat from the party leader (the leader and, depending on the command, every member act on it). A character order is sent as party chat from that one character.
  • When MCP does not answer, the dashboard puts the order into Logs\cmd\inbox.json instead. Every swarm.js window checks that file once a second and runs what is addressed to it. Logging accounts in or out, and some L2Swarm chat-box commands, still need MCP.
  • Windows of the same L2Swarm talk to each other with L2Swarm's App events (for example "I am low on supplies", "I am being hit").

#1.2 Which L2Swarm version

L2Swarm is a closed program by its own developer, and this kit contains none of its files. You need your own L2Swarm install, set up and updated with its own installer / updater.exe. Nothing in the kit changes L2Swarm's program files.

Use L2Swarm 3.8.14 or newer. While running 40 accounts we found a number of bugs inside L2Swarm (a UI deadlock, MCP server hangs, memory growth, hook overhead, a map redraw error) and reported them with their causes; the developer fixed all of them, the last ones in 3.8.14. Older versions (3.8.10 - 3.8.13) still work, but with those known problems. swarm.js finds out by itself which L2Swarm it runs on and adapts; there is nothing to configure.

Never switch .NET "Server GC" on for L2Swarm. In our tests one script reload then grew the process to over 20 GB.

#1.3 Where things are written

Folder What is in it
Settings\<Login>.xml One L2Swarm config per account (login, encrypted password, character, follow settings, scripts).
Settings\settings.xml L2Swarm's global settings: MCP port and the AutoStart list.
Settings\client_mode.json Which characters play with the real game client ("ingame").
Settings\backup\ Every file our tools change is copied here first.
Scripts\data\ Data and your dashboard choices (see 1).
Logs\ LOG.log (L2Swarm's main log), swarm_state_<Name>.json (live state per character), intent_<Name>.log (what each character tried to do, with coordinates), swarm_errors.log, memwatch.log, l2swarm_ctl.log (start/stop), supervisor.log, deploy_swarm.log, dashboard_commands.log (every order sent), and logs per feature (dungeon.log, escape.log, supply_runs.log, raid_reports\, kamaloka.log, clan.log, dawn.log ...). L2Swarm's per-character logs (Logs\<Name>.log) mix lines from several accounts; search LOG.log by login name instead.

#2. Requirements

Thing Notes
Windows 10 or 11 L2Swarm is a Windows program.
L2Swarm 3.8.6 or newer This install runs the version in version.txt (3.8.10 at the time of writing). The scripts check the version and adapt. Install or update with L2Swarm's updater.exe.
Administrator rights L2Swarm.exe always asks for admin (its manifest says requireAdministrator). Setup therefore registers elevated scheduled tasks once, so that the dashboard and normal shells can start and stop it later without a UAC prompt.
Node.js (LTS) From nodejs.org. Needed for the dashboard, the wall-aware path finder (docs\plan\tools\geopath_service.js, started by the dashboard) and the tools. Python is not needed.
Microsoft Edge or Google Chrome Only for rebuilding this guide (headless screenshots). Any browser works for the dashboard itself.
The game client Only for characters that should play in the real game client (clientMode: "ingame"). Out-of-game bots need no client.
RAM See below.
A Lineage 2 High Five server The scripts were built for a High Five server with a free Community Board buffer (Alt+B), free .townname teleports and Cabinet settings such as "Follow Party Leader's Dialog" (the L2Toggle server). Many features depend on these server features.

Memory. L2Swarm's memory grows while it runs (about 1 GB per hour with ~40 accounts), and every reload of swarm.js adds more, because each account's JavaScript engine keeps its memory high-water mark. A PC with 8 GB of RAM crashed after about 165 script reloads in one day. Plan for:

  • 16 GB RAM or more for 20-40 accounts, and a large Windows page file (tens of GB). L2Swarm can then grow to several GB without trouble.
  • Few script reloads. Batch your swarm.js changes and deploy them together (see section 8).
  • MemWatch (a scheduled task) watches the memory and restarts L2Swarm only when the PC is about to run out of memory (see 6.4).

#3. Install on a new PC

Everything machine-specific lives in one file, swarm.config.json in the install folder. Every other part (swarm.js, the dashboard, the tools, the scheduled tasks) finds its paths and ports from that file or from its own location, so the folder can be anywhere (for example D:\Games\L2Swarm). The developer version of these steps is docs\plan\INSTALL.md.

#Step 1 - Copy the folder

  1. Install L2Swarm into a folder of your choice.
  2. Copy the swarm files on top of it: Scripts\ (swarm.js and Scripts\data\), Scripts_dev\, Dashboard\, docs\, Geodata\, Maps\, Data\, Settings\templates\, Settings\*.zmap, SETUP.ps1, SETUP.cmd, SETUP_PC_ALWAYS_ON.cmd, swarm.config.example.json and CLAUDE.md.
  3. Never copy someone else's Settings\*.xml, Settings\settings.xml, swarm.config.json, Logs\, Dashboard\key.txt or Scripts\mcp_script_*.js. The account configs contain encrypted passwords, and L2Swarm's encryption key is the same in every copy of L2Swarm, so anyone with L2Swarm can use them. The files in Settings\templates\ are safe: they have no login, password or character.

#Step 2 - Start L2Swarm once

Run L2Swarm.exe once (it asks for admin) and close it again. It creates Settings\settings.xml. In L2Swarm's settings make sure the MCP server is switched on (SETUP sets its port).

#Step 3 - Write swarm.config.json

Copy swarm.config.example.json to swarm.config.json and edit it. Every field is explained in section 4. Put no passwords in this file.

#Step 4 - Dry run

Double-click SETUP.cmd. This is a dry run: it prints every change it would make and changes nothing. Read the list: L2Swarm groups, account configs to create or change, the AutoStart list, client modes, scheduled tasks, and warnings.

#Step 5 - Apply

  1. Make sure L2Swarm is not running. (While it runs, it saves its own copy of settings.xml and the account configs from memory and can undo the changes.)
  2. Open a command prompt as Administrator in the install folder and run SETUP.cmd -Apply. From a normal prompt it restarts itself as admin, which it needs for the scheduled tasks.
  3. For every account that has no config yet, SETUP asks for the password with a hidden prompt. To avoid typing, set environment variables first in that admin prompt: set SWARM_PW_DEMO01=... (one per login, login in capitals) or set SWARM_PASSWORD=... when all accounts share one password. Only the encrypted password is written into Settings\<config>.xml.
  4. Run SETUP.cmd again. It should report "nothing to do".

SETUP options: -Apply (make the changes), -SkipTasks (do not create or update the scheduled tasks), -Config <file> (another config file), -Force (apply even while L2Swarm runs: not recommended).

What SETUP does (it is safe to run again at any time; every changed file is first copied to Settings\backup\<date>_setup\):

  • creates the folders Logs\, Scripts_dev\ (with a copy of Scripts\swarm.js when missing), Settings\backup\, Settings\templates\;
  • creates Settings\templates\<role>.xml from your roleTemplates (login, password and character removed);
  • creates Settings\<config>.xml for new accounts from the role's template (with docs\plan\tools\new_account.ps1);
  • sets in every account config: login, character, L2Swarm group (= party), login server, server id, game client path, script paths and zone file path of this folder, and the follow settings: members follow their party leader, healers do not assist-attack;
  • writes the AutoStart list in Settings\settings.xml with every entry enabled="false" (the start task logs accounts in one by one, see 6.3) and the MCP port;
  • writes Settings\client_mode.json, Settings\login_gap.txt and a dashboard key file (Dashboard\key.txt) when missing;
  • registers the scheduled tasks L2Swarm Start, L2Swarm Stop, L2Swarm Restart and L2Swarm MemWatch for this folder.

#Step 6 - Optional: a 24/7 PC

If the PC (for example a laptop) should run day and night, double-click SETUP_PC_ALWAYS_ON.cmd and accept the admin prompt. It runs docs\plan\tools\pc_alwayson.ps1, which:

  • sets lid close, sleep, hibernate, hybrid sleep and wake timers to "do nothing" / "never" on all power plans;
  • switches off power saving for Wi-Fi, USB and network adapters;
  • switches off Windows Update, Store auto-update, Delivery Optimization and automatic maintenance (a forced update reboot logs every bot out);
  • registers the four scheduled tasks;
  • keeps a backup and a report in Settings\backup\. Undo with docs\plan\tools\pc_restore.ps1 (as admin).

Think about this step: it changes Windows settings for the whole PC.

#Step 7 - Start

  1. Start the bots: schtasks /run /tn "L2Swarm Start", or the Start button on the dashboard's PC page once the dashboard runs. A plain double-click on L2Swarm.exe logs nobody in (on purpose, see 6.3).
  2. Start the dashboard: double-click Dashboard\start.cmd (see section 7).
  3. Optional, Claude Code (once per PC): claude mcp add --transport http --scope user l2swarm-mcp http://127.0.0.1:8083 (use your mcp.port). Then start Claude Code in the install folder.

Then work through the first run checklist.

#4. swarm.config.json, field by field

JSON has no comments, so the example file keeps its help text in keys that start with //. These keys are ignored. Here is a complete example for a small setup with demo values:

{
  "version": 1,
  "paths": { "root": "", "l2Client": "C:\\Games\\L2Client\\system\\l2.exe" },
  "server": { "name": "MyServer", "loginIp": "203.0.113.10", "loginPort": 2106, "serverId": 1,
              "gameIp": "203.0.113.10", "gamePort": 7777 },
  "mcp": { "port": 8083 },
  "dashboard": { "port": 8090, "keyFile": "Dashboard\\key.txt" },
  "login": { "gapSeconds": 8 },
  "mainLeader": "Aldric",
  "clanLeader": "Quill",
  "dailyLeaders": ["Aldric", "Borin"],
  "groups": { "format": "Party {party}", "overrides": { "Quill": "Solo Quill" } },
  "scripts": ["swarm.js"],
  "roleTemplates": { "sk": "Demo01.xml", "bishop": "Demo02.xml", "destroyer": "Demo03.xml", "default": "Demo03.xml" },
  "healerRoles": ["bishop", "shilliensaint", "healer"],
  "legacyConfigs": [],
  "accounts": [
    { "login": "demo01", "character": "Aldric",  "party": "Aldric", "role": "sk", "note": "main leader" },
    { "login": "demo02", "character": "Bryndis", "party": "Aldric", "role": "bishop" },
    { "login": "demo03", "character": "Cassius", "party": "Aldric", "role": "destroyer" },
    { "login": "demo10", "character": "Borin",   "party": "Borin",  "role": "crafter" },
    { "login": "demo11", "character": "Kestrel", "party": "Borin",  "role": "spoiler" },
    { "login": "demo12", "character": "Liora",   "party": "Borin",  "role": "healer", "clientMode": "ingame" },
    { "login": "demo40", "character": "Quill",   "party": "Quill",  "role": "dagger", "note": "levels alone" },
    { "login": "demo41", "character": "", "party": "Aldric", "role": "nuker", "autoStart": false,
      "classPlan": ["Elven Wizard", "Spellsinger", "Mystic Muse"], "note": "character not created yet" }
  ]
}

#Top-level fields

Field Meaning Used by
version Format version of the file (1). -
paths.root The install folder. Leave it empty: then it is the folder the file is in. Set it only if the config file lives somewhere else. everything
paths.l2Client Full path of the game client's l2.exe. Only needed for characters with clientMode: "ingame". SETUP writes it into their account config. SETUP, client mode
server.name A label for your server. -
server.loginIp, server.loginPort, server.serverId The login server and the game server id. SETUP writes them into every account config. SETUP
server.gameIp, server.gamePort The game server. Only used to test whether the server is up (the reconnect brake, 11). start/stop tool
mcp.port L2Swarm's MCP server port (default 8083). SETUP writes it into settings.xml. Change it only if 8083 is taken. SETUP, dashboard, tools
dashboard.port The dashboard's web port (default 8090). dashboard, start.cmd
dashboard.keyFile The file that holds the dashboard password for phone/LAN access. SETUP creates it when missing. SETUP, dashboard
login.gapSeconds Seconds between two account logins when the bots start. Never below 5: the login server refuses mass logins. Default 8 when not set. SETUP also writes it to Settings\login_gap.txt (that file wins if you edit it later). start task
mainLeader The character that leads the main party. It is the default leader for every character without its own party, and it may give commands to everyone. swarm.js, dashboard
clanLeader The character that owns (or will found) the clan: clan jobs, clan level, clan quests, sieges. swarm.js, dashboard
dailyLeaders Party leaders whose party can run the daily Kamaloka. The dashboard's Kamaloka page shows an on/off switch for each. dashboard
groups.format Name of the L2Swarm account-list group per account. {party} is replaced by the party leader's name, so "Party {party}" gives "Party Aldric". SETUP
groups.overrides Party leader -> another group name, for example a solo character: { "Quill": "Solo Quill" }. SETUP
scripts Script files (in Scripts\) every account starts with. SETUP adds missing ones to each account config. Normally ["swarm.js"]. SETUP
roleTemplates Role -> an existing account config used as the template for new accounts of that role. SETUP copies it once to Settings\templates\<role>.xml without login, password and character. default is used for roles without a template. On a new PC the existing files in Settings\templates\ are used. SETUP
healerRoles Roles that never assist-attack (FollowAtk off in their config). Default bishop, shilliensaint, healer. SETUP
legacyConfigs Old config files in Settings\ that SETUP must leave alone. They are never put in the AutoStart list, and SETUP warns if they are there. SETUP
dailyHallTeam Optional. Up to 6 character names that form the team for a Kamaloka Hall (Halls allow at most 6 players). swarm.js
teamRoutes Optional. Party leader -> a level-route file in Scripts\data\, for a party that should level along its own route, for example { "Borin": "support_route_h5.json" }. swarm.js
accounts One entry per game account (next table). everything

#Fields of each account

Field Meaning Default
login The account login name. Required. -
character The character to play on that account. L2Swarm selects it by name. Empty = not created yet (the account is set up, but swarm.js ignores it). empty
config File name of its L2Swarm config in Settings\. login with a capital first letter + .xml (demo01 -> Demo01.xml)
party The character name of its party leader. The leader has its own name here. Parties are always named after their leader. its own character (= a party of one)
role Its swarm.js role (see 5.4). Without a role swarm.js ignores the character. -
classPlan Optional. The three class names for the class changes at levels 20, 40 and 76, as they appear on the Community Board's Career page, for example ["Elven Wizard", "Spellsinger", "Mystic Muse"]. Needed for roles whose class depends on the race (nuker, and dagger if not a human Rogue). the role's default path
master Optional note: which master account it belongs to. -
autoStart true = logged in by the L2Swarm Start task. false = SETUP creates the config, but the start task does not log it in. true
enabled false = ignored everywhere (SETUP, swarm.js, dashboard). true
clientMode "oog" = out of game (network only, no game window) or "ingame" = the real game client through L2Swarm's Hook button. See Concepts: client mode. "oog"
note Free text. -

swarm.js reads the roster (character -> role, party, class plan) from swarm.config.json every time the script starts. A new account therefore needs no change in swarm.js: add it here, run SETUP, start it.

#5. Accounts, characters, parties and roles

#5.1 Adding an account

With SETUP (recommended):

  1. Stop L2Swarm (dashboard PC page -> Stop, or schtasks /run /tn "L2Swarm Stop").
  2. Add a line to accounts in swarm.config.json.
  3. Run SETUP.cmd (dry run, check the list), then SETUP.cmd -Apply as admin. It asks for the new account's password once.
  4. Start L2Swarm again.

By hand with new_account.ps1: docs\plan\tools\new_account.ps1 -Login demo42 [-Character Name] creates a ready-to-login config. Without -Password it asks for the password with a hidden prompt (or reads it from the environment variable named by -PasswordEnv). It encrypts the password with L2Swarm's own EncryptPassword function, the same format L2Swarm writes when you save a config in its window. Options: -Template (another template; default Settings\templates\default.xml), -Scripts (scripts to start with), -OutFile.

Password rules:

  • Never write a password in plain text in any file (not in swarm.config.json, not in notes, not in scripts).
  • Never set a password through MCP's manage_account_config modify Password: it saves an empty password, and the account can no longer log in.
  • Remember that Settings\*.xml files are only as safe as L2Swarm's encryption: do not share them.

#5.2 Creating characters

A new account usually has no character yet. You have two ways:

  • Dashboard, Accounts page, "New character": enter the login (and the password once, only if the account has no config yet), the start class, the sex and an optional name. The dashboard creates the config if needed (with new_account.ps1), logs the account in and loads a small one-off script that creates the character at the character-select screen (it retries every 5 seconds). Progress goes to Logs\create_chars.txt.
  • Dashboard, Clan page, "New accounts (Academy)": creates the config, logs in and creates the character from a preset class path, adds the account to Settings\start_extra.txt (logged in after the normal list) and to Scripts\data\roster_extra.json (its role), so it levels on its own without editing swarm.config.json. Progress goes to Logs\academy.log.

After the character exists, put its name into character in swarm.config.json and run SETUP, so it gets its party, group and follow settings.

The dashboard sends the password you type to its own server on your PC. Only use these forms on your own PC or your own home network.

#5.3 Parties and leaders

  • A party is all accounts with the same party value. That value is the party leader's character name, and the party is always called by that name ("party Aldric"), in the dashboard and in every message.
  • SETUP makes every member follow its leader in L2Swarm (follow distance from the template, FollowAtk on, except healers).
  • The main leader (mainLeader) leads the main party. Every other party leader leads his own party in exactly the same way.
  • A character whose party is its own name and that is alone is a solo character (it levels alone).
  • swarm.js forms and repairs the in-game party by itself: the leader invites missing teammates, and members accept invites only from their own team. If someone else became party leader, the right leader gets the leadership back.

#5.4 Roles

The role decides what swarm.js does with a character. The Community Board buff scheme and the default class path come from the role.

Role What it does Board buffs Default class path (20 / 40 / 76)
sk Tank and usual party leader. Uses Aggression whenever it is ready, area aggro when 2 or more monsters are on him, Ultimate Defense in raids when his HP drops fast. Defender Palus Knight / Shillien Knight / Shillien Templar
bishop Healer. Only heals, never attacks (not even in self-defence): fastest heal on anyone dying, group heal when several are hurt, cures debuffs, Recharge for casters, resurrection. Mystic Cleric / Bishop / Cardinal
destroyer Melee damage dealer. In raids: lowers its own HP below 30 % first, then opens with Frenzy, Zealot, Guts, Battle Roar and Rage when the tank has the boss. Warrior Orc Raider / Destroyer / Titan
doombringer Kamael melee damage dealer. Warrior Trooper / Berserker / Doombringer
necromancer Caster damage dealer; puts debuffs on raid bosses. Mystic Wizard / Necromancer / Soultaker
inspector Kamael support damage dealer (played as Soul Breaker / Soul Hound): party buffs Dark Weapon and Pride of Kamael, dark debuffs on raid bosses, soul attacks. Warrior Trooper / Soul Breaker / Soul Hound
doomcryer Orc buffer: Chant of Victory and Magnus' Chant (the board cannot give them), Chant of Life when the party is hurt, the party buff wave in boss fights. Mystic Orc Shaman / Warcryer / Doomcryer
shilliensaint Healer like the bishop; in raids it also debuffs the boss, but only while everyone is above 80 % HP. Mystic Shillien Oracle / Shillien Elder / Shillien Saint
crafter Dwarf crafter: keeps its best golem summoned and sends it at the target. Warrior Artisan / Warsmith / Maestro
spoiler Dwarf spoiler: Spoil and Sweeper on the monsters. Warrior Scavenger / Bounty Hunter / Fortune Seeker
healer Elven healer, same rules as the bishop. Mystic Elven Oracle / Elven Elder / Eva's Saint
nuker Mage damage dealer. Set classPlan (it depends on the race). Mystic (set per account)
dagger Fighter, typically a solo character. Warrior Rogue / Treasure Hunter / Adventurer

Healer roles (healerRoles) never assist-attack. Party members of every role follow the leader, defend themselves and their teammates, rest when low, rebuff from the board and resurrect the dead. See Concepts.

#6. Scheduled tasks, start and stop

#6.1 The four tasks

L2Swarm needs admin rights, so it is started and stopped through four elevated scheduled tasks. Anyone (the dashboard, a normal command prompt, Claude Code) can run them without a UAC prompt. Each task runs docs\plan\tools\run_hidden.vbs, which runs docs\plan\tools\l2swarm_ctl.ps1 -Action <action> without a console window. Everything they do is logged in Logs\l2swarm_ctl.log.

Task Action What it does
L2Swarm Start start Refuses if a start already runs or the AutoStart list looks wrong. Starts L2Swarm, waits for MCP, then logs the accounts in one by one (6.3). Checks three times afterwards that everyone is really in game and logs in the missing ones again.
L2Swarm Stop stop A hard stop of every L2Swarm process (a polite close would pop a "really quit?" dialog and re-save settings.xml). Also closes game clients that L2Swarm started; a client you started yourself is left alone. Leaves the file Logs\l2swarm_stopped.flag, so MemWatch does not start it again.
L2Swarm Restart restart Stop, wait 5 s, start.
L2Swarm MemWatch watch Runs every 2 minutes (6.4).

Run them from a command prompt: schtasks /run /tn "L2Swarm Start" (or Stop, Restart). The dashboard's PC page has the same buttons.

#6.2 Starting and stopping

  • Start: dashboard PC page -> Start, or schtasks /run /tn "L2Swarm Start". With many accounts the logins take a while (number of accounts x the login gap).
  • Stop: dashboard PC page -> Stop (a destructive order: it asks you to type YES), or the Stop task.
  • Before a planned stop (an update, a patch, a long break), send every party to a town first, for example with !town giran from the dashboard. Characters that are standing in a hunting ground when the connection drops stay in the world for a while and can die there.
  • Never stop or deploy while the Start task is still logging accounts in. Check with schtasks /query /tn "L2Swarm Start": it must no longer say "Running".
  • Never restart during a raid or a Kamaloka run. The dashboard shows a banner while one is live.

Two optional files control which accounts the Start task logs in:

File Meaning
Settings\start_extra.txt Extra config paths, one per line, logged in after the AutoStart list (accounts created on the dashboard are added here).
Settings\start_hold.txt Config file names, one per line (for example Demo07.xml), that are not logged in.

#6.3 Staggered login

The login server has flood protection. When L2Swarm's own AutoStart logs every account in within a few seconds, the server refuses all of them for about 5 minutes. Therefore:

  • SETUP writes the AutoStart list into settings.xml with every entry disabled (enabled="false"); the start task disables them again if needed and keeps a copy in Settings\backup\settings_before_stagger.xml.
  • The start task opens the accounts itself, one after another, login.gapSeconds apart (default 8 s, never below 5; Settings\login_gap.txt overrides it), in the AutoStart order, main leader first.
  • A manual start of L2Swarm.exe therefore logs nobody in. Always start through the task or the dashboard.
  • With no enabled AutoStart account, L2Swarm creates an empty default account called "Bot #1" (no login, no config), and makes a new one whenever the list becomes empty. The start task closes it right after the first real account is open, and once more at the end.
  • The start task refuses to run when the AutoStart list does not contain the main leader's config, or contains configs of retired accounts. This protects you from logging in an old team by accident.
  • After a mass disconnect the reconnect brake takes over (see 11).

#6.4 MemWatch, the watchdog

The L2Swarm MemWatch task runs every 2 minutes and keeps watching every 10 seconds within each run. It logs one line per check to Logs\memwatch.log (ok / WARN / HIGH / RESTART). It:

  • starts L2Swarm when it is not running (a crash), unless the Stop task left Logs\l2swarm_stopped.flag or a start is already running;
  • warns when L2Swarm uses more than 4.5 GB, but does not restart just because L2Swarm is big;
  • restarts L2Swarm only when the PC is about to run out of memory (less than about 3 GB of free commit memory, i.e. RAM plus page file), at most once per 30 minutes, and never while a raid or Kamaloka fight is live, unless it is an emergency (below about 1.5 GB);
  • restarts on the UI deadlock of unpatched L2Swarm versions: when MCP fails 3 times and scripts hang or 5+ characters stopped writing their state, it logs DEADLOCK RESTART and restarts (at most once per 15 minutes);
  • runs the reconnect brake after mass disconnects;
  • applies the client modes (Settings\client_mode.json, see Concepts);
  • raises L2Swarm's process priority to Normal and switches off Windows power throttling for it, so it is not parked on slow cores.

The thresholds are at the top of docs\plan\tools\l2swarm_ctl.ps1. Every restart logs all accounts in again, which takes minutes and breaks what the parties were doing, so keep the restart rules strict.

#6.5 The script supervisor

The dashboard has its own watchdog for scripts: when a character's Logs\swarm_state_<Name>.json is older than 90 seconds while the account is logged in, the dashboard stops and starts swarm.js on that account (Logs\supervisor.log). Limits: one restart per character per 5 minutes, 6 per hour in total, and none while L2Swarm uses more than 3 GB (every restart costs memory). To switch it off (for example while you stopped the bots on purpose), create an empty file Logs\pause_supervisor.

#7. The dashboard

#7.1 Starting it

  • Double-click Dashboard\start.cmd. It reads the port from swarm.config.json, opens http://127.0.0.1:8090 in your browser and runs node server.js in that window. Closing the window stops the dashboard.
  • To run it detached (no window), from PowerShell: Start-Process node -ArgumentList server.js -WorkingDirectory <install folder>\Dashboard -WindowStyle Hidden
  • The dashboard also starts the path-finder service (docs\plan\tools\geopath_service.js) as a child process; the bots ask it for wall-aware routes. It is restarted automatically if it dies.

Restarting it (needed after a change to Dashboard\server.js): stop the node process that runs server.js, then start it again. Changes to index.html and the other page files need only a page reload in the browser.

On an unpatched L2Swarm, killing the dashboard while it has an MCP request open can stop L2Swarm's MCP server until L2Swarm restarts (see 1.2). Restart the dashboard when nothing is being sent, or accept that MCP may need an L2Swarm restart afterwards. Orders still reach the bots through the file channel meanwhile.

#7.2 Opening it on a phone

  • On the PC itself the dashboard needs no password.
  • Every other device must send the key from Dashboard\key.txt: open http://<PC-IP>:8090/?key=<the key>. Without the right key the server answers "Access denied". Save the full link as a bookmark on the phone.
  • The dashboard listens on your local network only as far as your router allows. Never forward port 8090 to the internet. Anyone with the link and key can give orders to every bot.
  • If the phone cannot connect, allow Node.js through the Windows Firewall for private networks.

How to use the pages: Dashboard basics and the page chapters listed in the README.

#8. Changing swarm.js: Scripts_dev and deploy

L2Swarm watches Scripts\swarm.js. Every write to that file reloads the script on every account at once, which interrupts what they are doing (walks and purchases start over) and leaks memory. Therefore:

  1. Never edit Scripts\swarm.js. Edit Scripts_dev\swarm.js.
  2. Batch your changes.
  3. Deploy with docs\plan\tools\deploy_swarm.ps1, or the Deploy swarm.js button on the PC page (destructive: it asks you to type YES).

What the deploy tool checks (every result is written to Logs\deploy_swarm.log):

Check Result
No difference between the two files "SKIP: no changes"
node --check finds a syntax error refused
The last deploy was less than 15 minutes ago refused (the PC page then offers "Deploy anyway?", which forces it)
A raid or Kamaloka fight is live (Logs\raid_live.json / kamaloka_live.json updated in the last minute) refused
Accounts are still logging in (the start lock Logs\l2swarm_starting.lock is held) refused
Otherwise copies the file: a live reload on every account

-Force skips the time gap, the live-fight check and the login check (it is still logged). Use it rarely: several forced deploys in a row have pushed L2Swarm's memory up by gigabytes within minutes. The tool can also do a restart deploy (stop L2Swarm, copy, start with the staggered login) above a memory threshold set at the top of the script; at most one per hour, because it logs every account in again.

After a reload, activities that were running resume from Logs\activity_<Name>.json.

Files that need no deploy. Almost everything in Scripts\data\ is read live by the bots: hunting zones, chosen hunting spots, party tactics, gear preferences, the sell list, Giran routes, raid routes, field areas, dungeon rooms (re-read when the file changes). Change them on the dashboard; no deploy, no restart.

#9. First run checklist

  1. version.txt shows L2Swarm 3.8.6 or newer.
  2. swarm.config.json exists and has your server, your mainLeader and every account (no passwords in it).
  3. SETUP.cmd (dry run) shows only expected changes; SETUP.cmd -Apply ran as admin with L2Swarm stopped; a second SETUP.cmd says "nothing to do".
  4. schtasks /query /tn "L2Swarm Start" (and Stop, Restart, MemWatch) shows the four tasks.
  5. In Settings\settings.xml, <AutoStartEntries> lists only the accounts you want, all with enabled="false".
  6. The game server answers (the start task tests the game port only for the reconnect brake; if in doubt, try a login by hand first).
  7. Start: schtasks /run /tn "L2Swarm Start". Watch Logs\l2swarm_ctl.log: "opened " lines, then "everyone is in game".
  8. Start the dashboard (Dashboard\start.cmd). The Parties page shows every party with live HP and positions. A character whose row is faded and says "offline" ("not reporting for ... (offline or script stopped)") has no running swarm.js.
  9. Look at Logs\LOG.log and Logs\swarm_errors.log for errors.
  10. In game, check once per character: Community Board (Alt+B) -> Cabinet -> Settings. The swarm expects "Follow Party Leader's Dialog", "Follow Party Leader's .town" and "Quick Trade" (Party) on. You can switch them for a whole party with !cabinet <setting> on.
  11. Give a first harmless order from the dashboard, for example !status to one party, and see the answer in party chat / the timeline.
  12. Give !level to one party and watch it regroup in Giran and travel to a hunting spot (the Parties map and the What they do timeline).
  13. Open the dashboard on your phone with the ?key= link.
  14. Check Logs\memwatch.log after an hour: memory grows slowly and nothing restarts.

#10. Updating

#L2Swarm

  1. Read what changed (the developer's changelog).
  2. Send every party to a town (!town giran) and wait until no raid or Kamaloka is running.
  3. Stop L2Swarm (PC page -> Stop).
  4. Back up the install folder (at least Settings\ and the L2Swarm program files).
  5. Run L2Swarm's updater.exe.
  6. Check Settings\settings.xml: AutoStart list and MCP port (run SETUP.cmd to see any difference).
  7. Start L2Swarm with the Start task. swarm.js reads version.txt and adapts by itself.

#swarm.js

Edit Scripts_dev\swarm.js, then deploy (section 8).

#The dashboard

Replace the files in Dashboard\. A change to server.js (or commands.js, sieges_api.js, polyedit_api.js) needs a dashboard restart (7.1); a change to index.html or the other page files needs only a browser reload (the server sends the page with "no-cache").

#Data files

Files in Scripts\data\ are read live. Edit them on the dashboard where possible (zones, spots, rooms, routes, gear, tactics, sell list). The shape editor keeps the last 50 versions of every file it changes in Scripts\data\history\.

#Your accounts

Change swarm.config.json, then stop L2Swarm, run SETUP.cmd / SETUP.cmd -Apply, start again (5.1).

#11. Troubleshooting

Find your symptom, then follow the fix. The dashboard pages that help most: Parties (live state per member), Character page (one character in detail), What they do (timeline of intents), and PC (L2Swarm memory, start/stop, deploy).

#The dashboard shows nothing, or "MCP not answering"

Cause Fix
The dashboard is not running. Start Dashboard\start.cmd.
"Access denied" on the phone. The link needs ?key= with the exact key from Dashboard\key.txt.
L2Swarm is not running or still starting. PC page -> Start, or the Start task. MCP comes up a few seconds after L2Swarm.
MCP is switched off in L2Swarm, or the port is wrong. Run SETUP.cmd (it sets the MCP port) with L2Swarm stopped; check L2Swarm's settings.
A game client left over from a previous run still holds port 8083. The Stop task closes clients L2Swarm started; close any remaining l2.exe by hand, then start L2Swarm.
On unpatched L2Swarm: the MCP server stopped accepting connections after an MCP client was killed. Restart L2Swarm (planned, parties in town). Fixed in L2Swarm 3.8.12. Meanwhile most orders still work through the file channel.
The parties show, but every member row is faded and "not reporting". swarm.js is not running. Check Logs\swarm_errors.log, the script list of an account, and Logs\supervisor.log.

#A character's script is frozen

Signs: its row on the Parties page is faded and says "not reporting for ... (offline or script stopped)"; Logs\swarm_state_<Name>.json is older than 90 seconds.

Cause Fix
The script died or hangs. The supervisor restarts it after 90 s (see 6.5). Look in Logs\LOG.log for "ExecutionWatchdog" (a script blocked for too long) and in Logs\swarm_errors.log.
All characters froze together, MCP does not answer (unpatched L2Swarm up to 3.8.10). The UI deadlock. MemWatch detects it and restarts L2Swarm (DEADLOCK RESTART in Logs\memwatch.log). Until a fixed L2Swarm or the patch is installed, swarm.js makes party members fight with script attacks to make it rare.
The supervisor is off. Delete Logs\pause_supervisor if you do not need it any more.

#L2Swarm's memory keeps growing

Cause Fix
Normal growth (about 1 GB per hour with ~40 accounts). Nothing to do. MemWatch restarts only when the PC is nearly out of memory. Make sure the page file is large.
Many swarm.js reloads (deploys, saving Scripts\swarm.js directly). Deploy at most every 15-20 minutes, batch your edits, never edit Scripts\swarm.js.
Sudden jumps of several GB within minutes. Check Logs\memwatch.log and what the parties were doing (long walks with path finding were a cause before). The restart rules in 6.4 handle the emergency.

#Login refused, or mass disconnects

Cause Fix
Too many logins at once: the login server's flood protection refuses everyone for about 5 minutes. Always start through the Start task (staggered login). Keep login.gapSeconds at 5 or more.
"Login rejected: 3". The account does not exist on the server, or the login is wrong.
The server itself is down or restarting. The reconnect brake (in MemWatch): when 3 or more accounts are offline for 3 minutes, or the game port is closed, it closes them (this stops L2Swarm's own retry storm), waits 3, 6, 12, 24, then 30 minutes between tries, tests the game port, logs one account in, and only when that one is in game logs the others in one by one. State: Logs\reconnect_brake.json; "brake:" lines in Logs\l2swarm_ctl.log.
Some accounts were never opened by the start. The start task checks three times and opens them again. Otherwise use the dashboard's "Log in" order for that character.

#A character cannot move, or sees no NPCs

Cause Fix
After a teleport (or a login) the server waits for the client's Appearing packet, which L2Swarm does not always send. The character then sees no NPCs or monsters and every move is ignored. swarm.js sends it automatically after every teleport, after the script starts, and every 20 s while the character sees nothing. Test: the character's NPC list is empty while it stands in a town.
The character sits (resting). A sitting character cannot walk. swarm.js stands up before every walk, gatekeeper or .town. If you sat a character down by hand, send /stand.
Wedged in terrain. swarm.js clicks its way free in 16 directions at several distances and heights for up to 6 minutes, then uses the free .townname, and the leader regroups the team in Giran. /unstuck is the last resort (a destructive order: it waits up to about 5 minutes in place, then goes to the nearest town).
Running into a wall in a dungeon room. The escape and pull-back code uses the wall-aware path finder; make sure the dashboard (which runs the path finder service) is running.

#A party will not go to a catacomb or necropolis

The only way in is the Gatekeeper Ziggurat, and only characters registered in the Seven Signs may use it (on the winning side during the seal validation period). The swarm signs everyone up with the Lords of Dawn during the competition period. Until then such a dungeon is "closed"; a dashboard choice shows "closed (Seven Signs) -> auto · until ". See Concepts: Seven Signs and the Seven Signs box on the Clan page.

#A character in in-game mode is not found by name

A character that runs in the real game client (hooked) is reported by MCP as "not logged in" and without its character name, so a call with its name fails ("No account matches"). Address it by its config path or account id. The dashboard already retries with the config path.

#Trades fail

Cause Fix
System message 142 "... is on another task": the receiver has a shop window open. The receiver closes its shop window first and the giver retries 3 times (automatic).
The receiver was walking. Receivers stop, stand up and pause following during a trade (automatic).
A hanging trade blocks every NPC click. swarm.js cancels stuck trades.
The server asks for a confirmation. Switch on Quick Trade (Party) in Alt+B -> Cabinet -> Settings for every character (!cabinet Party on).

#Buying or selling at an NPC does nothing

On some servers L2Swarm's own buy/sell call is silently ignored. swarm.js then sends the shop packets itself. A merchant that does not answer is skipped for one hour (Logs\shop_fail.json). In Giran the characters walk only along the recorded town routes (Teleports page -> Giran town routes); a broken route makes them miss the shop.

#A dashboard order "did nothing"

  • Every order is logged in Logs\dashboard_commands.log, with the answer.
  • A party order is acted on by the leader; members only follow. If the leader is busy with something more important (an escape, a raid, a supply run), the order waits or is refused. The character's note line and the timeline say why.
  • After !stop, a party waits for orders until the next order (an automatic pause after a wipe ends by itself after 15 minutes).

#12. Safety rules

  1. Passwords are never written in plain text, never shown, and never set through MCP. Only SETUP / new_account.ps1 (and the dashboard's new-account forms, which call it) write them, encrypted.
  2. Every order on the dashboard asks for confirmation: it shows who gets it, how many characters, who is busy and will change what it is doing, and who is offline. Destructive orders (for example /unstuck, /trade, /leave, force attack, /sellitem, /config set and /config load, !enchant, log out, L2Swarm stop/restart, deploy, the full escape test) need a second confirmation where you type YES, and the server refuses them without it.
  3. Trades with players outside your own teams need your explicit decision every time. Trades inside your teams (supplies, adena, gear) are automatic.
  4. Do not edit account configs or settings.xml while L2Swarm runs. L2Swarm saves its own copy from memory and overwrites your change. Stop it first, then edit (or run SETUP), then start. Copy a file to Settings\backup\ before you edit it by hand.
  5. Never point an account at another config file (for example "save config as" a scratch file): the account then uses that file from then on. The dashboard refuses /config save <file> for this reason.
  6. The AutoStart list must not log in retired accounts. Keep old configs in legacyConfigs and check <AutoStartEntries> before a start.
  7. Keep the dashboard key private, use the dashboard only on your local network, and never expose port 8090 (or the MCP port 8083) to the internet.
  8. Do not share Settings\*.xml, settings.xml, swarm.config.json, Dashboard\key.txt or Logs\ when you give the folder to someone.
  9. No restarts or deploys during a raid or Kamaloka, and none while the Start task is still logging accounts in.
  10. Delete configs or accounts only on purpose, after a backup.

#Concepts: how the swarm works

This chapter explains the ideas behind the bots' behaviour. Each section says what it does and how you control it (the dashboard page and the command). Commands are typed in the dashboard's command center or picked from a party's "Commands" sheet; the full list is in the command reference. Unknown words: see the glossary.

Contents: Lead mode · Parties · Priorities · Survival, rest and healing · Board buffs · Hunting spots · Hunting pairs · Travel rules · Supply runs · Adena · Class changes · Gear and enchanting · Raids · Kamaloka · Seven Signs · Escape and rescue · Sieges · Clan · Client mode · Memory and deploys

#Lead mode: the leader decides

What it does. Every party has one leader (usually the tank). The leader's swarm.js window decides everything for the party: where it hunts, when it travels, when it buys supplies, which raid boss it fights. The members have no plans of their own. They:

  • follow the leader and assist him (they attack what he attacks; healers never attack);
  • defend themselves and every teammate who is being hit;
  • rest (sit) when their HP or MP is low and nothing hits them;
  • rebuff from the Community Board when their buffs run out or after a death;
  • resurrect the dead (one teammate is chosen for it; a resurrection skill is preferred over a scroll);
  • run the fast survival loops (potions, self heals, escape when left alone in a fight).

The leader regroups the team before every trip, never leaves anyone behind (a teammate who is stranded or far away makes the whole team regroup in Giran), and buys and hands out what the team needs. When a party has nothing to do for 3 minutes, its leader starts leveling by himself.

How you control it. Give orders to the party (they go to the leader). The main ones: !level (go leveling), !supply (supply run), !stop (stop everything and wait for orders), !town <town>, !mission raid <boss>, !raidhunt. Watch the result on the Parties page and the What they do timeline.

After !stop the party waits until your next order. An automatic pause (for example after a raid wipe) ends by itself after 15 minutes and the party goes back to leveling; the Parties page shows "waiting for orders since ...".

#Parties are named after their leader

What it does. A party is all characters whose party field in swarm.config.json is the same leader name. The party is always called by that leader's name: "party Aldric", "party Borin". The dashboard, party chat messages and the logs all use this name. A character alone in its own party is a solo character and levels alone.

How you control it. Change party (and role) in swarm.config.json, then run SETUP with L2Swarm stopped (see Getting started).

#Priorities P0 to P6

What it does. Every window runs many loops at once. Only one task at a time holds the control of the character (or of the team, for the leader). A more important task takes control from a less important one; the less important one notices and steps aside, and less important tasks wait until control is free.

Level Task
P0 Survive heal, potions, run away when alone, respawn
P1 Unfreeze Appearing packet, click free from terrain, .town as a last resort
P2 Team safety help teammates under attack, resurrect the dead, regroup anyone left behind (Giran)
P3 Safe teleport fight off monsters, move to a safe spot, everyone together and out of combat
P4 Orders your orders: !stop, !supply, !collect, !level, missions, raid hunt
P5 Leveling pick a spot, travel together, hunt
P6 Upkeep rebuff, class change, selling

Long tasks (walks, waits at checkpoints, gathering the team, the regroup before a teleport, Giran routes) check whether they were interrupted and stop cleanly. Survival (heals, potions) and the Appearing packet run in their own fast loops and never wait for control.

How you control it. You do not set priorities; you see them. The dashboard shows each character's current task, and a refused order says which task holds control. An order you give is P4: it interrupts leveling and upkeep, but not an escape or a rescue.

#Survival, rest and healing

What it does.

  • Everyone: below 25 % MP a Mana Potion (every 6 s); below 45 % HP the best self heal it knows; below 30 % HP with no heal a Healing Potion. Casters that know a heal stop attacking below 35 % MP.
  • Rest: a character sits down below 40 % HP (casters also below 20 % MP) when nothing hits it, and stands up at 85 % HP / 70 % MP or when attacked. It never sits in a town, while far from its leader, or while a more important task owns the team. A sitting character cannot walk, so swarm.js stands up before every walk.
  • Healers only heal (bishop, shillien saint, healer roles): never an attack, not even in self-defence. Each tick: the fastest heal on anyone below 40 %, a group heal when 3 or more are below 70 %, cures for debuffs, a normal heal below 75 %, Recharge for casters below 40 % MP. In raids and dungeons they heal anyone below 80 % and drink Mana Potions freely.
  • Hive help: everyone attacks a monster that hits a teammate nearby; the dead are resurrected by the one chosen teammate.
  • Ignored monsters: Treasure Chests are never attacked (they hit hard and are not worth it); a character hit by one steps away.

How you control it. Nothing to set. Character state, HP/MP bars and cast bars are on the Parties and Character pages.

#Board buffs

What it does. Buffs come for free from the server's Community Board (Alt+B -> Buffs -> a scheme -> Buff Me). One click gives 18-28 buffs that last 12 hours. The scheme depends on the role: Defender (tank), Warrior (melee fighters, dwarves, dagger), Mystic (casters and healers).

  • Every window checks its buffs every 10 seconds. It needs a rebuff after a death, or when fewer than 10 buffs have more than 5 minutes left.
  • The leader keeps a rebuff queue (the revived first, then whoever's buffs end soonest). One character at a time leaves the fight, waits until its combat flag is gone (the board refuses buffs in combat), clicks through the board (3 tries) and goes back. The others protect it meanwhile. A failed turn waits 5 minutes before the next try; with no answer from the leader for 2 minutes the character buffs itself.
  • Boss fights: nobody leaves the fight. The doomcryer gives the whole party Warrior buffs with "Buff Party", then every caster adds Mystic on top; at most one wave a minute, and after 2 failed waves they stop until the fight ends.
  • While board buffs are on, characters do not cast their own self-buffs. Exceptions are party buffs the board cannot give: the doomcryer's Chant of Victory and Magnus' Chant, and the Soul Breaker's Dark Weapon and Pride of Kamael.
  • Toggle skills (for example Vicious Stance, Accuracy) are switched on only in a fight and off in towns and about 12 seconds after the fight.
  • A Kamaloka instance removes all buffs on entry; the board works inside.

How you control it. !buff (rebuff now, one at a time), !buffauto on|off (automatic rebuff), !raidbuff (a boss buff wave now). Each member's buff state shows on the Parties page (a chip when buffs are low).

#Hunting spots

What it does. The leader chooses where the party levels. There are four kinds of places:

Kind What it is Where you see / edit it
Custom zones Your own zones per level range, for all parties or for one party (Scripts\data\custom_zones.json). Zones
Datapack spots Hunting spots generated from the game's spawn list (Scripts\data\hunting_spots_h5.json). Spots
Dungeon rooms Every room of the dungeons, catacombs and necropolises as an outline, with levels, entry and walk route (Scripts\data\dungeon_rooms.json). A party hunts inside one room and only attacks monsters in it. Rooms
Field areas Outdoor hunting grounds cut into areas along walls, cliffs and height steps (Scripts\data\field_areas.json), with levels, safe spots and the way in from the nearest landing. the spot picker on Parties

All four can be reshaped in the shape editor.

Automatic choice (Auto). The leader picks for the party's lowest level, in this order: the party's own fitting zones, the level route zones near its level, another party's zone for this level, the party's route file, a free field area, datapack spots (busy ones first), and as a last resort a route zone up to 8 levels lower. It skips:

  • spots on the skip list (a failed trip, "occupied", too few kills);
  • spots claimed by another of our parties (Logs\spot_claims.json; a claim is refreshed every minute and dropped after 3 minutes) and anything within 1500 of another party's hunting centre on the same floor. When two of our parties share a big zone, the later one moves into a sub-area of it;
  • catacombs and necropolises the Seven Signs rule closes;
  • landings where monsters are more than 6 levels above the party's highest level (the danger rule).

An automatic spot is left when the party gets fewer than 3 kills in 5 minutes, too little exp, monsters more than 2 levels below it on average, or when it outgrows the spot. The hunting area is the spot's circle or square times 3 (rooms and areas use their own outline), and members who drift away walk back to it. Nobody fights inside a town.

Occupied by other players. While hunting, the leader checks every 10 seconds. When 2 or more foreign players (not ours, not in the party or clan; private stores do not count) stay inside the area for 2 minutes, the spot is "occupied": skipped for 30 minutes and the party moves on. If another of our parties is in the same area, the one with the newer claim yields.

Manual choice (dashboard). On the Parties page, "Hunting spot: ... Choose…" opens a full-screen picker:

  • one or more rooms of a dungeon (across floors), "Any free room", or one or more outdoor areas of a hunting ground ("Select all fitting");
  • the order for several rooms/areas: nearest next, or in your order. The party rotates: it stays while it fights; after about 35 seconds without monsters it moves to the next one that should hold at least 3 monsters, skipping occupied and claimed ones; on the same floor or in the same region it walks, a room on another floor is reached through the floor teleporters;
  • stay even if occupied: never give the spot up because of other players;
  • move on when outgrown: when the party's lowest level is more than 3 above the monsters there, the choice ends by itself and the party goes back to Auto. Without this box, a chosen spot is never given up for few kills or low monsters (the party only says so in party chat every 30 minutes);
  • level override: a spot above the safe level asks "Yes, override" / "Save without override". Without the override the party hunts an automatic spot and the line says "needs your OK";
  • a closed catacomb/necropolis can be saved anyway; it waits until the Seven Signs let the party in;
  • Back to auto ends the choice.

A new choice takes effect within seconds: walks and waits step aside, and the party goes there (a supply run that is already running finishes first, without gear and dye shopping). It waits during raids, Kamaloka, escapes and rescues, and while a teammate below 50 % HP is fighting. The choice is saved in Scripts\data\party_spots.json; the Parties page shows its live status (travelling, ETA, in the room, occupied, waiting).

How you control it. !level (go leveling), !autolevel stop (stop leveling), !dungeon <name> / !dungeon off (level inside a catacomb or necropolis), !assist <name> / !assist off (the party hunts around another character to help him). Pages: Parties (picker, map, status), Zones, Spots, Rooms, Shape editor.

#Hunting pairs

What it does. A party with many damage dealers can split them into small groups, each with its own monster, instead of everyone hitting the same one. Only while leveling (never in raids, Kamaloka, missions, travel or towns). The leader gives each group a monster within the leash distance of himself and close enough to every teammate for the exp to count (party range). Healers keep healing, spare dealers assist the leader. Monsters hitting a healer are taken first. The party goes back to focus fire at once when someone drops below the fallback HP, someone dies, or too many monsters are on the team (then 2 minutes before groups may form again).

Modes: off (default), on, or auto (only when the party has enough dealers, the monsters are not above its level plus a margin, the HP average was at least 70 % for a minute and nobody died in the last 10 minutes). Settings: group size (1-3), max groups, leash, zone size, minimum dealers, level margin, fallback HP, include the doomcryer.

How you control it. The "Tactics" box of each party on the Parties page (saved in Scripts\data\party_tactics.json, read live). Switches are announced in party chat and logged in Logs\tactics.log.

#Travel rules

What it does.

  • Towns only with .townname. The server teleports you and your party for free with .giran, .dion, .aden and so on (11 towns: Gludin, Gludio, Dion, Giran, Oren, Aden, Hunters, Heine, Goddard, Rune, Schuttgart). The swarm never chains town-to-town gatekeepers and never uses a Scroll of Escape to travel.
  • Gatekeeper only for town -> field. The last step from a town to a hunting ground uses that town's gatekeeper. With "Follow Party Leader's Dialog" on (Cabinet setting), only the leader clicks and the server takes the party along.
  • Regroup before every teleport. The leader first fights off every monster on any teammate, moves away from aggressive monsters to a safe spot, waits until everyone is within 900 and everyone is out of combat for 10 seconds, says "teleporting: X in 3 s" in party chat, then ports. He never ports while a teammate in his area is still fighting.
  • After a teleport the leader waits about 10 seconds (the team loads in) and holds a roll call. Members the server did not take along use the same .town themselves; the leader waits until the whole team is there.
  • Never walk out of a town. Leveling trips teleport to a field landing and walk from there (exception: raid routes you recorded yourself).
  • Giran is the hub: every trip to a new spot regroups there first. Inside Giran the characters walk only along the recorded town routes (start, grocer, warehouse, weapons, armor, jewelry, blacksmith, symbol maker).
  • Danger rule: a field teleport is refused when monsters near the landing are more than 6 levels above the party's highest level.
  • Nobody is left behind: a teammate reported left behind, or more than 15000 away for 90 seconds, makes the leader regroup the whole team in Giran.

How you control it. !town <town> (the party goes there together), !gk <destination> (gatekeeper teleport), !park [place] (the party goes to Giran and waits at a recorded place), !goto <place>, !soe (retreat: everyone leaves the fight and goes to town). The Teleports page shows every gatekeeper menu and edits the Giran town routes.

#Supply runs

What it does. The leader buys for the whole team in Giran at the grocer Helvetia and hands out each member's share by trade.

  • Each member reports what it lacks: Scroll of Escape (top up to 5), Scroll of Resurrection (to 3), soulshots or spiritshots for its weapon grade (fighters up to 10,000, casters up to 5,000, when below 2,000), Mana Potions (up to 2,000 when below 500), Spirit Ore for a tank's cubics, Healing Potions.
  • The leader buys the total, then trades each member its share at the Giran start point.
  • The same run also does: gear upgrades and safe enchanting, dyes, selling junk and marked items, unloading the leader's full bag to the teammate with the most free slots, and adena collection. Only characters that have something to buy, draw or sell walk to a shop. One summary line per run (with each step's time) goes to party chat and Logs\supply_runs.log.
  • Automatic: every window checks every 30 seconds whether it is low (fewer than 2 Scrolls of Escape, no Scroll of Resurrection, fewer than 200 shots, fewer than 100 Mana Potions, fewer than 5 Healing Potions) and the leader starts a run by himself. A run also happens at a Giran regroup when the last one is more than 30 minutes old. At most one automatic run per 30 minutes (not during raids or missions, not after !stop).

How you control it. !supply (also !restock), !sell [name] (sell now). The items to sell are chosen on the Character page (saved in Scripts\data\sell_list.json). Supply state per member is shown on the Parties page (chips for low SoE, shots, buffs).

#Adena: collect and hand out

What it does.

  • Collect: members trade the adena above what they should keep to their leader: 2M below level 40, 2.5M at 40-75, 3M at 76+. Amounts below 50,000 are not traded. Loot goes to the leader anyway (Cabinet "Forward Drop to Party Leader").
  • Cross-party funding: a rich party leader (above 30M) standing in Giran tops up characters of other parties that are already in Giran: a party leader to 8M (he buys the team's supplies), a member to 3M. Nobody is called away from hunting for it. Logged in Logs\fund_log.json.
  • Trades inside your own teams are automatic. Trades with anyone else are never done by the bots.

How you control it. !collect (to a party). Adena per character is on the Parties and Character pages.

#Class changes

What it does. Class changes go through the Community Board: Alt+B -> Career -> Professions, at levels 20, 40 and 76. The window clicks the button that contains its next class name from its class plan (the role's default path, or classPlan in swarm.config.json). When a character reaches the level, its leader orders the change automatically (once per level). The pages are saved to Logs\career_<Name>.html. There are no class quests.

How you control it. !classchange [name]. The class plan is in swarm.config.json (see Getting started); current classes show on Parties.

#Gear upgrades and enchanting

What it does.

  • At every supply run (and with !gearup / !upgrade) each character compares the Giran shops' equipment with what it wears and buys better pieces it can afford, keeping 300,000 adena. Fighters and tanks buy the cheap Common versions (same stats, no set bonus); casters and healers buy the real armor sets, with a Common weapon and jewelry. A worn special-ability weapon or an enchanted piece of the same grade is never replaced. Kamael weapons are bought as swords and changed with Change Weapon.
  • Enchanting: worn real pieces up to the safe limit, +3, or +4 for a full-body armor, with normal scrolls only. Common items are never enchanted (the server refuses them).
  • Dyes (symbols): planned per role, bought and drawn at the symbol maker in Giran.
  • Gear found as loot is not put on or traded around automatically; it goes to the leader.

How you control it. The Gear page: the items each class buys per grade and your preferred item per class and grade (saved in Scripts\data\gear_prefs.json, read live). Commands: !gearup [name] (party to Giran, everyone buys and wears upgrades), !gearplan [name] (dry run, writes Logs\gear_plan_<Name>.json), !upgrade [name], !enchant [name] (destructive: typed YES), !dyes / !dyeplan.

#Raids

What it does. Raid bosses are not aggressive, so the party fights them on its own terms:

  1. Stage: the team walks to about 1500 from the boss and stops. A raid only goes on when the team got within 3000 of the boss; a boss the team cannot reach twice is skipped for good (Logs\raid_unreachable.json).
  2. Clear the area: every other monster within 2000 of the boss (never the boss or its minions) is killed first, one target at a time, with every damage dealer on it.
  3. Countdown: gather, raise the dead, count down in party chat (10, 5, 3, 2, 1, GO).
  4. Pull: the tank pulls and keeps the aggro (Aggression whenever ready, area aggro on loose minions, Ultimate Defense when his HP drops fast). Destroyers lower their HP below 30 % before the pull and wait; healers leave them alone meanwhile. The moment the tank has the boss they fire Frenzy, Zealot, Guts, Battle Roar and Rage, and the healers heal them up. The leader sets one focus target for all damage dealers: minions first, then the boss. Debuffers (tank, necromancer, Kamael, shillien saint) put their debuffs on the boss.
  5. Never escape from a raid. The party fights until the boss dies or the last of them falls. No Scroll of Resurrection in a raid; the resurrection skill only when every living teammate is above 85 % HP. The shillien saint debuffs only while everyone is above 80 %.
  6. After a kill everyone picks up the loot. After a wipe the party stops and waits (an automatic pause, 15 minutes).

Raid curse: a raid boss and its minions curse anyone more than 8 levels above them. The swarm uses the lowest level of the boss and its minions and never pulls a boss that would curse a member.

Raid hunt (!raidhunt [min max]): the party works through the raid bosses, lowest level first. It skips bosses that would curse it, bosses more than 3 levels above its lowest member, dungeon bosses and unreachable ones, and stops at the first wipe or timeout.

How you control it. !mission raid <boss>, !mission stop, !raidhunt / !raidhunt stop, !routetest <boss> (walk the route without fighting), !jointraid <boss> with <parties> [cc <leader>] (several parties together, in a Command Channel if the leader has the right), !loot. Pages: Raid bosses (boss list, route editor, reports) and the Raid live view.

#Kamaloka dailies

What it does. Every leader whose daily switch is on checks every minute for a Kamaloka his whole party fits (level window; Halls take at most 6 players, Labyrinths at most 9) that was not done today (the day starts at 06:30 local time). Leveling or a raid hunt steps aside after the current boss or spot, the party travels to the captain, enters and fights, then the previous activity resumes. At most 2 tries per Kamaloka per day; "may not re-enter yet" counts as done. The leader enters only when he sees every online teammate within 900. Inside, the team holds a spot, the tank pulls one monster at a time and everyone hits the focus target; healers stay back and heal.

How you control it. The Kamaloka page (which Kamaloka fits which party, done today, daily on/off per party leader listed in dailyLeaders, a Run button, maps) and the Kamaloka live view. Command: !mission kamaloka [level]. Logs: Logs\kamaloka.log, Logs\daily.log.

#Seven Signs

What it does.

  • Every character signs up with the Lords of Dawn, never Dusk. Leaders take their party to the Priest of Dawn in Giran during the competition period and sign everyone up, one at a time. On a server where Dawn costs a fee or an item, the bot logs the page and stops.
  • Catacombs and necropolises: the only way in is the Gatekeeper Ziggurat, and only for characters who are registered (during the seal validation period: only the winning side). The rule is checked before any trip. When the dungeon is closed, the party does not travel at all; the spot is skipped until the period changes ("possible again from ").
  • The swarm reads the period from the priest's first page (at most every 6 hours) and calculates the weekly change (Monday 18:00 server time).
  • Optionally the characters hand in their seal stones at the priest.

How you control it. !dawn (sign up now). The Seven Signs box on the Clan page shows the period, the last winner, the next change and every character's state (Dawn / Dusk / not registered, may enter or closed). Each member row on Parties has a Dawn/Dusk mark. Logs: Logs\dawn.log, Logs\sevensigns_state.json.

#Escape and rescue

What it does.

  • Alone in a fight (no teammate who can fight nearby on the same floor; for a healer after 6 seconds, for others when HP is below 50 %, 3 or more attackers, or after 45 seconds): the character escapes. It puts a crowd-control skill on the attacker if it has one (sleep, fear, stun, root, ...; healers may too, it is not an attack), runs to a walkable safe spot (a dungeon floor's safe spot, a hallway outside the rooms, or open ground out of every aggro range; the wall-aware path finder plans it), stands still until nothing has hit it for 7 seconds (self heals, potions, crowd control again), then uses .townname. If the server refuses that (still in combat), it uses a Scroll of Escape while standing still. When the leader announces he is coming, the character holds at the safe spot instead and waits for him.
  • Rescue: the leader walks to a teammate who is fighting alone (up to about 15 minutes away), across dungeon floors through the floor teleporters if needed, and kills what is on him. Members left behind click the same teleporters.
  • Never in a raid (raid rules apply there) and never during a siege.
  • Every escape writes one line to Logs\escape.log.

How you control it. It is automatic. !soe makes the whole party retreat to town. !escapetest [name] runs the real escape in test mode (crowd control only on a monster within 900, stops before the teleport); !escapetest <name> full goes all the way (destructive: typed YES). The escape box, its live map and the cast bar appear under the member's row on Parties; see Party live states.

#Sieges

What it does. Fortress and castle sieges with several of your parties together: you plan the siege (target, time, which parties, regroup time, Command Channel leader, flag carrier, commander assignment, regroup point outside the siege zone); at the regroup time the parties stop, regroup in Giran, travel to the regroup point, wait for each other, form the Command Channel and fight the objectives in order. A fortress needs clan level 4, a castle clan level 5. Like raids, nobody escapes during a siege. This feature has not been used in a real siege yet.

How you control it. The Fortresses and castles pages (map, details, planner, plans list) and the Siege live view. Commands: !siege plan <plan>, !siege fort <fort>, !siege castle <castle>, !siege stop, !siegereg fort|castle <name> (the clan leader registers).

#Clan

What it does.

  • The clan leader (clanLeader in swarm.config.json) founds the clan by himself when he is level 10 or higher and stands in a town (at most 3 tries a day; the name comes from Scripts\data\clan_quests.json), then invites teammates who stand next to him.
  • Clan level: !clanlevel checks what the next level needs (SP, adena, an item, reputation, members), says exactly what is missing, or levels the clan up at a village master. !clanlevel auto on does it by itself when everything is there.
  • Clan quests: !clanquest <quest> [step] runs the automated steps of the clan level quests; some steps are manual (the dashboard says which).
  • Academy: accounts flagged as academy members are invited into the academy once the clan is level 5 and they are level 40 or lower.
  • Clan focus skill (!clanskill), clan warehouse view (!clanwh).

How you control it. The Clan page: a sub-tab per clan, level and reputation checklist, clan quests, clan events (joint raids with a Command Channel), raid team templates, Seven Signs, new academy accounts.

#Client mode: in game or out of game

What it does. A character runs either out of game ("oog": network only, no game window, the normal way) or in game with the real game client through L2Swarm's Hook button (you can watch it and play it by hand). The wanted mode per character is in Settings\client_mode.json. MemWatch applies it every 2 minutes: for "in game" it logs the network session out, starts l2.exe, injects the hook and types the login. Because that typing goes to the window in front, it only hooks when nobody has used the mouse or keyboard for 60 seconds, at most 3 times per character per hour. "Out of game" closes that client and logs the account in normally again. Log: Logs\client_mode.log.

Hooked characters cannot be found by name over MCP; the dashboard uses their config path instead (see Troubleshooting).

How you control it. The Character page: Client: In-game / Out of game (or the "Client mode" commands). The default for new accounts is clientMode in swarm.config.json.

#Memory and deploy discipline

What it does. L2Swarm's memory grows while it runs, and every reload of swarm.js on all accounts adds more. Too many reloads have crashed a PC. The safeguards:

  • you edit Scripts_dev\swarm.js, never the live Scripts\swarm.js;
  • deploy_swarm.ps1 copies it at most every 15 minutes, never during a live raid or Kamaloka, never while accounts log in;
  • MemWatch restarts L2Swarm only when the PC is nearly out of memory, never during a live fight unless it is an emergency;
  • the script supervisor restarts a dead script at most 6 times an hour;
  • data files are read live, so most changes need no deploy at all.

How you control it. The PC page (L2Swarm memory and threads, Start / Restart / Stop, Deploy swarm.js). Details: Getting started, sections 6 and 8.

#Other features

  • Soul crystals: fetching crystals, using them on monsters, storing finished ones (!soul get, !soul store, !soul on|off): the Crystals page.
  • The plan: the Plan page.
  • Every command with its arguments, who acts on it and its safety class: the command reference.

#Dashboard basics

The dashboard is a web page that shows every character, party and running fight, and lets you give orders. It runs on the PC that runs L2Swarm (Dashboard/server.js) and works the same on a PC screen and on a phone. This chapter explains what is the same on every page: how to open it, the header, the tabs and page addresses, how the page refreshes, and every kind of confirmation and message you can meet. Words you may not know are in the glossary.

#Opening the dashboard

On the PC that runs the bots: double-click Dashboard\start.cmd. It starts the dashboard server and opens http://127.0.0.1:8090 in your browser (the port comes from swarm.config.json, dashboard.port). Pages opened on this PC need no key.

On a phone or another PC in the same network: open http://<the PC's network address>:8090/?key=<key>. The key is the text in Dashboard\key.txt on the PC. Without the right key the server answers "Access denied: open the link with ?key=...".

  • The page remembers the key in the browser (local storage). After the first visit you can open http://<address>:8090/ without ?key=, and bookmark or add it to the home screen.
  • Keep the key private: anyone with the key can give orders to your characters.
  • The page is built for a phone held upright (390 px wide) and for a desktop. Everything works by tapping; keyboard shortcuts are extras.
  • Game icons, the item and skill tables load without the key (they hold no secrets); everything else needs it.

#The header

  1. Title - "Swarm".
  2. Status line - N/M characters reporting · updated HH.MM.SS. M is every character the dashboard knows, N how many of them wrote their status in the last 30 seconds. A character that stops reporting is offline, frozen or its script is stopped. The time is the last refresh. If the server cannot be reached, this line says "Dashboard server not reachable: ..." instead.
  3. Search or give an order... - the command center. Tap it (or press Ctrl K, or / when no text field has the focus) to find a character, a party, a page or a command and send orders. On a desktop the field shows the Ctrl K hint.
  4. Tab strip - one button per page (see below).
  5. Commands - on every party card (Parties tab) and on every character page: opens the command center with every command that fits that party or character. The button only appears once the command center has loaded.

Under the status line the header also holds the message line and the live banners (both explained below). They take no space when empty.

#The old "Tell them" bar

Before the command center existed, the header had a simple order bar. It is still in the page and comes back by itself only when the command center cannot load (for example an old server.js that does not serve commands.js). Normally you never see it.

  1. Who - a party ("Party Aldric") or one character ("Bryndis only").
  2. Free text - a phrase such as "restock", "kill raid boss Bifrons" or "teleport Gludio", or a !command. The server turns phrases into commands (the table is in the command reference).
  3. Send - asks the order confirmation, then sends.

#Message line

The line under the search field shows the answer to the last thing you did. It stays until the next message replaces it.

  1. A green tick (game "yes" icon) means it worked: for orders it shows the command, the target and how many sends went out, for example !status → party Aldric (1/1 sent). The characters confirm it in their notes. "Sent" means the order reached the game window; whether the character could do it shows a few seconds later in its notes (Parties tab, character page, "What they do").

  1. A warning sign (game "!" icon) means it did not work, followed by the reason, for example don't understand "dance a jig" — try level, supply, collect, ....

Every message that can appear there:

Message Where it comes from
sending to <name>… Old order bar and quick buttons, while the order is on its way.
✓ <command> → party <name>. The character confirms it in its notes. Quick buttons (Status, Level, Supply ... on a party card, Class change / Rebuff / Escape on a character page), the task menu with Do, the old order bar.
