✓ <command> → <target> (n/m sent). The characters confirm it in their notes. Command center, after Send. With - sent via file channel - ... when L2Swarm's control interface (MCP) did not answer and the order went through the file channel instead.
⚠ <reason> Any of the above when the server refused the order (unknown command, unknown party, destructive without confirmation, nobody to send it to ...) or could not be reached.
type the boss / town / place in the box next to the menu first The task menu with Do: the chosen task needs a word in the box next to it.
<name>: ingame — applied within ~2 min / <name>: oog — ... Client mode buttons on the character page (with a warning text in brackets when the server adds one), or <name>: <error>.
start… restart… stop… deploy…, then the program's answer or ... sent — status updates in about 15 s PC tab buttons.
✓ <leader>: <daily dungeon> ON / OFF Parties tab, daily dungeon switches.
✓ sell list saved — the bots use it at their next town visit Sell setting of an item in a character's bag (character page).
✓ saved — <slot> for <class> (<grade>) set / back to automatic Gear tab preferences.
✓ zone saved — auto-level picks it up on its next check Zones tab.
creating…, then ✓ <name> is being created on <login> — it appears here when logged in Accounts tab, new character.
✓ soul crystal plan saved Crystals tab.
✓ <what was saved>, clan name: 2-16 letters/digits Clan tab.
pick a dungeon and a level range (min ≤ max), tick at least one party, ✓ spot added: <dungeon> Spots tab, adding a dungeon spot.
siege plans saved, siege plan: <error>, set the siege time first Fortresses / Castles tabs.

Some pages also have their own small message spot next to their buttons (for example the zone editor's "saved — the bots use it on their next spot check", "give the zone a name", or the new-account form's "creating…"). Those pages explain them.

#Live banners

While a raid, a Kamaloka run or a siege is running, a red banner with a pulsing dot appears under the header on every page. It is the quickest way to notice that a fight is on. Tap a banner (Watch ›) to open its live view.

  1. LIVE raid - boss name, boss HP %, how many of the team are alive (7/9 alive) and the fight time. Opens the raid live view (#/live). Hidden while you are on that view.
  2. LIVE Kamaloka - which Kamaloka, the phase (Travel, Enter, Rebuff, Fight, Loot), alive count and time. Opens the Kamaloka tab with the live view. Hidden while you are on the Kamaloka tab.
  3. LIVE siege - fortress or castle, phase (Regroup in Giran, Travel, Regroup outside, Waiting for the start, Siege: objectives, Flag / artifact), objectives done, who holds the flag, alive count and time. Opens the siege live view (#/siege/live). Hidden while you are on that view.

A banner shows while its live file is fresh (written by the leader within the last 30 seconds) and the run is not finished. The page checks for a running raid every second, for a Kamaloka run every 3 seconds (every second while one runs) and for a siege every 8 seconds (every 2 seconds while one runs), so a banner can take a few seconds to appear.

#Tabs and page addresses

  1. The open tab is drawn pressed and in gold.
  2. On a phone the tab strip is one row that scrolls sideways: swipe it to reach the tabs on the right. On a desktop it wraps or scrolls (a mouse wheel over the strip scrolls it sideways). Opening a page scrolls its tab into view.

Every page has its own address after #. The browser's back and forward buttons work, you can bookmark any page, and you can send a link to a single character or boss. Pages that are not tabs (character page, raid boss page, live views, editors) are opened from links on other pages or from the command center; while one of them is open, the tab it belongs to stays highlighted where it makes sense.

Names in addresses are written as they are (#/char/Bryndis); spaces and special letters are encoded by the browser.

#Refreshing

  • The page asks the server for the newest state every 4 seconds and redraws only what changed. Some tabs load extra data on their own timer (Teleports every 15 s, Raid bosses every 30 s, PC every 15 s, Clan every 4 s, Fortresses / Castles every 15 s, Kamaloka every 20 s, live views every 1-2 s while they run).
  • While the page is hidden (another browser tab, the phone screen off) it does not refresh at all, so it costs nothing. When you come back it refreshes at once.
  • The redraw keeps what you are doing: the text you are typing, an open drop-down list, a ticked box, opened sections and the scroll position stay as they are. You can fill a form calmly while the numbers around it change.
  • Lists in drop-downs are only rebuilt when their choices really change, so an open list does not close under your finger.
  • The page remembers small things per browser: the dashboard key, which command-center categories you keep open, your recent orders, the last target you used, timeline settings. Clearing the browser's site data forgets them; nothing on the PC changes.

#Look (the L2 skin)

The dashboard uses the game's own interface textures (window frames, buttons, tabs, gauges, list headers) and the game's item, skill and class icons, in one dark theme on every page. There is no light theme. Colours mean the same everywhere: gold = headings and links, green = good / done, yellow = warning, red = problem, danger or offline, blue = moving / resting.

#Confirmations

Nothing that changes the game is sent without asking first. There are four kinds of question.

#Order confirmation (confirmOrder)

Shown by the quick buttons on a party card (Status, Level, Supply, Collect, Class, Buff, Stop), the task menu with Do, the quick buttons on a character page and the old order bar. It names:

  • the target: Send to the WHOLE party Aldric (9 characters): or Send to Bryndis only:,
  • the order in words and the exact command in brackets,
  • Busy right now and will change orders: <names> when members of that party are doing something (leveling, a trip, a fight). Idle characters and plain L2Swarm farming do not count as busy.

OK sends it, Cancel sends nothing. The command center has its own, more detailed version (see Command center: Confirm).

#Typed confirmation (destructive orders)

Orders that cannot be undone or can hurt (for example /unstuck, /leave, /trade, enchanting, logging a character out, restarting or stopping L2Swarm, deploying the script) ask a second time and only go out when you type YES (capital letters) into the box. Anything else, or Cancel, means "not sent". The server itself also refuses a destructive order that did not come with this second confirmation.

#Yes / no questions on pages

Simple browser questions with OK and Cancel. Cancel always means "do nothing". The full list:

Page Question (short)

The spot editor also has one text question: when you tap a landing where several gatekeeper teleports arrive, it asks Which teleport? with a numbered list; type the number.

#Choice dialogs (more than two answers)

A few questions need more than yes or no. They open as a small window inside the page, in the game skin, with one button per answer (tapping outside the window = Cancel). They come from the hunting-spot choice on the Parties tab:

  • <dungeon> is closed now (Seven Signs) - Save anyway (blocked until it opens) / Cancel.
  • Above the safe level - Yes, override / Save without override / Cancel.
  • Hunt above the safe level? - Yes, override / Cancel.

They are shown with pictures in the Parties chapter.

#Error boxes

Some editors report a failure in a plain browser box with only OK, for example Could not save: <reason>, A route needs at least 2 points, No x y z found, Need at least 2 lines with x y z, Set the start: a gatekeeper teleport ("Dion -> Plains of Dion") or a .townname, Use lowercase letters/digits, e.g. "gatekeeper" (Giran route names) and Pick something to edit first. (shape editor). Read it, press OK and fix what it says; nothing was saved.

#Toasts (the map editors)

The two full-screen map editors show short messages as a toast: a box that appears over the map and disappears by itself.

  1. Spot editor (#/spot/...): hints and results, for example the first steps of a new spot, Start: .giran — now draw the waypoints, <monster>: never fought in this spot, Give the spot a name first, Saved — the leaders use it on their next spot pick (within 5 min, no deploy needed) or Not saved: <reason>. It stays 3.5 seconds (longer for long hints).
  2. Shape editor (#/edit/...): normal toasts (geodata check results, ✓ Saved (...), ✓ Reset to the generated shape., recompute progress) and red error toasts (Not saved: ..., Fix the outline first ..., No monsters inside., or an error loading the shape as in the picture). A normal toast stays 4-15 seconds depending on its length; an error toast 15 seconds.

#Notes

  • The dashboard never shows or changes passwords, and it never sends anything to the game by itself: every order comes from a button you pressed and confirmed. (The bots act on their own, of course; the dashboard only watches them.)
  • "Sent" is not "done". Check the character's notes or the timeline after an order.
  • Keep the key out of screenshots and chats.

#Command center

The command center is the one place where you can give any order to any character, party, several of them, all parties or the clan. It is a search window: type a few letters, pick what you mean, fill in a short form, check exactly what will be sent, confirm. It knows all 121 commands of the system (the full list with every detail is the command reference).

Nothing is sent before you confirm, and the server checks every order again before it reaches the game.

#Opening it

  • Tap Search or give an order... at the top of any page.
  • On a PC: press Ctrl K (press it again to close), or / when no text field has the focus.
  • Tap Commands on a party card (Parties tab), or All commands for <name>... on a character page: the command center opens on that party's or character's command sheet.

On a phone it slides up from the bottom and fills most of the screen; on a desktop it opens as a window near the top. Close it with ✕, Esc, the phone's or browser's back button, or by tapping the dark area outside it. ‹ goes one step back (form -> sheet or search -> closed).

#Search

  1. Search field - type here. The list below changes with every letter.
  2. Section heading - results are grouped (see below).
  3. Recent order - the last orders you sent from this browser, with their target and how long ago. Tap one (↻) to open the same form again with the same details and targets already filled in; you still confirm before it is sent.
  4. ✕ - close.
  5. Hints - ↑↓ choose · Enter open · Esc close · ! swarm · / L2Swarm.

With an empty field you see, in this order:

Section What is in it
Recent Up to 6 of your last orders (the browser keeps 12). Stored only in this browser.
Common orders Level, Supply run, STOP everything, Town teleport, Status report, Raid a boss, Kamaloka, Retreat, Rebuff, Class change.
Parties Every party: size, level range, how many are online. Opens the party's command sheet.
Pages Every tab, plus "Live raid view" and "Hunting-spot map editor". Opens the page (↗).

#Typing

  1. Best hit - highlighted; Enter opens it. Move with ↑ ↓.
  2. Sections - the section with the best hit comes first.

The search is forgiving: letters only have to appear in order ("tlpt" finds "Town teleport"), and several words must each match something ("tele giran" finds Town teleport, because Giran is one of its keywords). It searches command titles, templates, keywords, category names and descriptions, character names, classes, roles, party names and page names. Legacy commands are pushed down.

You type You get
Part of a character name, class or role Characters: name, level, class, party, offline mark, what it is doing. Opens its command sheet (›).
Part of a party (leader) name Parties: opens the party's command sheet (›).
Part of a command Commands: title and the template that will be sent. Chips: L2Swarm (an L2Swarm chat-box command), dashboard (an action the dashboard does itself), safe, destructive.
A page name Pages: opens it (↗).
Text that starts with !, / or @ Send as typed: sends your text exactly as written. You pick the target in the form.
Any other text longer than 2 letters Tell them "..." (last row): free text that the server turns into a command, such as "restock" -> !supply.

The PC commands (Start / Restart / Stop L2Swarm, Deploy swarm.js) are only found through the search, because they have no character target:

When nothing matches, the window says Nothing found for "...". Commands start with ! (swarm) or / (L2Swarm).

#Command sheets

A command sheet lists every command that fits one party or one character, sorted into categories.

  1. Who - for a party: its size, how many are online, who is busy, and a row of class icons. For a character: level, class, party, offline mark and what it is doing now.
  2. Open / Open page - closes the command center and opens the Parties tab or the character page.
  3. Filter commands... - narrows the list.
  4. Category - tap to fold or unfold. The dashboard remembers which categories you keep open (at first: Move, Fight, Party, Supply, Leveling, Raids).
  5. Command tile - title and template (… marks an optional part). The title colour shows its safety (green = safe, normal = confirm, red = destructive); hold the mouse over it on a PC to read the description. Tap it to open the form.

Which commands appear:

  • On a party sheet: every command that can target a party.
  • On a character sheet: every command that can target one or several characters.
  • Clan leader commands (clan level, clan quests, siege registration, clan warehouse ...) only appear on the clan leader's own sheet and on his party's sheet.
  • PC commands never appear on a sheet (search only).

  1. The character. 2. Open page. 3. A destructive tile is drawn in red.

#The command form

  1. Command - icon, title, category; "L2Swarm chat-box command" for / commands; a safe or destructive chip. Below it the description: what the command does.
  2. Details - the arguments (only when the command has some). Required ones must be filled in; optional ones are marked optional.
  3. Who - the target picker (see Targets).
  4. What will be sent - the preview (see Preview).
  5. Send - grey until a target is picked and every required argument is filled in. Back returns to where you came from.

Every kind of argument has its own control:

Lists that come from the server (bosses, Kamalokas, dungeons, gatekeepers, sieges) show "loading…" for a moment the first time; they are kept for 5 minutes.

  1. Fill in: <field> - a required argument is empty. 2. Send stays grey.

#Targets

  1. All parties - every party (with the number of characters).
  2. Clan <name> - every clan member we play.
  3. Party <name> - a party (with its size). Picked chips are drawn pressed.
  4. ▸ Characters - opens the list of single characters, grouped by party (with "(n picked)").
  5. A character - with class icon and level; offline characters are dimmed.

Only the kinds of target that make sense for the command are offered (for example /trade only offers one character). The rules:

  • You can pick several parties and characters at once. All parties and Clan stand alone: picking one of them drops the rest.
  • Commands made for exactly one party or one character take only one.
  • A command that does not allow "several characters" lets you pick only one character (picking another replaces it).
  • Clan leader commands have a fixed target: the clan leader (shown as a fixed chip, "Only the clan leader's window acts on this command").
  • PC commands have no target: "Runs on this PC (no character target)".
  • Client mode needs exactly one character.
  • The form starts with a sensible target: the party or character whose sheet you came from; for a character-only command opened from a party sheet, that party's leader; otherwise the target you used last (remembered in this browser), or the main party.

  1. Pick who gets it. - no target yet; Send stays grey.

#Preview (dry run)

While you fill in the form, the dashboard asks the server what it would send (a dry run: nothing reaches the game). The preview shows one line per send:

  1. The exact text, for example #!level. Swarm commands get a # in front: that makes the line party chat.
  2. How and from whom: party chat from <leader> (a party target: the whole party hears it once), party chat from <name> with "only <name>'s own window obeys" (a single character), normal chat from (no party) (a character without a party), L2Swarm command on <name> (a / command, one line per character), logout on / login on (account actions). A red offline marks characters that will not get it.
  3. Summary - number of sends, how many characters are affected, how many are offline, who is busy, checked by the server when the dry run answered (otherwise the page's own estimate), and who acts: "Only the party leader acts; the others follow him.", "Every character that hears it acts." or "Each character that hears it acts for itself."

  1. A / command to a party: one line per member.

If the server refuses the order (unknown command, wrong file for /config load ...), a red line Server: <reason> appears above the preview. Dashboard actions (client mode, PC) show only their label, for example client mode: in-game → Edwyn.

#Confirm and send

Press Send. A question names exactly what happens:

Send to the WHOLE party Aldric (9 characters):

   Level (Giran -> hunting spot)   (!level)

Busy right now and will change orders: ...
Offline (will not get it): ...

Continue?

The target part reads the WHOLE party <name> (n characters), <name> only, ALL parties (n characters) or the clan (n characters); several targets are joined with + and the total is added:

#Destructive commands

  1. The destructive chip. 2. The button reads Send… (confirm twice).

After the normal question, a second one asks you to type YES:

DESTRUCTIVE: <command>, the description, and Type YES to send it to n characters. Anything other than YES (capital letters) means it is not sent, and the form says so. A command you typed by hand gets the same second question when the server marks it destructive.

#PC and client-mode actions

These do not go through chat:

  • Start / Restart / Stop L2Swarm, Deploy swarm.js: first <title>? <description> Continue?, and for the destructive ones (restart, stop, deploy) a second <title> is destructive. Type YES to do it now. They run the same task as the buttons on the PC tab.
  • In-game / Out of game: the same question as on the character page (Switch <name> to IN-GAME? ...). You must pick exactly one character, otherwise the form says "pick exactly one character".

#Result

After sending, the result appears at the bottom of the form, and the same text goes to the message line:

  • ✓ green: <command> → <target>: n/m sent. When everything went out the window closes by itself after about 1.5 seconds.
  • ⚠ yellow: some sends failed; one line per failed character with the reason. The window stays open.
  • ✗ red: nothing was sent, with the reason (for example "not sent (no YES)", "nobody to send it to", or the server's refusal).

"Sent" means the line reached that character's game window. Whether it could carry it out shows a few seconds later in its notes (Parties tab, character page, "What they do").

A sent order is added to Recent (free-text sentences and PC / client-mode actions are not), and a single target is remembered as the next default.

#Free text

A free-text order ("Tell them ...", listed under Debug / Reports) is translated by the server only when you press Send, so the form cannot show the real command in advance:

  1. The preview shows a red line Server: a command starts with ! (swarm), / (L2Swarm) or @ (account) and, below it, your sentence as typed. For free text you can ignore that red line (the description's "The preview shows what it became" is not true here: the result does).
  2. The result shows the command the server made of it (here !supply), and so does the message line. If the server does not understand the sentence, the result says don't understand "..." with a list of phrases it knows (see the command reference).

#How an order travels

You do not need this to use the command center, but it explains the preview:

  • ! swarm commands go as party chat (#!command) through L2Swarm's control interface (MCP): once per party, from the party leader's window; for a single character from that character's window. A character without a party gets it as normal chat. Our script in every window of the party reads the line and acts according to the command's rule (leader / each / self / clan leader).
  • / L2Swarm commands are typed into each chosen character's L2Swarm chat box, one by one.
  • @login / @logout open or close the account in L2Swarm.
  • File channel: when L2Swarm's control interface does not answer at all, swarm commands (and the simple / commands the script can do itself) are written to Logs\cmd\inbox.json instead. Every window reads that file once a second and confirms what it did. The result then says sent via file channel - <why>. Commands that need L2Swarm itself (/config, /sellitem, /partyinfo, @login, @logout ...) fail with "needs MCP". An order that timed out after the interface had answered is not sent again (it may still run), so do not resend it at once.
  • Every sent order is written to Logs\dashboard_commands.log (time, command, target, how many went out, errors).

#What the server checks

The server checks every order again, whatever the page did:

  • the command word must be in the catalog (! words the script knows, / words L2Swarm knows), one line, at most 300 characters;
  • a command that names a password is refused; passwords are never read or set;
  • /config set <key> <value>, /config save (never with a file name: saving to another file would re-point the account) and /config load <file.xml> (the file must exist in Settings and belong to that character);
  • the targets must exist (party:<leader>, char:<name>, chars:<a>,<b>, all, clan);
  • a destructive command is refused (HTTP 409, "confirm it explicitly in the command center") unless the page sent the typed confirmation.

For scripts and tools: POST /api/command { cmd | text, targets: [...], confirmDanger, dryRun } sends (or, with dryRun: true, only plans) an order; GET /api/commands returns the catalog, the parties and the clan. The page itself loads the catalog from /commands.js.

#Notes

  • The command list lives in one file, Dashboard/commands.js. A new command must exist in the script (or in L2Swarm) before it is added there; then it appears in the search, on the sheets, in the server checks and, after node docs/guide/tools/build_commands.js, in the command reference.
  • If the dashboard server is older than the page (it does not answer /api/commands), the command center still sends ! commands one target at a time; / and @ commands then fail with "the dashboard server runs the old code: restart Dashboard/server.js ...".
  • Recent orders, open categories and the last target are kept in this browser only.

#Parties

The Parties tab (#/parties) is the page you use most. It shows every party as one card: who is in it, what each character does right now, where the party hunts, a small live map, and the buttons that give the whole party an order. It opens when you open the dashboard. Words like leader, spot, claim, SoE and Seven Signs are explained in the glossary.

The page refreshes by itself every 4 seconds (every 1.5 seconds while somebody escapes from a fight or casts something long, see Party live states). Nothing on it changes the game until you press a button and answer OK in the question that follows.

#Parties tab (#/parties)

  1. Tabs - the dashboard's pages. Parties is the first one (see Dashboard basics).
  2. Party header - the party's name (= its leader's name), how many of its characters report right now out of all, and the lowest and highest level in the party. After it, in green, lowest 51→52 in 9h14 (Pell last): when the party's LOWEST level goes up — the slowest of the online members at the lowest level decides, because hunting spots are picked by the lowest level. It reads lowest lvl 60: no estimate for Late when one of them gets no exp. The live party view shows the same in its summary line.
  3. Party buttons and task menu - orders for the whole party (Party buttons).
  4. Tactics - hunting pairs on/off and their settings (Tactics box).
  5. Hunting spot - where the party hunts, your own choice and its live status, Choose… (Hunting spot line).
  6. Party map - the leader's surroundings: members, monsters, the hunting room or square (Party map).
  7. Member rows - one row per character (Member rows). Tap a row to open that character's page.

What else can appear on the tab:

  • Above the party cards: the raid hunter line (Raidhunt not running. Last: …, with a Raidhunt button), and while a raid or a Kamaloka runs, its live view. These belong to the raid and Kamaloka pages: see Raid bosses, Raid live view and Kamaloka live view.
  • Under the header: the status banner, party alerts (Alerts) and, only for a class-quest escort, a line Class-quest escort (one at a time, the whole party helps): A → ▶ B → C with the character being helped now in gold.
  • No party at all: No characters are reporting yet. Is L2Swarm running with swarm.js loaded? - start L2Swarm (see PC) and check that swarm.js is loaded on the accounts.

The order of the cards follows the character names. A character belongs to the party of its leader as set in swarm.config.json (see Getting started). A solo character (here Quill) gets its own card.

On a desktop the map and the member list stand side by side; on a phone the map comes first and the members below it.

The whole page at desktop size, for reference:

#Party buttons

  1. Party name · online · levels - 9/9 online means all nine characters reported within the last 30 seconds.
  2. ● Live (green) - opens the party's live map page (#/live/<leader>): what every member does right now (aggro, casts, fights, stuck, routes, selling). That page has its own chapter: Live party map.
  3. Commands - opens the command center sheet for this party: every command, sorted by category, with a dry run before it is sent (see Command center).
  4. Status - !status: every member writes HP, MP and what it does into party chat (you see it in the What they do timeline and on the character pages).
  5. Level - !level: the leader takes everyone to Giran, regroups, picks a hunting spot for the party's lowest level (or your chosen spot, see below) and teleports the team there.
  6. Supply - !supply: in Giran every member reports what it lacks (Scrolls of Escape, Scrolls of Resurrection, shots, Spirit Ore, potions), the leader buys it all at the grocer and hands it out by trade.
  7. Collect - !collect: members keep 2M adena below level 40, 2.5M at 40-75 and 3M from 76, and trade the rest to the leader.
  8. Class - !classchange: everyone whose level allows it changes class through the Community Board (Alt+B → Career → Professions).
  9. Buff - !buff: rebuff from the Community Board.
  10. Stop - !stop: everyone stops what it does and stays stopped until the next order (Level, Supply, a mission …).
  11. Task menu - every other party order (see the table below).
  12. Argument box - for the menu entries that need a name: a boss, a town, a place, a character.
  13. Do - sends the order chosen in the menu (with the text of the argument box).

Every button asks first. The question names the party and how many characters get the order, shows the command, and lists the members that are busy right now and will drop what they are doing:

Press OK to send it, Cancel to do nothing. After sending, the line under the page header says ✓ !level → party Aldric. The character confirms it in its notes. (or the error). The order goes to the party leader's window, and the leader passes it on.

Task menu + Do. Choose an entry, type the argument if the entry needs one, press Do. Example: Town teleport .<town> with giran in the box sends !town giran:

If an entry needs an argument and the box is empty, nothing is sent and the page says type the boss / town / place in the box next to the menu first.

Menu entry Command sent What the party does
Level (regroup in Giran → leader teleports the team to a spot) !level Same as the Level button.
Supplies: leader buys SoE/SoR/shots/spirit ore in Giran + hands out !supply Same as Supply.
Collect adena to the leader !collect Same as Collect.
Better gear now !gearup Party to Giran, everyone buys and puts on upgrades (see Gear).
Better gear for one character… !gearup <name> Party to Giran, only that character buys.
Gear plan (dry run) !gearplan Writes what each would buy to Logs/gear_plan_<name>.json, buys nothing.
Dungeon: level inside… !dungeon <name> Level inside a dungeon (e.g. Branded, Sacrifice, Worship).
Dungeon off !dungeon off Back to the normal hunting spots.
Soul crystals: fetch / store / status !soul get / !soul store / !soul See Crystals.
Seven Signs: sign up with the Lords of Dawn (Giran) !dawn Every member signs up with Dawn.
Class change now !classchange Same as Class.
Cabinet setting… !cabinet <setting> on/off Switches a Community Board Cabinet setting, e.g. Forward Drop on.
Status / Rebuff !status / !buff Same as the buttons.
Sell marked items + junk now !sell Sells at the shop (list on the Gear page).
Raid hunter / Stop raid hunter !raidhunt / !raidhunt stop Hunts raid bosses in the party's level range (see Raid bosses).
Raid mission… !mission raid <boss> One raid boss.
Joint raid… !jointraid <boss> with <leader>,<leader> Several parties on one boss (order the main party).
Learn the clan focus skill now !clanskill Clan leader only (see Clan).

Siege… / Stop the siege !siege fort <name> / !siege castle <name> / !siege stop See Sieges.
Stop mission !mission stop Ends a raid or Kamaloka mission.
Help character… / Stop helping !assist <name> / !assist off The whole party assists that character / follows the leader again.
Town teleport .<town> !town <town> gludin, gludio, dion, giran, oren, aden, hunters, heine, goddard, rune, schuttgart.

Walk to… !goto <NPC / place / x y> Walks there.
Stop leveling !autolevel stop Ends leveling.
Escape (SoE) !soe Everyone leaves the fight and goes to a town (.townname).
Stop everything !stop Same as Stop.

Every command is described in the command reference.

Phone tip. On a narrow phone the button row is wider than the screen: the last buttons, the argument box and Do are cut off at the right edge (picture below: 1 header, 2 Live, 3 Commands, 4 the task menu). Use Commands (it has every order) or turn the phone sideways.

#Status banner

Right under the header a banner says in one sentence what the whole party does now (supply run, regroup, fund round, trip, hunting, raid, waiting for orders), with a step bar, how long the step has taken, what comes next, the trades in progress and who the leader waits for. It turns yellow when a step takes unusually long. Everything about it (every sentence, the steps of each run, the warnings, the trade lines on the map): Party status.

#Alerts

Under the header the card lists what needs your attention, worst first. At most three lines show; the rest hide behind n more (tap to open).

  1. Red line - a character is dead, or has not reported for a while (not reporting for 8m (offline or script stopped)).
  2. Gold line - a step failed in the last 10 minutes (Walk 640 to … — failed: stood still 40 s), or one of its last notes says it gave up / failed / could not. Normal path retries are not shown.
  3. n more - the hidden lines.

A line No Scroll of Escape: … sums up every live member with no SoE left (a supply run buys them).

#Member rows

The leader is always first, the others follow in name order.

  1. Leader - the gold star after the name.
  2. Dead - dark red row.
  3. Problem - a red bar on the left edge: this character has an alert (see above).
  4. Resting - the task reads resting … with the sitting icon; on the map the dot turns light blue.
  5. Offline - a faded row with offline 8m after the class: no report for more than 30 seconds.
  6. Low supplies - red chips before the adena: SoE n (fewer than 2 Scrolls of Escape), shots n (100 or fewer).
  7. Low buffs - buffs n (fewer than 10 buffs).

A name in light red means the character fights right now. Tap anywhere on a row to open its character page.

#One row, part by part

  1. Class icon - the game's class icon (a role icon when the class is not known yet).

  2. Level.

  3. Name - with a gold star for the party leader.

  4. Class - the current class name.

  5. Seven Signs mark - see below.

  6. Experience - how far into the current level, in %. For about 6 seconds after a change a small pop-up appears left of it: green +1,234 exp (+0.01%) for a gain (+3 kills: … when several kills came together, LEVEL UP! on a new level), red −5,000 exp (−0.20%) died for a loss. Hover it on a desktop for the monsters and times.

    In the picture: 1 a gain from two kills, 2 a level up, 3 a loss on death.

    After the % comes the next level estimate in short: lvl in 1h25 (green), lvl in 6d for more than 48 hours, no exp 22m when the character got nothing for a while, no exp when it gets nothing at all. Hover or long-press it for the rate and the clock time; it is calculated as on the character page. The same short text is on the cards of the live party view and next to the level on the Accounts page.

  7. HP and MP bars - red and blue; the HP bar turns warning-coloured below 30 %.

  8. Task - what the character does now in plain words, with an icon: Trading with Tankard: receiving 2.0M adena (window open, waiting for the items), waiting for its turn at Helvetia (grocer) — 3rd in line, fighting Liangma (63% HP, 120 away), … plus a stuck / no progress chip when it does not get on. Every line is explained in Party status.

  9. Adena - short form (35M, 2.6M, 840k), after any low-supply chips.

Under a row a cast bar or an escape box can appear while the character casts something long or escapes from a fight (Party live states).

#Member rows during a team task

During a supply run, a collect or a fund round the activity line says who trades with whom (with four stage dots: ask → window open → confirm → done), who waits while others trade, who is ready, whose turn it is, and red chips mark a member that is stuck, not moving, a trade with no progress or a team step that takes long. Pictures and every text: Party status → Member rows.

#Seven Signs mark

  1. ☀ Dawn (gold) - signed up with the Lords of Dawn this cycle.
  2. ☾ Dusk (purple) - signed up with Dusk.
  3. 7S – (grey) - not signed up this cycle (or never checked).

Hover a mark on a desktop to see when it was checked. Catacombs and necropolises need every member signed up (always Dawn here), so a party full of grey marks cannot hunt there - see the Seven Signs check in the picker. The data comes from Logs/sevensigns_<name>.json, written by the bots when they read the Priest of Dawn; the order Seven Signs: sign up (!dawn) in the task menu signs everyone up.

#Tactics box (hunting pairs)

Normally the whole party attacks the leader's monster (focus fire). With hunting pairs the leader splits the damage dealers into small groups and gives each group its own monster near him, so more monsters die at once. It is used only while leveling - never in raids, Kamaloka, missions or during teleports.

The closed box is one line:

  1. Tactics: On - groups are live: green pairs ON chip and the reason (on: 6 damage dealers).
  2. Tactics: Auto - the leader turns groups on only when the party is strong; here they are off right now and the reason says why (auto: team HP average 62 % (needs 70 % for a minute)).
  3. Tactics: Off - focus fire (everyone on the leader's monster).

After the state: how many damage dealers the party has and, when not off, → up to N groups of 2. waiting for the leader's report means the leader has not reported a tactics state yet (offline, or an older script).

Tap the line to open the box:

  1. Summary - tap again to close.
  2. Live groups - one chip per group: Corwin + Delphine → Giggling Wind 48%; looking = no monster yet; a gold chip (helping X) = that group helps another group whose monster is strong.
  3. Mode - Off — focus fire, Auto — only when strong, On — always pairs.
  4. Group size - 1 (each dealer alone), 2 (pairs, default) or 3 (trios).
  5. Max groups - 1 to 6 (default 3). Dealers left over keep helping the leader.
  6. Leash from leader - 600 to 1300 (default 900): how far from the leader a group's monster may be.
  7. Zone size - ×1.0 to ×2.0: makes the hunting zone bigger while groups are on.
  8. Auto: min dealers - Auto mode needs at least this many damage dealers (default 4).
  9. Auto: monster lvl ≤ team min + - Auto mode only when the monsters are at most this many levels above the party's lowest level (default 2).
  10. Back to focus fire below HP % - default 40.
  11. Doomcryer joins a group - normally the doomcryer stays a buffer; tick to count it as a dealer.
  12. Save tactics for party … - saves (asks first, see below). saved hh:mm appears next to it.

Who counts as a damage dealer: destroyers, doombringers, inspectors (Soul Breaker / Hound), necromancers, nukers, daggers, mages, archers. Healers keep healing everyone in any mode.

The rules the bots follow (also written under the settings): every group's monster stays within the leash of the leader and within 1400 of every teammate (the server shares experience only within 1600). The party goes back to focus fire at once when someone drops below the HP limit, someone dies, or more than 6 monsters attack the team - then it waits 2 minutes. Auto also needs enough dealers, monsters not above the team (see the level margin), a team HP average of at least 70 % for a minute, and no death for 10 minutes.

Saving asks first:

The settings are saved in Scripts/data/party_tactics.json (one entry per party leader; _defaults holds the defaults). The bots read the file within a minute - no restart or deploy. A few expert fields (maxAdds, expRange, hpAvgMin, noDeathMin, cooldownMin, helpHp) exist only in the file; the dashboard keeps them when it saves. Switches are written to party chat, the leader's notes and Logs/tactics.log.

The live view of the groups is explained again in Party live states → Hunting pairs.

#Hunting spot line

The leader normally picks the hunting spot himself (Auto): the best place for the party's lowest level from the team's list of zones, then the datapack spots. On this line you can choose the spot yourself - a dungeon room, several rooms, field areas, one of your zones or a datapack spot. Your choice wins over the automatic pick until you press Back to auto.

  1. Current choice - Auto, or (gold) what you chose: Cruma Tower · cruma-2-left-c, Cruma Tower · any free room, Cruma Tower · 4 rooms (in your order), Windy Hill · 2 areas (nearest first), Windy Hill · area 3, a zone name, or a datapack spot (datapack). Added flags: · stay (stay even if occupied) and · level override (you allowed a spot above the safe level).
  2. Live status - what the leader does with your choice right now (all states below).
  3. now: … - where the leader hunts at this moment (his hunting zone, or the spot he claimed).
  4. Choose… - opens the hunting-spot picker.
  5. Back to auto - only shown while a choice of yours is active. Asks first, then the leader picks again by himself.

Further chips on the line: the rotation chip while the party moves between several rooms or areas, and for a chosen catacomb or necropolis a red or gold Seven Signs chip when the party cannot enter now.

#Live status of your choice (every state)

The leader reports the state of your choice every few seconds. Two pictures show all states (on these two pictures the maps and member rows are hidden so the spot lines of several parties fit on one screen).

  1. chosen 06:54 · travelling · ETA 1:20 - the leader is on his way. An ETA is shown when he walks on the same dungeon floor; teleport trips have none.
  2. · stay - this choice stays even when other players hunt there.
  3. Rotation chip - rotating 2 areas (nearest first): now 1 · 9 here - see Rotation.
  4. occupied by others → auto · retry in 4:10 (red) - other players hunt there. The party hunts its automatic spot meanwhile and tries your spot again within 5 minutes. Tick stay even if occupied in the picker to stay anyway.
  5. closed (Seven Signs) → auto · until Mon 12 Oct 20:00 (red) - a catacomb or necropolis the party may not enter in this Seven Signs period. No trip is made; the party hunts its automatic spot and goes there by itself when the period changes. The red chip after it explains why (closed: Seven Signs validation — only Dusk winners …).
  6. · level override - you allowed this choice although it is above the safe level.
  7. waiting: after the fight (Pellinor 34 %) - the leader has seen your choice but waits: after the fight, the supply run first, in a raid, in Kamaloka, on a mission, escaping, rescuing a teammate, dead, or a !dungeon / !assist order holds the spot.
  8. needs your OK: too high level → auto (gold) + Override… - the place is more than 6 levels above the party's highest level (monsters or the teleport landing). The party hunts its automatic spot until you press Override… and answer Yes, override.

  1. chosen … · not reachable now → auto · retry in 3:11 (red) - the trip failed (here: could not get to Cruma Tower 2nd floor via Ponti; hover for the full reason). The party hunts its automatic spot and tries again within 5 minutes.
  2. back to auto · back to the automatic choice - you pressed Back to auto; the leader is switching.
  3. chosen 06:41 · waiting for the leader - your choice is saved but the leader has not reported anything about it for 30 seconds (offline, busy logging in, or an older script).
  4. chosen 11:30 · travelling (no ETA) - travelling by teleport (.town, gatekeeper, floor teleporter); hover for normal travel ….
  5. not reachable now → auto on a solo character: same as 1.

Other texts you may see in the chip: in the room ✓ / in the area ✓ / there ✓ (green: arrived), seen by the leader, leaving the current spot.

#Rotation between rooms or areas

When you choose several rooms (or field areas), the party hunts the first one and moves on to the next when it is empty. The chip reads rotating 4 rooms (in order): now 1 · 6 here:

  • in order / nearest first - which one comes next: your order, or the nearest.
  • automatic - the rotation was set up by the leader, not by you.
  • now N · M here - the number of the current room or area and how many monsters the leader sees in it.
  • · moving on: … - the leader decided to move on and why (e.g. no monster for 35 s).

Hover the chip on a desktop for the full list: every room with its number, (now), why it is blocked (claimed by party Borin), how many monsters are expected and how many were killed. The party map shows the same list, numbered.

#Hunting-spot picker (Choose…)

Choose… opens a full-screen window for that party. It lists every place that fits the party's levels; dungeons and outdoor hunting grounds open a map where you tap rooms or areas.

#The list

  1. Title - Hunting spot · party Aldric (lvl 49–50).
  2. Auto (the leader picks) - go back to the automatic choice (asks first).
  3. Close - closes without saving (tapping the dark background does the same).
  4. search… - filters the list by name as you type.
  5. all levels - shows every place, not only those that fit. Normally a place shows when its level range is within 3 levels of the party's levels.
  6. stay even if occupied - the party stays even when other players hunt there (otherwise it hunts elsewhere and tries again within 5 minutes).
  7. move on when outgrown - when the party's lowest level is more than 3 above the monsters there, the leader goes back to Auto and finds a better place.
  8. now: … - the current choice.
  9. Groups of places, each row with its level range on the left:
    • Dungeons — pick rooms on the map - N rooms · tap for the map; catacombs and necropolises also show their Seven Signs chip.
    • Hunting grounds (outdoor) — pick areas on the map - N areas (M far) · landing · tap for the map.
    • Our hunting zones - the zones from the Zones page (kind, dungeon, which teams); a zone made of dungeon rooms opens the room map, any other zone is saved at once (asks first).
    • Datapack spots (teleport + walk) - spots from the game's data: gatekeeper link and number of monsters (at most 150 rows). Saved at once (asks first).
  10. Who holds a place - party Borin chip = one of your parties hunts there now; red occupied by 3 players (4 min) = other players were seen there (the minutes = how long the bots keep away).

The note at the bottom repeats the rules: your choice wins over the automatic pick; a place that is not your level is visited anyway (with a warning in party chat); other players there make the party hunt elsewhere for now unless stay is ticked. No deploy is needed: the leader reads the choice within about 15 seconds.

With all levels ticked and a search word, e.g. catacomb:

  1. Search word.
  2. all levels ticked.
  3. Seven Signs chip of each catacomb / necropolis for this party (see Seven Signs check).

#Dungeon room map

Tap a dungeon (or a zone that is made of dungeon rooms) to open its room map:

  1. ← List - back to the list (the selection is dropped).
  2. Any free room - the leader takes whichever fitting room is free (saved at once, asks first).
  3. Close.
  4. Floor buttons - one per floor with its level range; the floor that fits the party best opens first.
  5. stay even if occupied / move on when outgrown - as in the list.
  6. Selection bar:
    • Select all fitting (this floor) - adds every room of this floor that fits the party, can be walked to and is not taken by another party or by other players.
    • Clear - empties the selection.
    • Next: nearest first / in my order - tap to switch: after the current room, go to the nearest chosen room, or follow your order.
    • Hunt in N rooms (or Hunt in this room) - saves the choice (asks first). Greyed out while nothing is chosen.
    • Numbered chips - the chosen rooms in order; a room on another floor shows its floor (F1 left-a).
  7. Map - every room's outline on the game map. Colours: green fits the party, gold close (±3 levels), grey other levels, red other players hunt there (occupied: …), party colour one of your parties hunts there (party Borin). Tap a room to choose it (a white numbered circle, in the order you tap); tap again to remove it. You can choose rooms on several floors. Green shields are safe spots. Coloured dots with names are characters on this floor. On a phone, drag inside the map to see all of it.
  8. Room info - the last room you tapped: name, monster levels, which party levels it suits, outline quality, the monsters, who holds it, no walk route from the floor entry (red) if the bots cannot walk there, and the button Hunt only in this room (saves just this room at once, asks first).

Several rooms: the party hunts the first one, and moves on to the next when a room is empty (also across floors, through the floor teleporters).

Saving asks first:

Party Aldric (9 characters): hunting spot = Cruma Tower · 2 rooms (…; next: in your order)? The leader stops what he hunts now and goes there (normal travel: .town + gatekeeper / floor teleporter / Ziggurat). OK saves it, and the picker closes.

#Seven Signs check

Catacombs and necropolises are entered only through the Gatekeeper Ziggurat, and only when every member is signed up with the Seven Signs (here always Dawn) and the Seven Signs period allows it. The room map of a catacomb shows a banner with the party's state:

  1. Seven Signs chip - one of:
    • green Seven Signs: can enter,
    • gold needs sign-up (Dawn) first — competition period (the leader takes the party to the Priest of Dawn first),
    • grey Seven Signs period not read yet (the leader asks the Priest of Dawn first),
    • red closed: … with the reason and until when (e.g. closed: Seven Signs validation — only Dusk winners until Mon 12 Oct 20:00 (local)). In the validation period nobody can sign up; only those signed up in the last competition (on the winning side) may enter.
  2. Way in - the reminder that only the Gatekeeper Ziggurat leads in and every member must be signed up.

Choosing a room of a closed catacomb opens this question instead of the normal one:

Save anyway (blocked until it opens) saves the choice; the party hunts its automatic spot and goes there by itself once the period changes (the spot line shows closed (Seven Signs) → auto). Cancel saves nothing. A party that may enter shows the green chip:

#Level check (above the safe level)

A choice whose monsters are more than 6 levels above the party's highest level asks first:

  • Yes, override - saved with your override: the party skips the level and landing-danger checks for this choice. Survival, escape and rescue stay on, and the Seven Signs rule is never skipped.
  • Save without override - saved, but the party waits for your OK (spot line: needs your OK) and hunts its automatic spot meanwhile.
  • Cancel - nothing is saved.

The bots can also find a danger only on the way (a teleport landing next to high monsters). Then the spot line shows needs your OK with an Override… button, which asks the same question:

#Field region map (outdoor hunting grounds)

Tap a hunting ground under Hunting grounds (outdoor) to open its region map, split into areas:

  1. ← List / Close and the stay / move on when outgrown boxes, as in the dungeon map.
  2. Colour key - green fits, gold close (±3), grey too low, red too high (or monsters above the safe limit), bright red other players, party colour one of your parties, ⛊ safe spot, ◆ teleport landing, dashed outline far from any landing (not picked automatically).
  3. Selection bar - Select all fitting (green) adds every green area that can be reached and is free (nearest to its landing first); Clear; Next: nearest first / in my order; Hunt in N areas; numbered chips area 1 (27-29).
  4. Map - each area with number · levels (far when no landing is near). Tap areas to choose them (numbered). The last tapped area also shows its way in from the landing as a light-blue dashed line. Blue diamonds are landings with their names (.giran Giran … for a town command).
  5. Area info - name, monster levels (and up to when single stronger ones live there), which party levels it suits, number of monsters, how many are aggressive, respawn time, the monster list, the way in (way in: … + 1.2k walk), the neighbour areas with walking distance, and a red warning when a raid boss is near.

The party hunts the first area and moves on to the next when an area had no monster for about 35 seconds, when other players hunt there, or when another of your parties takes it.

#Zones and datapack spots

A zone without rooms and a datapack spot have no map: tapping the row asks Party X (n characters): hunting spot = <name>? and saves it.

#What is saved

Every choice is saved in Scripts/data/party_spots.json, one entry per party leader (an old copy goes to Settings/backup/ first):

Field Meaning
mode auto or manual
kind rooms (dungeon), field (outdoor areas), zone (one of your zones), datapack
dungeon, roomId, roomIds the dungeon, the first room (any = any free room), all chosen rooms in order
region, areaIds the outdoor region and the chosen areas in order
order nearest or rotate (= in your order)
stay, moveOn the two tick boxes
override, overrideNote your "Yes, override" for a place above the safe level
at, by when, and dashboard

The leader reads the file within about 15 seconds; no deploy and no restart. When a choice changes while the party is on its way to the old spot, the trip stops and the new choice is taken.

#Party map

The square map shows the area around the party leader, on the game's own map art (the right underground layer inside dungeons). It grows to fit the members, the hunting room or square, and a chosen room. On a desktop it stands left of the member list.

  1. Hunting room - gold dashed outline with room: <name> and (your choice) when you chose it, (claimed) when the leader claimed it for this party. An outdoor area reads area: ….
  2. Legend - what the symbols mean (it changes with what is on the map).

What you can see on the map:

Symbol Meaning
Dot in the party colour a member; the leader's dot is bigger. Names next to it (several standing together: Aldric +4).
Red ring around a dot the character is fighting.
Light-blue dot resting.
Grey dot not reporting (offline).
Dark red dot with ✕ dead.
Small red dots monsters the leader sees (only on his floor).
Gold dot with ♛ and name + HP % a raid boss in view.
Gold dashed ring ♛ name (spawn — not seen) the raid boss the party is going for, at its spawn point, not seen yet.
Smaller dots in other colours, Name's party: 3 members of your other parties in view.
Gold dashed outline (polygon) the hunting room or field area.
Gold dashed square hunting: … the hunting square of a normal spot.
local fallback square (the chosen spot was not reached) / local fallback room the leader could not reach the spot and hunts where he is.
White dashed outline chosen: … · travelling the room you chose that the party has not reached yet.
Numbered outlines 2 ~9, 3 ✕ the next rooms / areas of a rotation: number, ~expected monsters, ✕ blocked.
Dashed circle in the party colour the leader's combat range.
far away: Name 25k, … (yellow, top left) members more than 20 000 away from the leader.
left, occupied: … by … (n min) (orange) spots the party left because other players hunted there.
Faint green lines, yellow dots, magenta squares inside a dungeon: the floor's hallway centrelines (the network every route follows), doors, and floor teleporters / landings / entries.
Bright green line with dots, a white ring, a dashed circle → target the leader's route: the planned walk along the centrelines (one dot per waypoint, 150-300 apart), the next waypoint ringed in white, the walk target. The part already walked is faint and dashed.
Thin line in the party colour a member's own route (when it walks by itself, e.g. back to the leader).
Red ring stuck 25 s · re-plan 1 a character that has not moved although it should; how long, and how many times it planned a new way.
Animated yellow line giver → receiver: what a trade in progress (a loop when both stand on the same spot); green ✓ = done, red ✗ = failed. See Party status.
Scale bar (bottom left) length on the map.

The monsters are asked from L2Swarm every 7 seconds while the tab is open. The routes come from each bot's live state (route, refreshed every few seconds, hidden when older than 90 seconds); the centrelines from Scripts/data/dungeon_graph/<dungeon>.json. Routes always follow the centrelines - through hallways and doorways, never a straight line through a wall - so a route that cuts across the map, or a red stuck ring that stays, tells you at a glance that something is off.

#More map pictures

The room you chose, while the party walks there along the hallway centrelines:

  1. Chosen room - white dashed outline with chosen: <room> · travelling.
  2. Leader's route - bright green along the centrelines, waypoint dots, the next waypoint ringed, → Torfe room at the end.
  3. Stuck member - red ring with stuck 25 s · re-plan 1.
  4. Legend - with a route on the map it adds ━ route (centerline), • door and ◯ stuck.

A rotation between rooms (current room gold, the next ones numbered with the expected monsters, a blocked one red with ✕):

An outdoor field area and the next area of the rotation:
