#How to …

Send the whole party leveling

  1. Press Level on the party card.
  2. Read the question (who is busy) and press OK.
  3. Watch the member tasks change to regroup and then autolevel: ….

Make a party hunt in one dungeon room

  1. Press Choose… on the hunting spot line.
  2. Tap the dungeon (e.g. Cruma Tower). The floor that fits the party opens.
  3. Tap a green room. Read the room info (monsters, levels).
  4. Press Hunt only in this room (or Hunt in this room in the selection bar) and OK.
  5. The spot line shows travelling, then in the room ✓. The party map draws the room.

Make a party rotate between several rooms or areas

  1. Choose… → the dungeon or hunting ground.
  2. Tap rooms / areas in the order you want (or Select all fitting).
  3. Press Next: until it says what you want (nearest first or in my order).
  4. Press Hunt in N rooms → OK.

Stop using your own choice

  1. Press Back to auto on the spot line (or Auto (the leader picks) in the picker) → OK.

Turn hunting pairs on

  1. Tap the Tactics line to open it.
  2. Mode Auto (recommended) or On; adjust group size and the rest if needed.
  3. Press Save tactics for party … → OK. Within a minute the summary shows pairs ON (or why not).

Give a special order

  1. Choose the entry in the task menu. 2. Type the argument (boss, town, name) if it needs one. 3. Press Do → OK.

#Notes and safety

  • Every order and every saved setting on this page asks first. Nothing is sent to the game before you press OK.
  • Orders go to the party leader's window, which passes them on in party chat. The What they do tab and the character pages show what each character made of it.
  • Files written by this page: Scripts/data/party_spots.json (hunting spot) and Scripts/data/party_tactics.json (tactics). Both are read live by the bots - no deploy, no restart.
  • Everything else on the page is read from the bots' live state files (Logs/swarm_state_<name>.json, written every few seconds) and from L2Swarm (the monsters on the map).
  • A row is faded when its character has not reported for 30 seconds: check L2Swarm and the PC tab.
  • The live parts of a card (escape box, cast bar, rescue trips, rotation, occupied spots, hunting pairs) are explained with pictures in Party live states.

#Party status on the Parties tab

Every party card on the Parties tab starts with a status banner: one sentence that says what the whole party is doing right now and why, a step bar, how long the current step has taken and what comes next. Every member row says in plain words what that character is doing, and trades are shown with both sides. So when the party seems to "just stand" in Giran, the card tells you that it is in the middle of a supply run, who is trading with whom, and who it is waiting for.

The banner and the rows only show things. They never send an order.

#The status banner

  1. Icon + sentence - what the party does, in words. The names and the place are in gold. Examples:
    • Regrouping in Giran before going to Windy Hill — supply run step 3/9: handing out (2/8 done, now Healix)
    • Supply run in Giran — step 2/10: buying at Helvetia (grocer) — Soulshot (D) x4000, Mana Potion x1500
    • Fund round: Tankard gives adena to characters below their target (1 of 3 done, waiting for Healix to accept)
    • Collecting adena: members hand what is above their keep to Tankard — step 3/3: handing adena over (1/4 done)
    • Travelling to Windy Hill: area 1 — step 4/4: walking to the area — 2400 to the centre
    • Hunting Windy Hill: area 1 · 24 monsters here · rotating 2 areas · 25 kills in 5 min
    • Raid: Serpent Demon Bifrons — clearing the area (4 left, now Turek Orc Warlord)
    • Waiting for orders since 21:26
  2. Time box (top right) - how long the current step has taken. It turns yellow when the step takes unusually long (see Warnings). A ≥ in front (≥ 40 s) means the dashboard only knows how long it has seen this state, not when it started.
  3. Step bar - one segment per step of the run: done steps dark gold, the current step bright gold (it pulses gently), the rest grey. Hover a segment on a desktop for its name.
  4. Step line - step 3/9 · next: enchanting gear · started 3m06s ago: where the run stands, the next step and how long the whole run has been going.
  5. Trade lines - every trade in the party: Trade: Tankard → Healix · 2.0M adena · window open, putting the items in with four dots (asked → window open → confirmed → done). A finished trade stays for about 30 seconds with done ✓ (green) or failed: … (red).
  6. Team step line - while the leader runs a step that everyone must answer: Team step reporting what it needs: 7/9 ready — waiting for Wisp (1.2k away), Dusk (dead).
  7. Waiting line - who the leader waits for before he moves on (gathering the team, a checkpoint, before a teleport).

#The steps of each run

Run Steps
Supply run regrouping in Giran · everyone reports what it needs · buying at Helvetia · handing out · enchanting gear · unloading loot to a teammate · members sell at Helvetia, one after another · gear upgrades in the shops · dyes and symbols · collecting adena above their keep
Giran regroup teleporting to Giran · walking to the Giran start · gathering the team · supply run (when one is due) · handing adena to other teams · Seven Signs sign-up
Trip to a hunting spot regrouping in Giran · gathering the team · teleporting · walking to the area
Collect adena asking who has adena · gathering · handing adena over
Fund round walking to the Giran start · handing out (n of m, who it waits for, who has not come to the start yet)

A supply run that starts inside a Giran regroup (or a regroup inside a trip) shows the inner run with the outer one in front: Regrouping in Giran before going to Windy Hill — supply run step 3/9 ….

#Warnings

When a step takes longer than usual the banner gets a yellow edge, the time box turns yellow and a line under it says why, when the dashboard knows: waiting for Wisp (1.2k away), Dusk (dead) — for 4m20s. Other reasons: a trade that does not move on (trade Tankard → Healix stays at "asking Healix to open the trade (try 3/5)"), members that do not move (not moving: Ashen), or simply taking longer than usual.

Usual times: 3 minutes for most steps; buying 5 minutes; enchanting 6; walking to the area 7; members selling and dyes 10; gear upgrades 15; the fund round 2.5. Hunting and waiting for orders never warn.

#Member rows

The line under the HP/MP bars says what the character does, with an icon, in up to two lines (three for a trade):

Line Meaning
Trading with Tankard: receiving 2.0M adena (window open, waiting for the items) it is in a trade; the other side, what, and where the trade stands. The four dots: asked, window open, confirmed, done.
Traded with Tankard: received Spiritshot (D) x1000 (done ✓) a trade that just ended (about 30 seconds).
waiting while Tankard trades with Healix (Soulshot (D) x1999) it is in the leader's team step, but someone else trades now.
waiting for its turn at Helvetia (grocer) — 3rd in line, ~12 s members sell or shop one after another; it waits for its turn.
ready — waiting for the others (selling at Helvetia) its part of the team step is done.
walking to the Giran start point (1.6k left) it walks a recorded Giran route (grocer, warehouse, weapon shop, …).
stuck for 48 s — re-planning (try 1) on the way to the Giran start its walker reports it is stuck; it tries a new path by itself.
waiting for Wisp (1.2k away), Dusk (dead) the leader is gathering the team.
following Tankard (73 away), fighting Babbling Wind (70% HP, 80 away), resting (HP 40%, MP 22%), dead — waiting for a resurrection the usual states.

Chips at the end of the line:

  • stuck 48 s (red) - its route walker reports it is stuck. not moving 25 s (yellow) - it should be walking but has not moved.
  • no progress 1m10s (yellow) - a trade has been at the same point for more than 45 seconds.
  • step 3m20s (yellow) - its part of a team step has been running for more than 3 minutes.

Hover a row on a desktop to see the raw task text the script reports.

#Trade lines on the party map

Every trade in progress is drawn on the party map as a gold dashed line from the giver to the receiver, with a dot that travels in the direction the items go and a label Tankard → Healix: 2.0M adena. When both stand on the same spot (the Giran start) the line is a loop above them. A finished trade turns green (✓) or red (✗) for about 30 seconds. A trade with a character of another party (fund rounds) is drawn too.

#Older scripts

The step bar, the step times, the items of a trade and the "waiting for its turn" lines need a current swarm.js. With an older script the card still works out what it can from the task texts: Trading in town: Oldie → Moss — 1 member waits for their turn, trading with Oldie (receiving), waiting while Oldie trades with Moss. The time box then shows ≥ (how long the dashboard has seen it).

#Motion

The pulsing current step, the trade dots and the moving trade lines are switched off when the device asks for reduced motion (iPhone: Settings → Accessibility → Motion → Reduce Motion). Everything else stays the same.

#Character page (#/char/<Name>)

The character page shows one character in full, live: what it is doing right now (in plain words, with the cast it is casting, its target and the monsters on it), a live map, its gear, bag, skills with cooldowns, buffs with the time left, its recent steps, its progress and supplies, and direct orders: use this skill now, take a potion, Scroll of Escape now, drop an item. Open it whenever one character behaves oddly, or when you want to check or change its gear, buffs or bag.

It looks and moves like the Live party view, but for one character.

How to open it

  • Tap a member row on the Parties tab, a dot on the Map, "open ›" on a live party card, a name in What they do, Teleports or Accounts, or a teammate button at the top of another character page. On its own map, tap a teammate's dot.
  • Or type the address: #/char/<Name>, for example #/char/Aldric. Back / forward in the browser work; Esc goes back (or closes an open pop-up first).

  1. Header - name, class, chips, CP / HP / MP / EXP bars, money, teammates (below).
  2. Right now - the activity in plain words, the cast, target, aggro and the quick orders.
  3. Where it is - the live map.
  4. Buffs - debuffs and buffs with time bars.
  5. Skills - with cooldown sweeps; tap one to use it now.
  6. Equipment - the paper doll.
  7. Inventory - icon grid with filters; tap an item to use, drop or mark it for selling.
  8. Recent steps - the intent timeline.
  9. Progress, supplies, stats.
  10. Orders - Class change, Rebuff, Retreat, the task menu, client mode.
  11. Priority + quest plan.

#Layout per device

Screen Columns Order
Phone (under 760 px) 1 header, Right now (+ quick orders), map, buffs, skills, equipment, inventory, recent steps, progress, orders, priority
Tablet (760 - 1279 px) 2 left: Right now, map, buffs, recent steps, orders · right: equipment, skills, inventory, progress, priority
Desktop (1280 px and wider) 3, full width left: Right now, map, recent steps · middle: equipment, inventory, progress, priority · right: skills, buffs, orders

The boxes move between the columns when you turn a tablet or resize the window; open menus, scroll positions and typed text stay.

Where the data comes from (see the Glossary for MCP, swarm_state and intent):

Part Source Refresh
Activity, cast, target, aggro, route, exp pop-ups, teammates, monsters around the leader /api/live?party=<party> (the characters' swarm_state files + the leader's monsters, cached 3 s) 1.5 s
Bars with numbers, stats, buffs, inventory, skills + cooldowns, NPCs and monsters around it /api/char (the game through MCP, read only) 5 s
Recent steps /api/intent (Logs/intent_<Name>.log) 10 s
Quest plan /api/questplan (Logs/questplan_<Name>.json) 30 s

Nothing is fetched while the browser tab is hidden; the cast ring, cooldowns and buff bars animate locally between refreshes. With "reduce motion" switched on in the system, the animations are off.

#Header

  1. ◀ Back - the page you came from (or Parties). Same as Esc.
  2. Class icon with the level badge - the game's class mark for the current class.
  3. Name - a ★ after it means party leader.
  4. Class · role · party · login - tap the party name to open the party's live view.
  5. Chips - online / offline, bot on / bot off (L2Swarm's bot switch), in combat (glows), dead, sitting, the zone (town (peace), general zone ...), and last report N min ago (red) when the script has been silent for more than 30 seconds.
  6. Live - the party's live view.
  7. Commands - every command for this character in the command center (screenshot).
  8. Override… - the override panel for this character (below).
  9. CP bar - current / maximum.
  10. HP bar - turns to a warning colour under 30 %.
  11. MP bar.
  12. EXP bar - progress to the next level. After a kill a green +18,420 exp (+0.02 %) pops up inside the bar for about 6 seconds (red when exp was lost, gold on a level-up). The bars slide smoothly when the values change.
  13. Next level line (under the bars) - when the character reaches the next level: lvl 52 in ~1h 25m, the clock time (at ~14:47, with the weekday when it is not today), the rate (7.4 %/h) and what it is based on (last 60 min, 1 death left out). A thin yellow mark on the EXP bar shows where the bar will be in 30 minutes (a green mark at the end = it levels within 30 minutes). Hover or long-press the line for the details. See Next level estimate.
  14. Money line - adena, SP, exp per hour (the same rate as the next level line) and the exact position x, y, z.
  15. Teammates - one button per party member (leader first), with a thin HP line under the name. Tap one to open its page. Dead teammates are dark, silent ones grey.

When the game data cannot be read, the bars show the percentages the script last reported.

#Next level estimate

The estimate uses the exp the character really got lately: the exp points of the last hour (fewer minutes right after a script restart), with deaths left out (a death moves the bar back once, it does not make the hunting slower; the loss is already in the exp %), turned into % of the current level and smoothed so it does not jump on every refresh. A level-up does not spoil it: the points per hour stay, the new level just needs more of them. In the first 5 minutes after a script (re)start it says measuring…; without a gain for 10 minutes it says no exp for 14 min (in town, travelling, waiting); with no gains at all no exp lately. Above 48 hours it is shown in days. Offline characters show nothing.

#Right now

What the character does this second, and the fastest orders.

  1. live / reported N s ago - how fresh the data is (green = live, red = silent).
  2. Activity line - in plain words, the same sentence as on the live party card ("healing Greater Heal → Cassius", "fighting Liangma (72 % HP)", "walking to Gludio (point 3/9, 1.2k left)", "stuck for 40 s — re-planning", "selling at Helvetia" ...). A new activity flashes once.
  3. Cast icon - the skill (or scroll) being cast, with a progress ring and a sweep drawn on top of the icon: it fills clockwise until the cast lands; green = done, red = interrupted.
  4. Cast bar - the same progress as a bar, with the seconds left (or how the cast ended).
  5. Aggro - 1 monster on Bryndis and one chip per monster: name, level, HP %, and hits when it is hitting.
  6. Last skill - the last skill it used, on whom, and how long ago (for 2 minutes).
  7. Quick orders - see the next section.
  8. last notes - tap to unfold the character's last 3 notes.

A fighter shows its target too:

  1. Activity - fighting Liangma.
  2. Target - name, HP bar and distance.
  3. 2 monsters on Cassius - the aggro count.
  4. Monster chip - name · level · HP · hits.

#Quick orders (direct, run once)

# Button What is sent Notes
1 Mana !ov <Name> use <item id> The best Mana Potion in the bag (Greater first) and how many there are. Greyed out when there is none.
2 Heal !ov <Name> use <item id> The best Healing Potion.
3 CP !ov <Name> use <item id> The best CP Potion.
4 SoE now !ov <Name> soe Asks first. Uses a Scroll of Escape now; the party does not follow.
5 Stop !ov <Name> stop Stops the current attack / cast once (its routine may pick a target again).
6 Target !ov <Name> target <monster> Targets the nearest monster it can see.
7 Sit / Stand /sit or /stand L2Swarm chat command (the button shows Stand while it sits).

Bryndis: use a Scroll of Escape NOW? It stops what it is doing and goes to the nearest town (the party does not follow). — Cancel sends nothing.

#Results of an order

Every direct order goes to this character only, once, and it carries on with what it was doing afterwards. A toast in the corner says "sent…", then "delivered" (or why it was not sent), then the character's own answer ("used Mana Potion", "Greater Heal is on cooldown" ...) when its window reports it (through the override result file). Orders go through MCP, or through the file channel when MCP does not answer ("delivered (file channel)").

  1. Toasts - each stays about 6 seconds; green border = worked, red = failed.

#Where it is (live map)

The same layers as the live party view, centred on this character.

  1. Where - in words, next to the title: in Giran or 24k north of Dion.
  2. Me - the big dot in the party colour with a pulsing ring; a gold arc around it fills while it casts. Red outline = in combat, blue fill = resting, dark red = dead, grey = silent.
  3. Aggro line - an orange line from a monster to the member it attacks (thick for this character).
  4. Monster with aggro - red dot with an orange ring. Other monsters are small red dots; raid bosses are gold with a ♛.
  5. Hunting room / area - the leader's hunting room or area outline (gold, dashed) with its name.
  6. + / − / ◎ - zoom in, zoom out, and follow: ◎ lit = the map keeps the character and what it is doing in view. Dragging or zooming switches follow off; tap ◎ to switch it on again.
  7. Tapped monster - tap a monster to see its name, level, HP and who it is attacking (shown here). Tap a teammate's dot to open its page.
  8. Legend - me, teammate, monster, aggro, target, route, casting, NPC, hunting area.

Drag to move, pinch / mouse wheel / + − to zoom. All labels have the site's small map size at every zoom. The map art switches to the right underground floor in dungeons, and NPCs are drawn as diamonds (blue = gatekeeper, green = shop, grey = other) with names for the important ones.

Target line and teammates:

  1. Target line - a yellow dotted line from a member to its current target.
  2. Teammates - smaller dots in the party colour; teammates standing together share one label (Aldric +3).

Planned route:

  1. Route - the green line is the planned walk through the dungeon's room graph (teammates' routes are drawn thin and dim).
  2. Next point - the green ring.
  3. Goal - the green flag, labelled with where it goes.

A plain walk without a route is a yellow dashed line with a ring at the end; an escape run is a yellow dashed line labelled escape: <safe spot>.

Underground floor:

  1. Monsters - when zoomed in, the monsters get labels: name, level and HP when hurt.
  2. Floor map - the map art of the floor for the character's height (here a tower floor instead of the surface).

#Dead or silent characters

  1. dead chip in the header.
  2. dead as the activity. The healers resurrect it, or it respawns in town (Concepts).

  1. offline · last report 25m ago - the script stopped reporting.
  2. Live game data unavailable - red banner with L2Swarm's reason; equipment, bag, skills and buffs are then empty and the page shows what the script last reported. A character counts as online when L2Swarm says it is logged in, or its script reported within the last 2 minutes (a character played in-game through the client is not seen as logged in by L2Swarm, but its script still reports).

#Equipment

A paper doll like the game's.

  1. Paper doll - earrings, necklace and rings on the left, helmet / chest / legs / gloves / boots in the middle, weapon, shield, hair, shirt, cloak on the right. Empty slots show their name.
  2. +enchant - blue, top left of the icon.
  3. Grade - top right (D, C, B ...).
  4. ▲ - a full armor (robe, full plate) also covers the legs slot.
  5. Weapon - by name, with enchant and grade.
  6. Worn pieces - every other worn item by name.
  7. Shots - the soulshots / spiritshots in the bag, and a red low shots chip at 100 or fewer.

Tap a worn item for its details. Worn items can never be used, equipped or dropped from here:

  1. Name, enchant, grade - count, type, slot, worn.
  2. Worn items cannot be dropped from here.

Common Item - ... pieces are the cheap no-set-bonus versions the bots buy for fighters (see Gear).

#Inventory

  1. Count - 90 items · 1 quest.
  2. All - everything except quest items.
  3. Use - potions, scrolls, shots, elixirs, herbs, boxes, coupons, spirit ore, crystals.
  4. Gear - weapons and armor.
  5. Materials - everything else.
  6. Quest - quest items.
  7. find… - type part of a name; switches the filter to All and also finds quest items.
  8. Count - bottom right of an icon (1.2k, 3.5M ...). Enchant top left, grade top right.
  9. Tinted icon - the item is on a sell list (the bots sell it at every town visit).

Worn items and adena are not in the grid. Sorted: Use, Gear, Materials, Quest, then by name.

#Tap an item

  1. Item - name, enchant, grade, count, type and slot.
  2. Use now (Equip now for weapons and armor) - !ov <Name> use <item id>. Runs once, no confirmation.
  3. Drop… - asks how many (when there is more than one), then asks you to type YES (anything else cancels), then sends !ov <Name> drop <object id> <count>: the item falls on the ground. Never offered for worn items, quest items or adena.
  4. Sell at every restock - — (not on a list; known junk may still be sold), sell (<Name>) (only this character), sell (all bots), never sell. Saved at once to Scripts/data/sell_list.json; the bots read it at their next town visit, no restart.

On a phone the menu is a sheet at the bottom of the screen; on a desktop it opens next to the item. Tap outside or press Esc to close it.

#Skills

  1. tap = use now - every skill icon is a button.
  2. Ready skill - active skills as icons with the name underneath, the most used first.
  3. Cooldown - a dark sweep on top of the icon shrinks clockwise, with the seconds left; when the skill is ready again it flashes once.
  4. Passive skills (n) - folded; hover (or long-press) an icon for its name, level and description.

Toggles get their own row; a green ring means the toggle is on:

#Tap a skill

  1. Skill - level, MP cost, range, and ready or ready in 7.0 s.
  2. Use now on its target - !ov <Name> cast <skill id>.
  3. on itself - !ov <Name> cast <skill id> self.
  4. on - one button per living teammate: !ov <Name> cast <skill id> <teammate>.
  5. On cooldown - the order waits in the character's window until the skill is ready (or fails; see the toast).

Self-only skills just show Use now. No confirmation: the order is sent when you tap.

#Buffs

  1. Buffs n · debuffs n - the counts.
  2. Debuffs - first, with a red frame.
  3. Under a minute - the time turns yellow and blinks.
  4. Time bar - under each icon: the time left relative to the longest time seen for that buff on this page; the text shows hours and minutes (1h47), minutes (12m) or seconds (45s). Hover (or long-press) for the name, level and exact time.

Buffs are sorted shortest first. A character with fewer than 10 long buffs shows few long buffs: it rebuffs from the board at the next chance; you can also tap Rebuff under Orders.

#Recent steps

Every step the character tried, why it tried it, and how it ended. This is the best place to find out why a bot did something.

  1. only problems - only failed steps, quest retries and steps that ended without a result.
  2. show fights - also every monster it attacked (hidden by default, they are many).
  3. show coordinates - start point, target, distance and where the step ended.
  4. Time - when the step started (your local time). Newest on top, at most 150 lines (the box scrolls).
  5. What it tried - in plain words, with an icon for the kind of step (walk, talk to an NPC, teleport, town command, fight, help a teammate, gather or lead the team, quest, resurrect ...).
  6. while: - the bigger job this step was part of.
  7. … in progress - the newest step is still running (only the newest, and only for 15 minutes; light blue background).
  8. ✓ - the step worked, with the time it took in brackets, for example ✓ Helvetia answered (1s).
  9. — no result (replaced by the next step) - the script moved on before this step reported an end. Normal when a newer plan replaces an old one.
  10. ×n - the same step happened n times in a row (within 10 minutes) and was merged into one line.

How to read a line: 08:22:25 · Free teleport to Giran (.giran) — regroup in Giran: next hunting spot · while: dungeon: Ponti · ✓ landed 83473,148554 (1s) means: at 08:22:25 the character used the free .giran command because the team regrouped in Giran; it was doing the dungeon job at that time; it landed in Giran after 1 second.

The three ticks are remembered in your browser and apply to the same timeline on What they do.

  1. only problems ticked.
  2. ✗ - the step failed and why, for example not there — 3539 left (a walk ended 3539 units short) or Priest of Dawn did not answer 3 clicks (676 away). Failed lines have a light red background.

  1. show fights - Fight <monster> lines appear.
  2. show coordinates ticked.
  3. Coordinates - from x,y,z → x,y,z (distance) · ended at x,y,z.

#Progress, supplies, stats

  1. Progress - exp per hour (% of a level), next level (time left and clock time), kills per hour, kills in the last 5 minutes, exp in the last hour, recent deaths, level and exp %.
  2. Supplies - Scrolls of Escape, resurrection scrolls, shots, mana / healing / CP potions. Red when low (SoE 2 or fewer, res scrolls 1 or fewer, shots 200 or fewer, mana potions 100 or fewer, healing potions 5 or fewer).
  3. Combat stats - P.Atk, M.Atk, P.Def, M.Def, Atk.Spd, Cast.Spd, Accuracy, Evasion, Crit, Speed, Load (weight %), Karma, STR, DEX, CON, INT, WIT, MEN. Folded on a phone, open on wider screens.

#Orders

Orders for this character only. Every button here asks for confirmation first.

  1. Class change - !classchange: Alt+B → Career → Professions, if its level allows the next class.
  2. Rebuff - !buff: fresh buffs from the Community Board.
  3. Retreat to town - !soe: leave the fight and go to town with the free .townname command (see Concepts).
  4. All commands… - the command center sheet for this character.
  5. Task menu - every task the dashboard knows (Level, Supplies, Collect adena, Better gear, Dungeon, Soul crystals, Seven Signs, Class change, Cabinet setting, Status, Rebuff, Sell, Raid hunter, Raid mission, Joint raid, Kamaloka, Siege, Help character, Town teleport, Gatekeeper teleport, Walk to, Stop leveling, Escape, Stop everything ...). Full list: Command reference.
  6. Text box - for tasks that need a boss, town or other text (the menu entry ends with …), for example giran for Town teleport.
  7. Do - sends the chosen task.
  8. In-game (l2.exe) - play this character through the real game client (client mode).
  9. Out of game - back to playing without a client.
  10. Note - direct orders (skills, potions, items) run once and then the character carries on.

After sending, the message bar says !buff → char Aldric. The character confirms it in its notes. Orders meant for a whole party (Level, Supplies ...) are better given on the Parties tab.

Every order asks: Send to Aldric only: Rebuff (!buff) Continue?. Cancel sends nothing.

A task with a text shows the full command, for example !town giran. When the task needs a text and the box is empty, nothing is sent:

  1. Message bar - type the boss / town / place in the box next to the menu first.

#Client mode (in-game or out of game)

L2Swarm can play a character out of game (no game window, the normal way) or in game through the real game client l2.exe (L2Swarm's Hook button). In-game is useful when you want to watch or play that character yourself.

In-game (l2.exe) asks: Switch Aldric to IN-GAME? L2Swarm logs Aldric out, starts l2.exe and logs in through the client (within ~2 min). The client uses 1-2 GB RAM.

Out of game asks: Switch Aldric back to OUT OF GAME? Its l2.exe is closed and it logs in without a client.

After OK the wish is saved in Settings/client_mode.json and the watchdog task (MemWatch, see PC) starts at once; it applies the change within about 2 minutes. The message bar says Aldric: ingame — applied within ~2 min. The server refuses (message in the bar) when no config in Settings has this character selected, or when its config has no valid <L2ExePath> (L2Swarm would open a "Select L2.exe" window): close the account in L2Swarm, add <L2ExePath> with your client path to its XML, and open it again. L2Swarm runs only one hooked client at a time; if another character is already in game you get a warning and this one waits.

#Priority + quest plan

  1. P0 ... P6 - the script's priority list: P0 Survive · P1 Get unfrozen / unstuck · P2 Team safety · P3 Safe teleport · P4 Orders from you or the leader · P5 Leveling · P6 Upkeep (rebuff, class change, selling). Lower = more important; a more important task can interrupt a less important one.
  2. NOW: - the line holding control is gold, with the task that holds it. Survival (healing, potions) runs on its own and never waits for control.
  3. Current class-quest step - quest, step n/total, a progress bar and the next step (action, NPC or teleport, item to collect, place). The bots normally change class through the Community Board and class quests are off in the standard set-up, so this is usually a reference. no class quest plan right now = nothing fits this character.

#Commands sheet

Commands (header) and All commands… (Orders) open the command center's sheet for this character: every command, by category, with its options. See Command center.

#Override panel

Override… in the header opens a compact panel with every direct order for this character in one place (the same panel the raid view uses).

  1. Name, HP, MP and ✕ to close (Esc or a tap outside also close it).
  2. on … - who the skill buttons target: its current target, itself, or a teammate.
  3. Skills - tap to cast now (cooldown seconds shown on the button).
  4. Potions / scrolls - with the count in the bag; greyed out when there is none.
  5. Quick - Attack its target, Stop attacking, Scroll of Escape NOW, Move to a teammate, and Resurrect for every dead teammate. A Drop an item section (typed YES) appears when the bag is known.

Every action is one !ov <Name> <action> command, run once; the answer comes back as a toast.

#How to ...

Find out why a character is standing still

  1. Open its page (tap it on Parties).
  2. Read the activity line in Right now, and the map: a route, a walk line, aggro?
  3. In Recent steps, tick only problems to see the last failures and their reasons.
  4. Look at Priority + quest plan: if a more important task holds control (for example P2 Team safety), it is waiting for that.

Give a healer a mana potion now

  1. Open the healer's page.
  2. In Right now, tap Mana. The toast says "delivered", then the character's answer.

Make a character cast a skill on a teammate

  1. In Skills, tap the skill.
  2. Tap on . If the skill is on cooldown, the order waits until it is ready.

Throw away an item

  1. In Inventory, tap the item, then Drop….
  2. Enter how many, then type YES. Anything else cancels.

Stop a bot from selling an item

  1. Tap the item in Inventory.
  2. Pick never sell in sell at every restock.

Play a character yourself in the game client

  1. Tap In-game (l2.exe) under Orders and confirm.
  2. Wait about 2 minutes: the game client starts and logs the character in.
  3. When done, tap Out of game and confirm.

#Notes and safety

  • The page only reads game data until you press an order button. Dangerous orders ask first: SoE now, every order in Orders, client mode, and Drop (typed YES).
  • Direct orders (quick buttons, skills, items, Override) run once on this character only and do not change its plan; orders from Orders replace what it is doing.
  • Client mode restarts the character's login: do not use it during a raid or a siege.
  • If boxes stay empty (no buffs, no skills), the game data is not available right now: check the chips and the red banner in the header.
  • The dashboard uses one text scale on every page (11 px icon counts and map labels, 12 px captions and buttons, 13 px body, 14 px box titles, 16 px window titles, 20 px the character name), defined once at the top of Dashboard/index.html.

#Override menu (Act / Override…)

The override menu makes one character do one thing once, right now: cast one of its skills, use a potion or a scroll, target, attack, stop, walk to someone, resurrect a dead teammate, or drop an item. It works at any time, also in the middle of a raid. After the action the character carries on with what it was doing. Use it when the automatic behaviour is not enough, for example a healer should heal someone now, a mage is out of mana, or someone must leave with a Scroll of Escape.

It is a small panel for one character. It opens from:

Where Button Panel
Raid live view Act on each team card raid set: targets boss and focus, "Target the boss", "Move to the tank" ...
Kamaloka live view Act on each team card character set (no boss / focus targets), with Drop an item
Character page #/char/<Name> Override… in the header character set, with Drop an item

The same orders also exist as commands in the command center (category Fight, "Override: ...") and in the command reference (!ov ...).

#The panel in a raid

  1. Header - "6. Fenwick" (the member's number on the raid map and its name), its HP and MP (and "dead"), and ✕ to close.
  2. Note - "Runs ONCE on Fenwick only, right now, even mid-raid; then it carries on with what it was doing." When the character has not reported its own skill and item list yet, the note adds "Skill / item lists are a guess until its swarm.js reports them."
  3. on - who a skill is cast on: boss, focus (the minion the team kills now), self or a living teammate. On the character page the first choice is its current target.
  4. Skills - its active skills (toggles left out). A dimmed button with seconds = on cooldown ("ready in 12 s" when you hover); hover also shows the MP cost.
  5. Potions / scrolls - potions, elixirs, Scrolls of Escape / Resurrection, antidotes, herbs ... in its bag, with the count. A button with count 0 is greyed out.
  6. Quick - one-tap actions (list below).

The panel floats next to the button on wide screens (640 px and wider) and slides up from the bottom as a sheet on phones. It refreshes every second. Close it with ✕, the Esc key or a tap outside it. In a raid it also closes by itself when the raid ends.

#Every action

Quick buttons:

Button Raid Character page / Kamaloka What the character does
Target the boss yes - selects the boss
Target the focus yes - selects the team's focus target (the boss when there is none)
Attack (focus / boss) yes - attacks the focus target, else the boss
Attack its target - yes sends attack without a target: the character attacks the team's focus target, else the boss. Outside a raid or Kamaloka there is neither, so it answers "no monster "focus" in sight".
Stop attacking yes yes stops moving and drops its target (its own routine may pick one again)
Scroll of Escape NOW yes yes reads a Scroll of Escape (any kind in its bag). A hit can interrupt the cast. The party does not follow.
Move to the tank yes - walks next to the tank
Move to the boss yes - walks next to the boss
Move to - yes walks next to the first teammate in the list
Resurrect one per dead teammate one per dead teammate its resurrection skill on that teammate; a Scroll of Resurrection only when it has no res skill

Skill buttons cast that skill once on the target chosen in on. Potion / scroll buttons use that item once.

What the character checks before it acts (it refuses and says why):

  • it is dead (only stop works then);
  • a skill it has not learned, a skill on cooldown, or not enough MP;
  • a target that is not in sight;
  • no such item in the bag;
  • a walk to someone more than 6,000 game units away ("too far for an override walk");
  • a resurrection on a teammate that is not dead, or no res skill and no Scroll of Resurrection.

It always stands up first if it is sitting.

#Confirm and result

  1. Confirm line - tapping any action does not send it yet. A yellow line asks "Fenwick: Death Spike on boss?" with Do it and Cancel.

After Do it:

  1. A toast at the bottom says "Fenwick: ... — sent…".
  2. The order goes to that character only, as the swarm command !ov <name> <action>.
  3. The dashboard waits up to 25 seconds for the character's answer and shows it as a toast: green = done, red = refused or failed. Without an answer: "no answer from its window yet (it may still run)". If the order could not be sent at all: "not sent — ".

  1. Result toast - for example "Fenwick: Mana Potion used (HP 93% -> 93%, MP 34% -> 54%), 1959 left". A cast answers like "Death Spike → Carnage Lord Gato cast (MP 64% -> 58%)".

Each toast stays about 6.5 seconds.

#On the character page (Drop an item)

  1. Override… - the button in the character page header.
  2. on - its current target, self or a teammate.
  3. Quick - the character page set (attack its target, stop, Scroll of Escape, move to a teammate, resurrect).
  4. Drop an item - opens the list of its bag. Equipped items and quest items are never listed (and the character refuses to drop them).

Dropping is destructive. It asks twice, with browser dialogs:

  1. "drop how many ? (1-n)" - only for stacks; the whole stack is suggested.
  2. ": DROP ×n on the ground. This cannot be undone. Type YES to do it." - only the exact word YES sends it. Anything else (or Cancel) shows "cancelled" and sends nothing.

The dropped item lies on the ground where the character stands.

#How to ...

Give a mage a Mana Potion in a raid

  1. On the raid live view, tap Act on the mage's card.
  2. Tap Mana Potion under Potions / scrolls.
  3. Tap Do it. The toast shows the MP before and after.

Make the healer heal the tank now

  1. Act on the healer's card.
  2. Set on to the tank's name.
  3. Tap the heal skill (it must not be dimmed), then Do it.

Get a stuck character out with a Scroll of Escape

  1. Open its character page and tap Override….
  2. Tap Scroll of Escape NOW, then Do it. Keep in mind that a hit interrupts the scroll, and that the party stays where it is.

#Notes

  • One action = one swarm command !ov <name> <action> ... sent to that character (through L2Swarm, or through the file channel when L2Swarm does not answer). Party chat reaches the whole party, but only the named character's window acts.
  • The character writes its answer to Logs/override_<name>.json and to its notes as "user override (...)", so it also shows in its recent steps on the character page.
  • The skill and item lists come from the character's own report in its live state file (ov: skills with ready / cooldown, potions and scrolls with counts, the bag for dropping). Until a character reports them, the panel shows a guess: the skills it used most in the raid and the usual potions and scrolls, without counts.
  • The !ov commands: cast <skill id> [boss | focus | tank | self | <teammate> | <object id>], use <item id or object id>, soe, drop <object id> [count], target <...>, attack [<...>], stop, move <tank | boss | teammate>, res <teammate>.

#Map (#/map)

The world map shows every character as a dot on the Lineage 2 world map, coloured by party, with a dashed line to where each one is walking. Use it to see at a glance where the parties are, whether someone was left behind, and who is offline or dead. Below the map is a list of all characters; tapping one centres the map on it.

The map is the game's own world map art (one tile per game region, from your Maps folder). It is drawn with the Leaflet map library, which the page loads from the internet (cdnjs). Without internet the tab says map library could not load (no internet?). Positions come from the script state of each character (Logs/swarm_state_<Name>.json) and refresh every 4 seconds.

#The map

  1. Keep in view - which characters the map keeps in view: Everyone (all online characters), Party <leader>, or one character by name.
  2. follow - when ticked, the map moves by itself to keep that choice in view as the characters move. Dragging the map unticks it, so you can look around; picking something in the menu ticks it again.
  3. Online count - 38/39 online · tap a dot for details: characters that reported in the last 30 seconds / all characters seen in the last 6 hours.
  4. Dot labels - Name level. Characters standing within 300 game units of each other share one label: Aldric 50 +8 means Aldric and 8 more stand there. Labels are hidden when you zoom far out.
  5. Zoom - + / − buttons; you can also pinch (phone) or use the mouse wheel. Drag to move the map.

#One party in view, walk-target lines

  1. Party Valerius picked in Keep in view: the map zooms to that party (here hunting in pairs, spread over a field).
  2. Character dot - filled with the party colour (each party has its own colour; the same colours are used on the Parties tab and the character mini-map). The party leader's dot is larger.
  3. Walking to - a dashed line in the party colour from a character to the place it is walking to (its current step, while that step has no result yet).
  4. Label - name and level (+n when several stand together).

Dot colours

Dot Meaning
party colour, white ring online, alive
larger dot party leader
dark red with a red ring, label ends with ✝ dead
grey, half transparent, label ends with (offline) the script has not reported for more than 30 seconds

Characters that have not reported for more than 6 hours are not shown at all.

Tap a dot to open that character's character page.

#One character in view

  1. One character picked: the map centres on it and zooms in.
  2. Its dot.

#The list below the map

  1. Colour dot - party colour; grey = offline, dark red = dead.
  2. Name · level · HP %.
  3. Task - the first 48 characters of what the character is doing.
  4. offline - shown on the right for characters that stopped reporting.
  5. ✝ - dead.

The list is sorted by party, leader first, then by name. Tap a row to keep that character in view: the map centres on it, follow is ticked, and the page scrolls up to the map.

follow keep the choice in view while they move no
Drag / zoom look around (unticks follow) no

Tap a list row centres the map on that character no

Nothing on this tab sends an order or changes a file.

#How to ...

Find a character that was left behind

  1. Pick its party in Keep in view. A dot far away from the others stands out at once.
  2. Tap the dot to open its page and read its story and timeline.

Watch one character travel

  1. Tap its row in the list (or pick it in Keep in view).
  2. Leave follow ticked: the map pans along as it moves; the dashed line shows where it is going.

#Notes

  • The map shows the surface. For characters underground (catacombs, towers) use the character page live map, which switches to the right floor.

#What they do (#/logs)

This tab answers "what has this character been doing, and what is everyone doing right now?". It shows one character's full intent timeline and notes side by side, plus the latest activity of all characters and the latest script errors. Use it to follow a problem back in time, or to watch the whole swarm work.

#One character: timeline and notes

  1. Character - pick a character (the menu shows name, level and class). Your choice is remembered in the browser.
  2. Timeline filters - only problems, show fights, show coordinates. They work exactly like Recent steps on the character page and are shared with it (tick them here, and the character page shows the same).
  3. Newest step - the timeline, newest first: what it tried, why (while: ...) and how it ended.
  4. Notes from this character - its notes (see below).

On a desktop the timeline and the notes stand side by side; on a phone the notes come below the timeline.

#How to read the timeline

Each line is one step the bot tried:

08:22:25  [icon]  Free teleport to Giran (.giran) — regroup in Giran: next hunting spot     ✓ landed 83473,148554 (1s)
                  while: dungeon: Ponti -> 2nd floor
  • Time - when the step started (your local time).
  • Icon - the kind of step: walk, talk to an NPC, teleport, free town command, fight, help a teammate, gather or lead the team, quest, resurrect, wait ...
  • Text - what it tried, in plain words.
  • ×n after the text - the same step happened n times in a row (within 10 minutes) and was merged into one line.
  • while: - the bigger job the step served.
  • Result on the right:
    • ✓ - it worked, with the time it took in brackets;
    • ✗ - it failed, and why (red background);
    • … in progress - the newest step, still running (light blue background; at most 15 minutes, after that it counts as no result);
    • — no result (replaced by the next step) - the bot moved on before the step reported an end.
  • With show coordinates: from x,y,z → x,y,z (distance) · ended at x,y,z.

Up to 150 steps are shown (the server reads the last 400 lines of Logs/intent_<Name>.log).

#Notes from this character

  1. Time of the note.
  2. Green line - something worked (DONE, worked, arrived, OK).
  3. Red line - something failed (FAIL, failed, gave up, stuck, error, dead).

These are the last 250 notes of the character from the shared log Logs/swarm_buffs.log (every bot writes its notes there), newest on top. The character page shows only the last 3 of them (Right now → last notes).

#Everyone: latest activity, and script errors

  1. Filter text - type any text (a name, a place, a word like failed) to show only matching lines. Not case-sensitive.
  2. Name - which character wrote the line. Tap it to open that character's page.
  3. What happened - the note itself. Green and red colours as above.
  4. Script errors - the last 12 lines of Logs/swarm_errors.log: JavaScript errors inside swarm.js on any character. A few old errors are normal; many new ones after an update mean something is broken (see PC for deploying a fixed script).

Everyone — latest activity shows the last 60 notes of all characters, newest first.

#Filtering

  1. Typed filter - here Quill.
  2. Only matching lines remain.

#Every control

Control What it does Saved?
Character menu whose timeline and notes are shown in your browser
only problems / show fights / show coordinates filter the timeline (also on the character page) in your browser
Filter text filter Everyone — latest activity no
Name in a line opens the character page –

Nothing on this tab sends an order or changes a file.

#Refresh

The everyone/errors lists refresh every 4 seconds; the chosen character's timeline and notes every 8 seconds. Nothing refreshes while the browser tab is hidden.

#How to ...

Find out why a character failed to teleport

  1. Pick the character.
  2. Tick only problems.
  3. Look for a red Teleport to ... or Free teleport ... line; the text after ✗ says why (no adena, the NPC did not answer, landed in the wrong place ...). Tick show coordinates to see where it stood.

See what one party did in the last minutes

  1. In Filter text, type a word from the party's task, or the leader's name.
  2. Read the lines from top (newest) to bottom.

#Teleports and Giran town routes

The Teleports tab (#/tp) answers four questions: which gatekeeper menus do the bots know, where is every character right now, which roads do the bots walk inside Giran, and where is a certain NPC (the Find an NPC box, described on its own page). The gatekeeper menus are the real menus the bots saw on the server: every time a bot opens a gatekeeper, the menu is saved to Scripts/data/gk_live/<gatekeeper>.json, and the bots plan every trip from these menus (a destination that is not on the menu of the town a character stands in is reached through other towns). Words like .townname, landing and SoE are in the glossary.

#Teleports tab (#/tp)

  1. Find a destination… - filter the gatekeeper cards: only cards with a matching destination (or a matching town name) stay, and the matching destinations turn green.
  2. Giran town routes - one button per recorded route inside Giran, plus a field and + New route (see Giran town routes).
  3. Find an NPC - search every NPC of the world by name, id, role ("grocer dion") or what it offers, and send a party to it. It has its own page: Find an NPC.
  4. Where everyone is now - one chip per character (see below).
  5. Gatekeeper cards - one card per gatekeeper the bots have seen, sorted by town.

The tab loads its data when you open it (open it again to refresh).

#Where everyone is now

Each chip reads Name: Town or Name: in the field:

  1. Town (bold) - the character stands within 6000 of a known gatekeeper of that town. Hover (desktop) to see which gatekeeper.
  2. in the field (yellow) - no known gatekeeper nearby; no SoE! in red is added when it has no Scroll of Escape left.
  3. Red chip - the character has not reported for more than 30 s (offline or frozen).

Tap a chip to open that character's page (Character page).

#Filter

  1. Matching destination in green (here "oren": Town of Oren, Oren's teleports …).
  2. Town and gatekeeper of each card that has a match.

#One gatekeeper card

  1. Town · gatekeeper (title).
  2. Here now - characters standing next to this gatekeeper.
  3. Destinations - every destination link of every menu page the bots opened. A gatekeeper usually has two pages with the same places: one without prices and one with the price in adena ("Town of Oren - 9400 …").
  4. Other menu entries - links that are not destinations (Teleport, Exchange Dimension Diamonds, Nobless teleports, Arena / Monster Race, Fantasy Isle, Quest …).
  5. Seen … by … - when the menu was saved and by which character. "no destinations seen yet" = only the first page was opened.

#Giran town routes

In Giran the bots walk only recorded routes: start = the .giran landing, then to a shop (grocer, warehouse, weapons, jewelry, armor, blacksmith, symbol maker …). They never take a shortcut through the town. This box lets you correct those routes with the same editor as the raid routes (route editor). The bots re-read Scripts/data/giran_routes.json every minute, so a saved change is used within a minute.

  1. Route button - place · NPC (number of points). Tap to open that route in the editor below (it asks first when the open route has unsaved changes).
  2. New route name - lowercase letters and digits, for example gatekeeper.
  3. + New route - opens a draft for that name.
  4. Status - "Giran route ''" with when it was edited (or "recorded by hand"), or "new route, not saved yet".
  5. Map - the same map as the raid editor: the blue square is the Giran start (the .giran landing), the gold ♛ marks the end (the NPC); tap to add points, drag to move, wheel to zoom. The bar above has Map, Zoom + / −, Fit route and Landing = point 1.

  1. + its current position - insert a character's position after the selected point (pick the character in the menu on the left).
  2. Record - record a character's walk (a point every ~250 units).
  3. Save - save the route (2 to 200 points). Town routes have no lock: what you save is what the bots walk. If point 1 is more than 300 away from the Giran start, the start is put in front automatically.
  4. Delete route - delete it (confirmation). Bots that need it then cannot walk there.
  5. Undo changes - reload the saved version.

The point list (x / y / z, ↑ ↓ + ✕) and Paste coordinates work exactly as in the raid route editor. Every save or delete keeps the old file in Scripts/data/routes/giran_history/.

#A new route

  1. new route, not saved yet. 2. The draft starts with one point, the Giran start: "New route: point 1 is the Giran start. Add points on the map (or a character position) and press Save."

#Delete

"Delete the Giran route ''? (The old file is kept in Scripts/data/routes/giran_history.) Bots that need it then cannot walk there."

#How to ...

Check whether a character can teleport somewhere

  1. Type the destination in Find a destination….
  2. Look which towns' cards still show it; then look in Where everyone is now which town the character stands in.

Fix a Giran walk that gets stuck

  1. Tap the route button (for example grocer · Helvetia).
  2. Select the point before the problem (tap it on the map or its row), then tap the map to add a point around the obstacle, or walk a character there in the game and press + its current position.
  3. Press Save. The bots use it within a minute.

Add a route to a new Giran NPC

  1. Type a name (gatekeeper) and press + New route.
  2. Add the points from the start to the NPC (record a character's walk is the easiest).
  3. Press Save.

#Notes

  • The gatekeeper menus are only what the bots have seen; a gatekeeper nobody opened yet has no card.
  • A price shown with the menu is the server's price at the time it was saved.
  • The Giran town routes are shared by every party.

#Find an NPC (NPC atlas) (#/tp)

Find an NPC searches the NPC atlas: every NPC of the game world, where it stands (town, dungeon floor and room, or field), what it does (grocer, gatekeeper, warehouse, priest of dawn ...), which teleports it offers and which quests it gives. Each match has a small map, and one tap sends a party there: the leader takes the whole party to that NPC and opens its dialog. Use it when you need a particular NPC and do not want to walk the party there by hand.

It is a box on the Teleports tab (#/tp), between "Giran town routes" and "Where everyone is now".

#The search box and a match

  1. Search box - type at least 2 letters. The results appear about a third of a second after you stop typing.
  2. NPC name - followed by its title (Grocer, Gatekeeper ...), its NPC id (#30080) and, when it differs, its name in the spawn list.
  3. ✓ live (green) - a bot has opened this NPC's dialog and its menu was saved. Hover to see which saved dialogs it comes from.
  4. ⚠ menu differs (red) - the live menu does not match the datapack (hover for the differences). Live matches come first in the list.
  5. Where - the dungeon · floor · room, or the town, or the region and how far it is from the nearest town; then its position (x, y, z) and its roles.
  6. Small map - 3,000 x 3,000 game units around the NPC (yellow dot), on the game's map art. In a town the street network is drawn faintly; in a dungeon the hallway network of its floor.
  7. Send party - one button per party whose leader reported in the last 2 minutes. See Send a party.

A match can also show Teleports: (the first 6 destinations it offers, with what they need, for example a level or an item) and Quests: (the first 5 quests it starts or takes part in).

#What you can type

You type Finds
a name: Penelope, Helvetia the NPC with exactly that name (or that spawn-list name). From 4 letters, names that contain the text are found too.
an id: 30487 or #30487 the NPC with that id
a role: grocer, gatekeeper, warehouse, priest of dawn, class master, blacksmith ... every NPC with that role (a role that starts with the text counts too)
role or name + town: grocer giran, warehouse in dion, gatekeeper at oren the same, only in that town
what it offers: teleport:Cruma Tower 2nd floor (also link: or offers:) NPCs whose teleport list, or whose live dialog links, contain that text

At most 12 matches are shown, live ones first. "nothing found" means no NPC matches.

  1. First match 2. Second match - every warehouse keeper of Giran, each with its own map and buttons.

  1. Teleports it offers - the destinations of a dungeon teleporter, for example the Cruma Tower floor teleporters.

#Send a party

Send party sends the swarm command !goto npc #<id> to that whole party. It asks first:

The dialog names the party, how many characters it has, the order ("Go to Helvetia (Giran)") with its command, and which members are busy right now and will change orders. Cancel sends nothing.

What the party does (the leader leads, the members follow):

  1. The leader stops leveling and any raid hunt, and takes control of the party. (If a more important task holds control at that moment, for example survival or a safe teleport, the order is skipped and the leader notes "a more important task holds control".)
  2. To the town - when the NPC is in a town, the party teleports there with .townname.
  3. Into the dungeon - for an NPC in a dungeon: the gatekeeper route to the dungeon, the floor teleporter or the walk-in to the right floor, then a room-by-room walk to the NPC (floor teleporters on the way are used).
  4. Into the field - for an NPC outside towns and dungeons: a teleport as close as possible, then a walk.
  5. In town - in Giran the recorded Giran town routes are walked; in other towns the street network.
  6. Talk - the leader opens the NPC's dialog (it is saved to Logs/npc_<name>.html).

After that the party stays there and waits for your next order: leveling does not start again by itself (as after !stop). The trip shows in What they do as "npc trip: ... -> ...: ", with done or failed and the reason ("could not get to Giran", " is not in sight", " did not answer" ...). The task line of the leader shows the current step, for example "to Helvetia: walk (3/4)".

#The command

Command Does
!goto npc <what> the party leader takes the whole party to the best matching NPC and opens its dialog. <what> is anything from the table above.
!goto npc <what> <character> only that character goes, alone

The command understands a few short forms the search box does not: gk (gatekeeper), wh (warehouse), shop (merchant), dawn / dusk (priest of dawn / dusk), master (class master), weapons, armor, jewelry, trainer, spellbook, ziggurat, olympiad. A name in the command must be the exact NPC name.

"Best matching" means the cheapest trip from where the leader stands: the same dungeon floor first, then the same dungeon, the same town, and so on. With an id (#30081) there is only one NPC. In the command center the command is Move → Go to an NPC (anywhere)… (it also asks first).

#How to ...

Take a party to a grocer

  1. Open the Teleports tab and type grocer giran in the Find an NPC box.
  2. Check the match (the small map shows where it stands).
  3. Tap Send party and confirm with OK.
  4. Follow the trip on the live party view or in What they do.

Find which NPC teleports to a dungeon floor

  1. Type teleport: and the destination, for example teleport:Cruma Tower 2nd floor.
  2. Each match lists its teleports; the ones you need are in the list.

#Notes

  • The atlas is Scripts/data/npc_atlas.json, built from the datapack (spawns, teleports, quests, shops) and from the NPC dialogs the bots saved (the "live" menus). swarm.js re-reads it when the file changes, so a rebuilt atlas is used without a restart.
  • The dashboard reads the atlas on every search (/api/npcfind?q=...); the search only reads, it never changes anything.
  • The street and hallway networks on the small maps come from Scripts/data/town_graph/ and Scripts/data/dungeon_graph/. Without them the small map shows only the map art.

#Raid bosses, raid routes and reports

The Raid bosses tab is where you plan and follow raid boss hunting. It is a board: one compact card per raid boss of the High Five datapack with its level, whether it is probably up (with a live respawn countdown), which of your parties it fits and how far away their leader is, and badges for a saved route or fight area. From here you send a party to one boss, start an automatic raidhunt (one boss after the other) for any party, open a boss's own page to correct its walking route and its fight area, and read the saved routes, fight reports, loot log and daily dungeons sections. The raid team templates (which classes a big boss needs) live on the Clan tab and are described at the end of this page. While a raid fight runs, it is pinned on top of the board; the fight itself is shown in the Raid live view (raid HUD).

Words used on this page (raid curse, focus, minion, landing, .townname, …) are explained in the glossary.

Where the data comes from (all read live, no restart needed):

What File
Boss list, levels, spawns, minions, nearest teleport, curse level Scripts/data/raidbosses_h5.json (datapack)
Drop lists Scripts/data/raid_drops_h5.json (datapack)
Seen alive / killed / found dead Logs/raid_status.json, Logs/raid_seen.log, Logs/raid_respawn.log (written by the bots)
Raidhunt progress Logs/raidhunt.json (the party leader writes it every 2 s)
Saved routes Scripts/data/routes/raid/<boss id>.json (old versions in routes/raid/history/)
Fight areas see Raid fight area
Loot Logs/raid_loot.log
Fight reports Logs/raid_reports/*.json + Logs/raid_heals.log
Daily dungeon switches Logs/daily_enabled.json, progress Logs/daily_<leader>.json, Logs/daily.log, Logs/kamaloka.log

#The board (#/raids)

Open it with the Raid bosses tab. Your choices on this page (party, filters, sort, which sections are open) are remembered in your browser.

  1. Party - "party Aldric (9, lvl 49-50)". The fit chips, the distances, the next badge and the Raid buttons of the cards are for this party. (A running raidhunt's party is chosen by default.)
  2. Summary - how many bosses, how many seen alive, how many saved routes.
  3. Raidhunt - a fold-out with one row per party; the title says who hunts right now ("party Aldric hunts Carnage Lord Gato" or "nobody hunts right now"). Open by default.
  4. One party's row - party name, level range and size, Raidhunt (start it for that party, with confirmation) and Next if it hunts: the first three bosses raidhunt would take now. While that party hunts, the row shows its progress instead (see Raidhunt row).
  5. Find a boss, zone or minion - text filter (also matches minion names and the teleport).
  6. Region - "near Oren (12)" etc.: only bosses closest to that town.
  7. Sort - by level, by respawn (up first, then the soonest to come back), by distance from the party leader, or by name.
  8. fits / all levels - "fits" hides bosses that are too hard or would curse the party; the number is how many bosses there are.
  9. Status filter - any status / up now (alive, should be up, maybe up) / respawn < 3 h / dead, each with its count.
  10. min lvl / max lvl - level range.
  11. Count - "N of M bosses", show all (clears every filter), and which party the fit is for.

#Boss cards

Tap a card (anywhere but its buttons) or its name to open the boss page.

  1. Level and status ring - the boss level; the ring's colour is the status (alive / should be up, maybe up, dead, unknown).
  2. Name - opens the boss page.
  3. Badges - next (gold: what raidhunt takes next for this party; the card has a gold edge), LIVE (being fought now), area (a fight area is set), route / route ✓ (a saved route / a locked one; ! = it failed recently), epic, no hunt (raidhunt skips it: epic, inside a dungeon, no walkable way, or not for one party - a manual Raid order still works).
  4. Zone line - zone, nearest town, number of minions, and safe ≤ N: the highest member level that does not get the raid curse (the lowest of boss and minion levels + 8). Hover for the teleport and walk.
  5. Status - alive (seen at …), dead with "up in 5h 12m" and a bar, maybe up with "window ends in …" and a bar, should be up ("window ended …"), or unknown ("never seen dead"). The countdowns tick every second.
  6. Parties - a chip for every party the boss fits, plus the chosen party even when it does not fit: fits, easy (well below the party but no curse), too hard (more than 3 levels above the party's lowest member), curse (a member would be cursed), and the distance from that party's leader.
  7. Raid - send the chosen party to this boss now (!mission raid <boss>, confirmation).

Under the parties a line shows the last kill ("✓ killed …") with the three biggest loot items, or the last loot.

The fit rule is the same as raidhunt's: no member above the boss's curse level + 8, and the boss at most 3 levels above the party's lowest member. A card that changes status flashes once.

Cards with every status, sorted by respawn:

  1. alive. 2. should be up (the respawn window is over). 3. maybe up with the countdown to the end of the window.
  2. Last kill and its loot. A dead card (killed, earliest respawn still to come) shows "up in …" with a bar the same way.

The respawn window is the death time plus the datapack respawn time (for most bosses 12-60 hours; the server's real times are not known). A boss "found dead" (not killed by us) gives only an upper bound for its death time. When the bots have measured a respawn themselves, the bar's tooltip says "measured … h" (≤ = upper bound).

Badges and fit chips (desktop, all levels 38-45):

  1. epic. 2. no hunt. 3. route badge (✓ = locked, ! = failed lately). 4. curse chip. An area badge and a too hard chip look the same way.

#Confirmations

Every order asks first. The box names the party, how many characters get the order and which of them are busy and will change what they are doing:

Button Sends Confirmation
Raidhunt (party row) !raidhunt to that party yes, with busy characters listed
Stop (hunting party row) !raidhunt stop yes
Raid (card) !mission raid <boss> to the chosen party yes
Raid it (boss page) !mission raid <boss> yes
Delete (saved route) deletes the route file yes

#What a raid order does

!mission raid <boss> makes the party leader run the whole raid by himself: the party stops what it does, regroups in a town, rebuffs from the Community Board, restocks, teleports to the landing (or the start of a saved route) and walks to the boss's waiting spot. There it clears the monsters around the fight area, gathers, raises the dead, counts down in party chat (10, 5, 3, 2, 1, GO) and the tank pulls. The party never escapes from a raid: it fights until the boss dies or the last member falls. After a kill everyone loots for a minute. The leader writes the live view during the fight and a fight report at the end. Where it waits, what it clears and where it fights can be set per boss: Raid fight area.

#Raidhunt

Raidhunt is "take the next boss on the list until it gets too hard". The party leader:

  1. Builds the candidate list: normal raid bosses (no epic bosses), whose raid-curse level is at least the party's highest level - 8 and whose level is at most the party's lowest level + 3; no bosses inside dungeons (towers, temples, crypts, caves, deep underground); no boss whose way there passes monsters far above the party; no boss that is known dead and still inside its earliest respawn; none that failed to be reached twice (Logs/raid_unreachable.json) or was skipped in the last 12 hours (Logs/raidhunt_skip.json).
  2. Sorts it: clan quest bosses first, then lowest level, then nearest.
  3. Runs a full raid mission on the first one (see above), records the outcome and waits 30 s.
  4. Stops at the first wiped or timeout ("too hard"). A boss that was not found is marked dead; one that could not be reached is skipped.
  5. When no boss is up, the party levels meanwhile and looks again every 15 minutes.

A raidhunt survives a restart of the bots (it is resumed).

#Raidhunt row

While a party hunts, its row shows the progress (refreshed every few seconds):

  1. raidhunt · current boss (lvl, time on this boss); tap the boss for its page.
  2. Stop - stop the raidhunt (confirmation).
  3. Phase - Regroup → Teleport → Walk → Fight → Loot → Done; the current one is highlighted, passed ones are dimmed.
  4. Raw step - the leader's own task text (for example "leading team to Carnage Lord Gato (route point 7/22)").
  5. Next / Done - the next bosses on its list, and the last results: killed (green), wiped / timeout (orange), not-found / lost (grey).
  6. Other parties - their own row with Raidhunt and "Next if it hunts".

#A raid running: the LIVE pin

While a raid fight runs, a red LIVE strip is pinned on top of the board:

  1. LIVE · boss. 2. Party, members alive, fight clock, phase, and the boss HP bar. 3. Watch - the full raid live view. 4. Party view - the live view of the fighting party (party live view).
  2. The hunting party's row shows the Fight phase.

#Saved routes

A fold-out under the board, closed by default (your choice is remembered). Its title counts the routes: bosses, locked, learned, and how many failed lately.

  1. Saved routes and the counts.
  2. What they are - these are learned routes, not characters wandering off: when a party reaches a raid boss, its leader saves the walk from the teleport landing to the boss, and every party reuses it next time (one route per boss). Routes drawn or corrected on the dashboard are locked: the bots walk exactly those.
  3. all / locked / learned / failed - filter with counts.
  4. Region group - "near Oren (5)".
  5. Route shape - a small drawing of the walk (start dot, end dot).
  6. Details - the boss (link) and level, locked / learned; "From · points · km walk" (a .town start, a gatekeeper start, or "after the automatic teleport"); who recorded it and when, or when it was drawn / corrected on the dashboard; how often it was used, the last good use, failures (red) and automatic fixes.
  7. Map / Lock / Delete - Map opens the boss page scrolled to the route editor; Lock / Unlock changes the lock at once (a learned route is dropped after 2 failures, a locked one never); Delete asks first:

"Delete the saved route to ? The old version is kept in routes/raid/history. The bots record a new walk next time they reach it."

#Fight reports

A fold-out under the board (closed by default; the title shows how many fights and the last one).

  1. Fight reports - number of fights and the last result.
  2. Levels - every character's level, experience % and class (★ = party leader).
  3. Loot found in raids - total adena and every item ever picked up in raids, with counts.
  4. Kills - every boss killed (×N when more than once) and the last kill time.

Below them one line per fight, newest first: boss, level, the outcome (dead green, wiped / lost / timeout orange, not-found grey), the fight time (m:ss), when, and ✝ N when members died. Tap a line to open it:

  1. Boss and level. 2. Outcome and duration.
  2. Started by (pull / engaged) and duration.
  3. Deaths - who died and how often.
  4. Heals - per healer: number of heals, per skill, and the three members healed most (from Logs/raid_heals.log during the fight). Also Minions killed, Ultimate Defense count, Loot (picked up within 5 minutes after the fight) and Level ups.
  5. Timeline - every event of the fight: deaths and wipes in red, minion kills / results / "back up" in green, Ultimate Defense, countdown and focus changes in yellow, resisted debuffs and aggro messages in white.

#Loot log

The last 20 kills from Logs/raid_loot.log (pick-ups from the same boss within 3 minutes count as one kill):

  1. Loot log - the title shows how many kills had loot and the last one.
  2. Boss and time of the kill. 3. Who picked it up. 4. Item with icon and count.

#Daily dungeons

  1. Daily dungeons - the title says for which parties a daily dungeon is on ("off for every party").
  2. Kamaloka: ON / OFF - one box per daily leader (the dailyLeaders list in swarm.config.json). When ON, the party leader takes the party into a Kamaloka that fits all members once per day, by himself, when the party is free. The bots read the switch live.
  3. Pailaka (coming), Rift (coming) - switches that exist but are not built in the script yet.
  4. Today - the day of the last daily run and, per dungeon, done / not done and the number of tries (max 2 per day). When the last run was on an earlier day it says "resets today". Recent lists entries from Logs/daily.log (ok green, fail orange).
  5. Kamaloka log - the last Kamaloka runs from Logs/kamaloka.log.

Tapping a switch asks first:

Switching OFF stops future runs but does not abort a run that has started. The answer is saved in Logs/daily_enabled.json. Kamaloka itself has its own tab: see Kamaloka.

#Boss page (#/raid/<id>)

Tap a card, a boss name, a raidhunt link or Map in the saved routes. The tab bar keeps Raid bosses highlighted.

  1. ◀ Back - back to where you came from (the board when you opened the page directly).
  2. Level and status ring.
  3. Name (with LIVE / epic badges), zone, nearest town, HP, datapack respawn hours.
  4. Party - the party the page is judged for (the same choice as on the board).
  5. Raid it - sends !mission raid <boss> to that party (confirmation). While the boss is fought, a Watch live button appears.
  6. All bosses - back to the board.
  7. Status bar - the status with its countdown and bar, as on the card.
  8. Status & respawn - status, the respawn window (earliest – latest), the datapack range and the measured respawn, when it was seen alive; below it the kill / respawn history.
  9. Facts & parties - see below.
  10. ✎ Edit (Fight area) - opens the fight area editor: Raid fight area.

  1. Status & respawn - status line, window, datapack / measured respawn.
  2. Kill / respawn history - every kill, "not found" and measured respawn ("respawned after ≤ 22.2 h (dead since …, found dead)"), newest first.
  3. Parties - every party with its level range, its fit (fits / easy / too hard / curse) and the distance from its leader.
  4. Facts - Curse ("a member above level N gets the raid curse", with the minions' lowest level), Minions, Way there (the nearest teleport, the walk, and the highest monster level on the way), Raidhunt (takes it when it fits, or why it skips it), Spawn coordinates, Raid points, and Danger notes when the datapack has them.
  5. Fight area - "area set" with the number of points and how the clear area and waiting spot are set, or what the team does without one ("clears only aggressive monsters within 1200 of the boss … waits ~1500 away … fights where the boss stands").

When the boss is being fought right now, a LIVE fight box with the live view appears at the top of the page:

  1. LIVE badge. 2. Watch live. 3. The LIVE fight box.

Further down the page: Route to this boss (the route editor, below), Drops, What we got from it and Fight reports of this boss.

#Route editor

The route editor is the Route to this boss box (its title shows the nearest teleport and the walk). It shows the walk the bots use from the landing (or a town) to the boss, and lets you correct it with numbers, taps on the map, a character's position, a recorded walk or pasted /loc lines. Nothing is saved until you press a Save button.

  1. Status - locked (the bots use exactly this route) or recorded by the bots (a better walk may replace it), how often it was used, how often it failed, and when it was recorded or edited. "not saved yet" = no route for this boss.
  2. Start - gatekeeper teleport or .townname (walk from the town). With a start set, every member walks this route from the start itself (the leader waits at checkpoints). Without a start the bots use the route only after their automatic teleport.
  3. Gatekeeper teleport - type or pick "Town -> destination" from the list (every destination the bots have seen on a live gatekeeper menu, prices removed).
  4. Map - world (outside) or dungeon / floor N (the client's own map of a dungeon floor, where one exists).
  5. Zoom + / Zoom − - zoom the map (also the mouse wheel).
  6. Fit route - zoom so the whole route, the landing and the boss fit.
  7. Landing = point 1 - put the landing in as the first point.
  8. Boss spawn = last point - add the boss spawn as the last point.
  9. The map - blue square = landing, green square = a .town landing, white dots = waypoints (every 5th is numbered), red = the selected point, purple = points inside a dungeon layer, gold ♛ = boss spawn, coloured dots = characters standing nearby (live). Tap = a new point after the selected one (it takes the height z of the selected point). Tap a point = select it. Drag = move the map. Wheel = zoom around the pointer.

Under the line "N points · km walk" the editor shows unsaved changes in yellow when you changed something, and the line Landing: ... · Boss spawn: x, y, z with the exact coordinates.

  1. Legend of the map and the mouse/touch help.
  2. Character - every character that reported in the last minute.
  3. + its current position - insert that character's exact x, y, z after the selected point.
  4. ● Record its walk - walk the character yourself in the game; the editor adds a point every ~250 units (and at every height change of 150+) on the map layer shown. The button turns into ■ Stop recording .
  5. Save & lock - save, and lock: the bots use exactly this route and never replace it with their own recording.
  6. Save unlocked - save without locking (a better recorded walk may replace it later).
  7. Unlock / Lock - change the lock of the saved route without changing its points.
  8. Delete route - delete the saved route (confirmation; the old file is kept in routes/raid/history). The bots record a new one the next time they reach the boss.
  9. Undo changes - reload the saved route (asks first when there are unsaved changes).
  10. Selected point - the gold row is the selected point (tap a row to select it; the map switches to that point's layer).
  11. x / y / z - type exact numbers; the change counts as soon as you leave the field.
  12. ↑ ↓ + ✕ - move the point up or down, insert a point half way to the next one, delete the point. The step column shows the distance from the point before (and "floor N" for dungeon points).

Saving needs at least 2 points and a start (or a landing text). Up to 500 points. Every save keeps the old version in Scripts/data/routes/raid/history/. Saving says "saved and locked — the bots use exactly this route" (or "saved").

#Tap on the map

  1. The new point appears after the selected one and becomes the selected (red) point; its number is shown.
  2. unsaved changes appears until you save.

#Add a character's position

  1. Pick the character. 2. Press + its current position. 3. The new point is inserted after the selected one (here after point 1).
  2. Its exact x / y / z come from the character.

#Record a walk

  1. While recording, the button reads ■ Stop recording and the message line counts the points. Walk the character in the game (or let it walk), press the button again when you are there, check the points and press Save.

#Start in a town (.townname)

  1. Choose .townname (walk from the town).
  2. Pick the town (Gludin, Gludio, Dion, Giran, Oren, Aden, Hunters, Heine, Goddard, Rune, Schuttgart). The bots use .<town> and land at the town's fixed landing spot (green square on the map).
  3. Town landing = point 1 puts that landing in as the first point. The route may lead through the town (for example to a gate); your own routes are allowed to walk out of a town.

#Paste coordinates

  1. Open Paste coordinates.
  2. One point per line: x y z, x, y, z, or a /loc line copied from the game ("Current location : -12345, 67890, -3456").
  3. Replace the route with these - replaces every point (needs at least 2 lines; asks first).
