  4. Add after the selected point - inserts the pasted points after the selected one.

#Delete

"Delete the saved route to ? (The old version is kept in routes/raid/history.) The bots record a new one next time."

#A boss without a saved route

  1. not saved yet. 2. The editor starts a draft from the landing to the boss spawn: "No saved route yet — this is a draft from the landing to the spawn. Add points and press Save." Nothing is written until you save.

#Dungeon floors

  1. Map → dungeon / floor N shows the client's map of that floor (only where the client has one for that area).
  2. Points you add while a floor is shown belong to that floor (purple); points of another layer are dimmed. Walk from the entrance outside on the world map to the door, then switch the map to the floor and continue inside. Use Record or + its current position inside, because the height (z) matters there.

#Drops

The full drop list from the datapack.

  1. Drop group - "group drops X% (×1.5 ≈ Y%), then ONE item", or "each item rolls on its own". Spoil groups are marked Spoil group.
  2. Count · chance · ×1.5 - how many drop, the datapack chance, and in bold an estimate for a server with 1.5 × drop rates (the server's real rates may differ).
  3. Who / what - for the chosen party at its current levels:
    • green use now: names - members that can wear/use it now;
    • soon (lvl N): names - members up to 8 levels below its grade;
    • blue (crafter material/recipe) - give it to the crafter;
    • upgrade gear (X-grade enchant) - an enchant scroll someone can use;
    • grey sell (...) - nobody in the party can use it; check (special) - life stones, soul crystals, dyes, books.
  4. Chance bar - the ×1.5 chance as a bar.

#What we got from it and its fight reports

  1. What we got from it - every kill of this boss from the loot log, per character.
  2. Fight reports - the fight reports of this boss only (same cards as in Fight reports).

#Raid team templates (Clan tab, #/clan)

For big bosses (epic bosses such as Queen Ant, Core, Orfen, Zaken, Baium, and many normal raid bosses) a template says which roles and classes the fight needs, the boss's weak element, and the tactics. The dashboard proposes a team from all your characters (any party). Open the Clan tab and scroll down to Raid team templates.

  1. Boss - pick a boss: ★ = epic boss, then name, level and "weak to " when it has one clear weak element.
  2. Summary - level window (the levels the template wants), weak to (or "no single weak element"), the element to avoid, the boss's defence per element, and how to get in (entry).
  3. Role ×count - tank, healer, buffer, nuker, melee, summoner, archer … with the classes that fit; Job says what that role does in this fight.
  4. Proposed - the best matching characters (class first, then role, then level): name (opens the character page), class, level and party. Orange chips warn: raid curse risk (above the level window) or under-levelled (below it). Missing = places no character could fill.

Under the table: N/M places filled from parties ..., the Tactics list, and the note that in a raid on this boss the bots use the template (nukers prefer skills of the weak element, the tank keeps the minions).

How the proposal is made: only characters that reported in the last 15 minutes count; a matching class scores most, a matching role less, a nuker whose class has strong skills of the weak element gets extra points, and a level inside the window counts too. Templates come from Scripts/data/raid_templates.json (generated by docs/plan/tools/raid_templates.js from the datapack). When that file is missing the box says so.

#How to ...

Find a boss for a party now

  1. Pick the party at the top of the board.
  2. Keep fits on, and pick up now (or sort by respawn).
  3. The card with the gold next badge is what raidhunt would take; any card with a fits chip and an up status works.
  4. Tap the card to check the route, fight area and drops, then press Raid it and confirm.

Let a party hunt bosses by itself

  1. Open Raidhunt at the top, press Raidhunt in that party's row, confirm.
  2. Follow its row (phase, next, done). During each fight the LIVE strip is pinned on top and the red banner appears on every page.
  3. Press Stop in its row to end it.

Correct a route the bots get stuck on

  1. Open Saved routes, filter failed, press Map (or open the boss page and scroll to Route to this boss).
  2. Tap a point near the problem to select it, then tap the map to add a point around the obstacle, or fix x / y / z in the list.
  3. Inside dungeons use Record its walk or + its current position to get the right height.
  4. Press Save & lock. The bots use it from the next trip on.

Write a route from a town

  1. Start: .townname, pick the town, press Town landing = point 1.
  2. Add the points (tap, position, record or paste), finish with Boss spawn = last point.
  3. Save & lock.

Choose where the team fights a boss

  1. Open the boss page, press ✎ Edit in Fight area and follow Raid fight area.

Switch the daily Kamaloka on for a party

  1. Open Daily dungeons under the board, tap Kamaloka: OFF in that leader's box, confirm.

#Notes

  • Every order (Raid, Raid it, Raidhunt, Stop, daily switches, route delete / replace) asks for confirmation; Cancel sends nothing.
  • Route saves, lock / unlock and deletes are written at once (Scripts/data/routes/raid/) and keep the old version in history/. The bots read routes live.
  • The fit, the next badge, the distances and the drop "Who / what" always refer to the chosen party.
  • The board re-reads the boss list every 30 s, the routes every minute, the raidhunt progress every 3 s; countdowns tick every second. The fight reports and daily sections load only while they are open.
  • A boss "found dead" gives only an upper bound for its death time; trust measured respawns over the datapack range once the bots have some.

#Raid fight area (#/edit/raidarea/<boss id>)

Before a raid the team clears the monsters around the boss. Without a fight area it clears every aggressive monster near the boss, which can be a large area. A fight area lets you choose exactly where the team fights.

For every raid boss you can draw where the team fights it, what is cleared before the pull and where the team waits. The area belongs to the boss (its npc id), so every party that raids that boss uses it.

#Where

  • Raid bosses tab (#/raids): a boss with an area shows a green area set badge next to its name.
  • Boss page (#/raid/<id>): section Fight area with ✎ Edit fight area and a one-line summary (points, own clear outline or "fight area + margin", stage set or automatic).

The button opens the full-screen shape editor (the same editor as rooms / zones / spots, see Shape editor).

#The three things you set

What On the map What the bots do with it
Fight area orange polygon The tank pulls the boss into it after taking aggro and keeps it there (boss walks out: the tank walks back in, the boss follows him). Casters and healers stand inside it, at its edge facing the boss when their normal spacing spot is outside.
Clear area yellow; dashed outline = your own, soft yellow band = automatic (fight area + margin) Before the pull the leader kills only monsters inside it: every aggressive one, passive ones only inside the fight area or on the way in from the stage (or all passive ones with "also kill passive"). Monsters that hit us are always killed.
Stage blue flag (faded = automatic) The team walks there first and waits there during the clear and the countdown. Must be within ~3400 of the boss (the leader must see it).

No area for a boss = the defaults: only aggressive monsters within 1200 of the boss (was 2000 and every monster) or on the way in, passive ones only right at the boss; the team waits ~1500 away on the way in and fights where the boss stands.

#How to use

  1. ✎ Edit fight area on the boss page. A boss without an area starts as a 900 circle around its spawn (not saved yet).
  2. ◯ Circle + the number next to it: replace the shape you are editing with a circle of that radius around the boss (quick start).
  3. Shape it: drag a point, tap the small + on an edge for a new point, double-tap / hold a point to delete it, ✥ Move shape moves the whole area (the boss spawn stays). Pinch / wheel = zoom, drag the empty map = pan. ↶ ↷ undo / redo.
  4. ⚔ Fight area / ▢ Clear area switch which outline you edit. The first time you open Clear area it starts as the fight area
    • margin; just looking and going back keeps it automatic. auto clear throws your own clear outline away (fight area + margin again).
  5. ⚑ Stage: drag the blue flag to where the team should wait. The button switches between Stage: auto and Stage: set.
  6. ☰: clear margin (used without an own clear outline), also kill passive monsters inside the clear area, stage x / y / z, on / off, notes, Remove this fight area (back to the defaults).
  7. Save (Ctrl+S): asks once with a summary (points, size, how many monsters will be cleared, stage distance).

#What the map shows

  • The boss spawn (purple ♛) with a dashed ring where its minions spawn, and the minion list with their levels (A = aggressive).
  • Monsters from the datapack spawns: bright = will be cleared, faded = left alone; a red ring = aggressive, with its aggro range dashed around it. Colour = level against the boss (grey low, green around, orange a bit above, red far above).
  • The saved route to the boss (white dashed), the landing (blue square), the stage -> boss path (blue dotted).
  • Bottom line: points, size, cleared before the pull: N (aggressive / passive), left alone, stage distance, warnings.

#Checks on Save

Refused: fewer than 3 or more than 200 points, an outline that crosses itself, smaller than 200 x 200, wider than 10000 (fight) / 14000 (clear), a stage more than 3800 from the boss. Saved with a warning: the boss spawn more than 300 outside the fight area (raid bosses walk home when pulled too far - keep the area at or near the spawn), parts of the fight area outside your own clear outline, a stage inside the fight area or more than 3000 from the boss, a fight area wider than 4000. Check walls / ⌖ Snap work like for rooms (geodata).

#In the live raid view

The live map draws the fight area (orange), the clear area (yellow), the stage flag and, during the clear, every monster still to kill inside the clear area (red ring = aggressive). The header shows Raid clearing: N left inside the clear area · K killed and a chip clearing: N left.

#Files and when the bots use it

  • Scripts/data/raid_areas.json { about, areas: { "<npc id>": { boss, fight [[x,y]..], clear [[x,y]..] | null, clearMargin, clearPassive, stage [x,y,z] | null, enabled, notes, manual, edited, updated } } }. Created on the first save; every save first copies the file to Scripts/data/history/raid_areas_<time>.json (last 50 kept); the write is locked + atomic; a stale editor gets "changed on disk" (409). Log: Logs/polyedit.log.
  • Why not the route file routes/raid/<id>.json: the bots rewrite it with route fields only after every successful walk and delete it after two failures, so an area stored there would be lost.
  • swarm.js (Scripts_dev, RAIDAREA block, after the next deploy) re-reads the file when its write time changes (checked at most every 10 s): a change counts from the next raid's clear; positions in a running fight follow within 10 s.
  • Dashboard: GET/POST /api/polyedit?kind=raidarea&id=<boss id>, POST ...&action=reset (remove), GET /api/polyedit?list=raidarea (badges). Needs a dashboard server restart once after the update (Dashboard/polyedit_api.js, Dashboard/raidlive_api.js changed); until then the boss page says so.

#Tests

  • node docs/plan/tools/test_raid_area.js: the clear rule with / without an area (passive vs aggressive, inside / outside, path, attackers), staging, the tank's pull-in plan, pacing and a chase simulation, the members' clamp, raidClearArea run with mocks on a synthetic boss camp, the API on a temp copy (save, history, 409, validation, remove), wiring checks.
  • node docs/plan/tools/mobile_check/raidarea_cdp.mjs [iphone] [desktop]: headless Edge against a sandbox (:8098, temp data, other GETs proxied read-only to :8090): boss page -> editor -> circle -> drag -> stage -> clear layer -> panel -> save -> badge -> live map. Screenshots docs/plan/mobile_check/raidarea_<device>_<n>_<step>.png.

#Kamaloka

The Kamaloka page (#/kamaloka) is where you run the daily Kamaloka instances. It shows every party of swarm.config.json (a party is named after its leader) against all 19 Kamalokas of the game (Halls and Labyrinths of the Abyss, level 23 to 83): which ones each party fits, which are used today, what the daily run will pick next, and where to enter. Each Kamaloka has its own page with the instance map, and a running Kamaloka is pinned at the top with a link to the live view. You can start a run with one tap (Run), and you can let a party leader run its Kamaloka by itself once a day (daily ON).

New to the words? A Kamaloka is a daily instanced dungeon (an instance, a private copy of a dungeon only your party can enter). A Hall is one room with a boss, for up to 6 players, 30 minutes. A Labyrinth is a corridor of rooms with a mini-boss and the Lost Captain as raid boss, for up to 9 players, 45 minutes. You enter at a captain NPC in a town (Gludio, Dion, Heine, Oren, Schuttgart, Rune).

The live view (what you see while a run is going on) has its own chapter: Kamaloka live view.

Contents:

  • The Kamaloka page
  • Today per party
  • Hall team per party
  • The Kamaloka cards
  • Daily Kamaloka ON / OFF
  • One Kamaloka and its map
  • Run history, daily log, how it decides
  • Run and Force run: the confirmation
  • What the leader does after you tap Run
  • How to ...
  • Notes and safety

#The Kamaloka page (#/kamaloka)

Open it with the Kamaloka tab button (the tab row scrolls sideways on a phone). From top to bottom:

  1. Summary line - number of instances and parties, for how many parties the daily run is on, the daily day and the time until the 06:30 reset (counts down).
  2. Party picker - the party the Run buttons on the cards and the "fits" filter are for ("party Aldric (9, lvl 51-52)"). It starts on the main leader's party and is remembered on this device. The Today rows have their own Run button per party.
  3. LIVE block - only while a run is going on (or just ended): Kamaloka, party, phase, alive / total, kills, time, the leader's current step. Watch opens the live view (#/kamaloka/live), Party view the live party page of that leader.
  4. Today per party - one row per party (below).
  5. Search and filters - find by name, level, boss, town or captain; all / fits ; Hall + Labyrinth / Hall / Labyrinth. The filters are remembered on this device.
  6. Kamaloka cards - one per Kamaloka, lowest level first (below).
  7. Run history, Daily log, How the daily run decides - collapsible sections (closed by default; open / closed is remembered on this device).

One column on a phone, two on a tablet, three on a wide screen. No sideways scrolling.

#Today per party

One row per party, with the party's colour on the left.

Part What it shows or does
Name, chars, lvl Leader name, number of characters, lowest-highest level. "N offline" in orange when some members are not reporting.
daily ON / OFF The party's daily switch (see Daily Kamaloka ON / OFF). Asks first.
Next / Would pick What the daily run picks for this party right now - exactly the leader's own rule (whole party first, then the hall team). "Would pick" when the daily switch is OFF. Without a pick it says why: "a Kamaloka needs 2 or more", "no Kamaloka fits 9 at lvl 28", "every Kamaloka that fits is used up today (39)".
Run now Starts the next pick now with this party (same confirmation as the cards). "Force" style when it is used up today.
waits until the whole party is in The daily run only starts when every member is logged in and in the party; it names who is missing.
Today chips Every Kamaloka this party touched today: "Labyrinth 49 - 1 try left", "Hall 53 - locked (#2100)", "Labyrinth 39 - cleared", "cleared (by hand)" for a run started with Run (not in the daily list).
last daily The leader's last daily run (time, Kamaloka, ok / fail, message).
Hall team Who goes into a Hall (max 6) when the party is bigger than 6, and where that comes from: set on this page, the old global list, or automatic. Tap it to change it (see Hall team per party). A party of 6 or fewer says "the whole party".
+ members & levels Opens the member list: name, level, green dot = reporting, grey = offline. Remembered per party on this device.
LIVE Instead of Next while this party runs a Kamaloka.

#Hall team per party

A Hall takes at most 6 characters, a Labyrinth 9. A party of 7, 8 or 9 can still run Halls: its hall team goes in, and the others leave the party for the run, travel to the captain's town (Dion, Heine, Oren, ...) and wait there. Their task line says "waiting in Dion — not in the Hall team (Hall 36)". After the run the leader invites them back and they follow him again.

Every party has its own hall team. Where it comes from, in this order:

  1. Set on this page - the team you saved for this party (stored in swarm.config.json as kamaloka.hallTeams).
  2. The old global list - dailyHallTeam in swarm.config.json (or the built-in default), but only for the party whose leader is in that list.
  3. Automatic - nothing set: for each Hall the leader picks the best 6 himself, from the members inside that Hall's level window: the leader, one tank (the leader when he is one), up to 2 healers (the highest level first), then the strongest damage dealers (level first, then role: destroyers, then doombringers / necromancers / nukers, ...), then anyone left.

Change a party's hall team

  1. In Today per party, tap the party's Hall team line. A box per member opens (name, level, role); the leader is always ticked.
  2. Tick up to 6 (at least 2). The counter shows "n/6 ticked". Your ticks stay while the page refreshes; Undo ticks puts them back.
  3. Tap Save hall team and confirm. The leader reads it within 30 seconds (no deploy, no restart of the bots).
  4. Use automatic removes the saved team again (asks first).

Saving writes swarm.config.json (the old file is kept in Settings/backup/swarm_config_history/, the last 50). If someone else changed the same party's team since your page loaded, the save is refused ("changed meanwhile - reload and try again").

#The Kamaloka cards

Part Meaning
Icon + number The Kamaloka's level.
Hall 53 / Labyrinth 49 + max 6 / max 9 Hall or Labyrinth and its party size. Tap the name (or the card) for its own page.
lvl 48-58 - 30 min - town, captain Level window, time limit, where to enter.
Boss Boss name and level, plus how many runs our bots made here and the last result.
next - (gold) The daily run of that party picks this one now.
cleared HH:MM - (green) Logs/kamaloka.log shows its boss killed since 06:30 (and by which party, when the log can tell).
LIVE A run of this Kamaloka is going on.
Party chips One per party: the ones it fits first, the others dimmed with the reason. Today's state is added for the ones that fit.
Run / Force run For the party in the picker; only when that party fits. Force run = used up today; the server may still refuse.
Map Opens the Kamaloka's page.

Party chip (the leader's own rule, Dashboard/kamalogic.js = swarm.js dailyDue):

Chip Meaning
fits (green) Every level is inside the window and the whole party fits in (up to 6 for a Hall, 9 for a Labyrinth).
fits — hall team: A, B, C, D, E, F (blue) A Hall for a party bigger than 6: these 6 (the party's hall team) go in, the others wait in the captain's town.
too low / too high / levels too spread (orange) Levels outside the window (names given when only some are).
too many (red) More characters than the instance takes and the party's saved hall team does not work (a name not in the party, more than 6, the leader missing) - the reason is in the tooltip.
too few (red) Fewer than 2 (a solo character).
levels unknown (grey) The leader has not reported a level yet.

Today (a new day starts at 06:30 local time, the same time the game resets the lock): 2 / 1 try left (open), locked (#2100), cleared, no entry today (could not enter twice), no tries left (2 starts today), done today (any other reason). It comes from the leader's daily list Logs/daily_<leader>.json (written by daily runs only).

#Daily Kamaloka ON / OFF

The daily ON / OFF button in a party's Today row switches the daily Kamaloka for that whole party. Every party has one (before 2026-10-09 only the two dailyLeaders had it; the server accepts every party leader once it runs the new code). It asks first: "Daily Kamaloka for the WHOLE party ... -> ON. The leader takes the party into by itself (once per day) when it is free." Switching OFF says "Stops future runs; a run already started is not aborted." The dashboard writes Logs/daily_enabled.json; the bots read it live.

What ON does. Once a minute the party leader checks whether a Kamaloka is due:

  1. The whole team must be in his party, and he must be free: not paused by !stop, not in a raid boss fight, not on a supply run or other team trip.
  2. He picks the highest Kamaloka that every member fits (levels and party size) and that is not done today and was tried fewer than 2 times today.
  3. Only if none fits the whole party: when the party is bigger than 6, the highest Hall its hall team fits (the saved one, or the automatic pick for that Hall).
  4. Raid hunting or leveling steps aside after the current fight, the run starts, and afterwards the team goes back to what it did before.
  5. Every started run counts as a try. The Kamaloka is marked done for the day when its boss died, when the server answered "may not re-enter" (#2100), or when it could not enter on the second try. A wipe is not "done": the server only locks a Kamaloka when its boss dies.

The Next on the page is computed with exactly this rule (it used to differ: the old page counted Halls first and ignored the tries).

#One Kamaloka and its map (#/kamaloka/<id>)

Tap a card (or its name / Map) to open its page, for example #/kamaloka/kamaloka-39. ‹ All Kamaloka goes back.

  1. Header - level, short and full name, LIVE / cleared badges.
  2. Facts - level window, party size, time limit, captain and town, boss, our runs (count, last one, result), rewards.
  3. Every party - one row per party: its fit (with the reason), today's state for the ones that fit or used it, next when its daily run picks this one, and its own Run / Force run button.
  4. Map - the instance on the game's own map art (entry, exit, room spawns, monsters our runs saw, mini-boss, boss, last path) with the legend, the room notes and the mini-boss. The map is a picture: scrolling over it scrolls the page.
  5. Our results here - the last results of this Kamaloka, with the party when known.

Map symbols

Symbol Meaning
Green dot "Entry" Where you arrive inside.
Blue dot "Exit" The exit point (Labyrinths).
Orange dots + "Room 1", "Room 2" Monster spawn points of each room, from the server's data files.
Purple dot Mini-boss (Labyrinths: the Lost Warden).
Red dot Boss, with name and level.
Pale red dots Monsters our bots saw inside, learned run by run (Logs/kamaloka_map.json).
Dashed gold line The leader's path in the last run.

A Hall has no monster positions in the data files; they appear after the first run.

#Run history, daily log, how it decides

  • Run history - every Kamaloka run of all parties from Logs/kamaloka.log, newest first: time, Kamaloka, party (when daily.log or the live file tells), result (cleared, wiped, timeout).
  • Daily log - the leaders' daily runs from Logs/daily.log: time, party, Kamaloka, ok / fail and the message.
  • How the daily run decides - the rule above in short, plus the current hall team and where it comes from (swarm.config.json dailyHallTeam, else the swarm.js default).

#Run and Force run: the confirmation

Every Run, Run now and Force run button asks before anything is sent. The text tells you which party gets the order, how many characters, the command, and which characters are busy and will drop what they do.

  1. Run confirmation - "Send to the WHOLE party Aldric (9 characters): Kamaloka now: ... They stop what they do, travel, enter and clear it. Only the hall team (...) goes in: 3 wait in town and rejoin after. (!mission kamaloka 53)".

  1. Force run confirmation - starts with "FORCE Kamaloka", repeats what the Today column says and why ("locked today" and the server message), and warns "the game server may still refuse at the captain".

OK sends !mission kamaloka <level> (for example !mission kamaloka 49) to the party leader through the dashboard's command line; the message line under the header confirms it. Cancel sends nothing. The same order is the Kamaloka command in the command center (pick a Kamaloka, or leave it empty and the leader takes the highest one the whole party fits). !mission stop aborts a running mission.

#What the leader does after you tap Run

The order goes to the party leader; the members follow him. This is the same run the daily switch starts.

  1. Free the team. Raid hunting and leveling stop. A raid boss fight is never left: the order waits until it is over (at most 30 minutes, then it is dropped).
  2. Hall team. If the party is bigger than the instance (a Hall with 7-9), the characters outside the party's hall team leave the party, use .townname to the captain's town and wait there. They are invited back after the run. If no hall team fits (for example a saved name left the party), the leader says why in party chat and does not start.
  3. Travel. The team uses the .townname command to the captain's town, gathers, and walks to the captain together.
  4. Gather at the captain. The leader waits (up to 2 minutes) until every teammate reports itself within 900 of him. If someone is missing he does not enter ("team not with the leader - not entered"). He never goes in alone.
  5. Enter. He talks to the captain and clicks the entry for this level. If the server refuses, the run ends with the server's reason.
  6. Inside. Everyone must show up next to him within 20 seconds. If the server only took him in (this happens when his old instance still exists), he tells the others to enter by themselves and waits 60 seconds; if they still do not come, he leaves at once.
  7. Rebuff. The instance removes all buffs, so everyone takes the Community Board buffs again.
  8. Fight. The team holds a spot (the anchor). The tank pulls one group at a time with Aggression and brings it back, every damage dealer hits the leader's focus target, casters cast from range, healers stay back and only heal. Between rooms the team rests, raises the dead and rebuffs, then moves on together.
  9. Loot and home. When the boss is dead and the room is empty the result is "cleared"; everybody dead = "wiped"; time limit = "timeout". The team collects loot for 20 seconds, the result goes to Logs/kamaloka.log, the team goes back to town and resumes what it did before.

From the moment the leader starts, the page pins the run at the top; Watch opens the live view.

#How to ...

Run a Kamaloka now

  1. Open the Kamaloka page.
  2. Either tap Run now in the party's Today row (its next pick), or pick the party in the picker, find a card whose chip for that party says fits / hall team, and tap Run (or open the card and use the party's button under Every party).
  3. Read the confirmation and tap OK.
  4. Watch the LIVE block that appears at the top; Watch opens the live view.

Let a party do its Kamaloka by itself every day

  1. Open the Kamaloka page.
  2. Tap daily OFF in that party's Today row, read the confirmation, tap OK. It turns green and says ON.
  3. The leader starts its Next within a minute or two once the whole team is in the party and free.

Try again a Kamaloka that looks used today

  1. Tap Force run on its card (party picker = that party) or on its page.
  2. Read why it looks used (the confirmation repeats the reason) and tap OK. If the game server still says "may not re-enter", the live view ends with that message.

See why a party does not fit Look at that party's chip on the card (dimmed = does not fit, with the reason), or open the Kamaloka: Every party spells it out ("too low (lvl 28, needs 34)", "hall team too low: ...", "too many (8 > 6) - hall team: not in the party: ...").

Stop a running Kamaloka Send !mission stop (or !stop) to the party leader, for example from the command center. The live view closes within about 15 seconds with the result "stopped".

#Notes and safety

  • Confirmation: Run, Run now, Force run and the daily switch all ask first. Filters, the party picker, opening sections and tapping a card send nothing.
  • Who gets the order: always the whole party of that leader. Busy characters are named in the confirmation; a Hall run names the hall team and how many wait in town.
  • Halls for big parties: every party bigger than 6 runs Halls with its own hall team (saved on this page, the old global list for its own party, or automatic). Two parties can run Halls at the same time; each leader benches only his own party.
  • Files: daily switch Logs/daily_enabled.json (read live by the leaders); daily progress Logs/daily_<leader>.json and Logs/daily.log; results Logs/kamaloka.log; learned monster spots and last path Logs/kamaloka_map.json; live run Logs/kamaloka_live.json. Instance layouts: Dashboard/data/kamaloka_layout.json; the Kamaloka list: Scripts/data/dungeons_h5.json.
  • Which parties appear: every party of swarm.config.json (accounts[].party). Hall teams: kamaloka.hallTeams per party leader, else dailyHallTeam / the swarm.js default for its own party, else automatic.
  • The server decides: the page only knows what the bots wrote down. A Kamaloka shown as open can still be refused at the captain (on L2Toggle one Hall kill usually locks the other Kamalokas for the day too, #2100).
  • Refresh: the page reloads every 20 seconds (and right after an order or a switch); the LIVE block every second.
  • Code: page Dashboard/kamapage.js + .css, data /api/kamapage (Dashboard/kamapage_api.js), the fit / next rule Dashboard/kamalogic.js (unit test docs/plan/tools/test_kamalogic.js, page test docs/plan/tools/test_kamapage_ui.js).

#Fortresses, castles and sieges

Routes: #/forts, #/forts/<id>, #/castles, #/castles/<id> and the live view #/siege/live (see Siege live view).

These two tabs are where you look up every fortress and castle, check whether your clan may attack it, plan a siege with several parties, and start it. The bots then run the whole siege by themselves: regroup in Giran, travel, regroup outside, wait for the start, kill the objectives, and raise the flag or engrave the artifact.

Read this first. The siege code is built but not tested on a live server. The rules and numbers come from the L2J High Five datapack (a "datapack" is the server's game data; see the glossary). Your server may use other clan levels, fees, start times or NPC levels. A fortress siege needs clan level 4, a castle siege clan level 5 (the values in Scripts/data/fortresses.json and castles.json). Fortress commanders are level 78.

Both tabs have the same layout, from top to bottom:

  1. the title bar with Live view and ↻ (reload),
  2. a compact live box (only while a siege runs),
  3. the clan eligibility bar,
  4. the world map (left) and the detail panel of the selected target (right; below the map on a phone),
  5. Plan a siege (the planner form) and its warnings,
  6. Planned sieges (saved plans),
  7. All fortresses / All castles (table),
  8. Rules + sources.

The page reloads its data every 15 seconds while it is open, and the countdowns in the plan list every 30 seconds.

#Fortresses tab (#/forts)

Use this tab to choose a fortress and plan a fortress siege. #/forts/<id> opens it with that fortress selected (for example #/forts/104 = Valley Fortress). Without an id, the page selects the fortress of the next planned siege, or the first one.

  1. Live view - opens the siege live view (#/siege/live).
  2. ↻ - reads the fortress, castle, plan and clan data again right now.
  3. Clan eligibility bar - your clan, its level, the clan leader (and "offline" when he is not reporting), the clan level a fortress siege needs, and whether you qualify. Green frame = you qualify; red frame and red text = "we cannot register yet (level X/4)". It also counts how many of your characters are in the clan and how many sieges are planned.
  4. World map - all 21 fortresses and all 9 castles on the game map. Tap a marker to select it.
  5. Legend - what the markers mean (below).
  6. Detail panel - everything about the selected fortress (see Fortress detail panel).

#The world map

  1. Selected fortress - a white ring. A red ⚑ next to a marker means a siege is planned there.
  2. Diamonds - fortresses. Gold = territory fortress, blue = border fortress. A larger diamond is a large fortress.
  3. Red boxes with a crown - castles. On the Fortresses tab they are dimmed; tapping one switches to the Castles tab. Thin dashed lines join each castle to its fortresses.
  4. Coloured dots - where each party leader is right now (one colour per party, the same colours as in the planner).

A pulsing red ring marks the target of a siege that is running now.

#Fortress detail panel

  1. Chips - Territory or Border fortress, Small or Large, the castle it belongs to (tap it to open that castle), the owner, and "siege planned " when a plan exists. "owner unknown" means no bot has seen a "... is victorious" system message for this fortress yet; the bots write the owner to Logs/siege_owners.json whenever they see one.
  2. Position block - map coordinates and nearest town, the nearest teleport landing (and which town's gatekeeper sends you there, and how far it is), and the regroup point: a safe spot outside the siege zone where the parties gather before the start (attackers inside the zone are sent to town when the siege starts).
  3. Close-up map - the area around the fortress on the game map (see Close-up map).
  4. Close-up legend.
  5. Can we siege it? - a checklist. Green ✓ = done, red ✗ = missing, • = a note:
    • the clan exists,
    • the clan level is high enough,
    • the clan leader is online (only he can register),
    • where to register (the fortress's Suspicious Merchant, with its position) and the fee; after a registration it shows "done ()" from Logs/siege_registrations.json,
    • a reminder that only members of a registered clan can hurt the fortress NPCs.
  6. Register (clan leader ) - sends !siegereg fort <name> to the clan leader, after a confirmation (below). Greyed out while the clan level is too low, with "clan level 4 needed — now X" next to it.
  7. Objectives - what has to happen, in order: kill every commander (each holds a barracks; listed with NPC id, level and position), then the command center door opens, pick up a Combat Flag inside, carry it to the flag pole and raise it.
  8. Skills for the owning clan - the residence skills the owner gets, with icon, id, level and effect. Below it: Functions (teleport, HP/MP regeneration ...), Rewards (Blood Oath, Knight's Epaulette, supply boxes ...) and the Dungeon (the fortress dungeon quest: level, time, re-entry, bosses per stage, reward).
  9. NPCs (n) - a fold-out list of every NPC of the fortress: role, name, title, NPC id and position.
  10. Defenders (n) - a fold-out count of the defending guards by name.

  1. NPCs - role, name, NPC id, position.
  2. Defenders - every guard type with its count (for example "Guard ×88").

#Close-up map

Marker Meaning
Red circle C1, C2 ... a commander (with its role: Archer, Guard, Support, General)
Yellow ⚑ a Combat Flag spawn point (inside the command center)
Yellow ring "flag pole" where the flag is raised
Blue bar a gate or door; the first command-center door is labelled "command center"
Grey dot an NPC (merchants, envoys, managers are named). Hover or long-press for name, title, role and NPC id
Blue square "landing: ..." the nearest teleport landing (only when it is on this map piece)
Green ✚ "regroup / staging" the regroup point (the plan's own point while you edit a plan)
"n km across" the scale

On the Castles tab the close-up also shows the Holy Artifact (yellow circle), Control Towers (purple triangles) and Flame Towers (orange triangles).

#Registering the clan

Register asks first: "Send to only: travels to and registers the clan for its siege ... (!siegereg fort )". Press OK to send it. The clan leader then:

  1. checks the clan level again (too low = it stops and writes "refused here: clan level 4 needed ..."),
  2. travels to the fortress's Suspicious Merchant (town first, then the gatekeeper, then a walk),
  3. clicks through the merchant's pages to the register link. The first clan to register pays 250,000 adena (L2J value). The merchant only stands there while the fortress can be registered for.

The result is written to Logs/siege_registrations.json and shown in the checklist. The NPC pages are saved as Logs/siegereg_*.html. In L2J a fortress siege starts 60 minutes after the first clan registers, so register first, then plan.

While the clan level is too low the button is greyed out:

  1. Red ✗ - the check that fails.
  2. Register - greyed out, with the reason next to it.

#Plan a siege

The form below the map plans a siege for the selected target. Its title says which one ("for Valley Fortress"). A plan is saved to Scripts/data/siege_plans.json, which the bots read live.

  1. Siege time - date and time of the siege start, in this device's time zone. The default is two hours from now, rounded down to the full hour.
  2. Regroup in Giran (minutes before) - 5 to 240 (default 30). At "siege time minus this", the bots stop what they are doing and start.
  3. Time zone line - the time zone used and the exact time the regroup starts. It updates while you type.
  4. Parties table - one row per party: party name (in its map colour, plus a "clan leader" chip for the clan leader's party), online/size, level range and average, tanks/healers/damage dealers, how many are in the clan, and whether the leader has the Command Channel right ("CC right").
  5. Checkbox - tick the parties that take part. By default the two biggest parties (3+ characters) are ticked.
  6. Command Channel leader (main leader) - one of the ticked party leaders. He starts the plan, waits for the other parties, opens the Command Channel (a channel joining several parties; see the glossary) and writes the live view. Leaders without the right are marked "(no CC right yet)".
  7. Flag carrier (fortress) - who carries the Combat Flag. Healers are never offered. The default is the clan leader when his party is ticked, otherwise the sturdiest member (tank first, then destroyers ...).
  8. Backup carrier - a second choice.
  9. Who kills which commander - one select per commander: a party or "any party". The default spreads the commanders over the ticked parties.
  10. Set on the map - pick your own regroup point (see below). The line before it shows the current point and whether it is the default ("safe spot between the landing and the walls") or "set by you".
  11. Notes - free text (up to 500 characters), shown in the plan list.
  12. Save plan - saves the plan (no confirmation). It becomes Save changes when you edit a saved plan, and New plan appears next to it.

For a castle the flag fields are replaced by Engraves the artifact (must be the clan leader) and there is no commander list (see Castles tab).

Ticking or unticking a party redraws the form and picks new defaults for carrier, backup, commanders and CC leader when the old choice is no longer in a ticked party. Your own choices stay when they are still valid.

#Warnings

Under the form a box counts the chosen parties and characters and lists every problem it finds. Red = it will not work, orange = it may not work, green = a confirmation. It updates while you change the form.

  1. Count - "2 parties · 18 characters" ("no problems found" when the list is empty).
  2. Red - for example "choose at least one party", "clan level 4 needed to register ...", "only the clan leader can engrave the Holy Artifact".
  3. Orange - for example characters who are not in the clan (only members of a registered clan can hurt the NPCs), characters offline now, a CC leader without the Command Channel right, no flag carrier, a carrier who is not the clan leader (in L2J High Five only the clan leader can raise the flag), a siege time in the past ("the leader would start at once"), a party far below the commanders' level, a party without a healer.

When the clan leader carries the flag the box says so in green: the flag slows him to 20 % and every party escorts him; the 3-minute Flag Display cast must not be interrupted.

  1. Ticked rows are highlighted.
  2. clan leader chip.
  3. Flag carrier - switched to the clan leader as soon as his party is ticked.
  4. Who kills which commander - spread over the ticked parties (round-robin).
  5. Warnings box.

#Setting your own regroup point

  1. After Set on the map the button reads "Tap the close-up map…" and the close-up map gets a green frame. Tap the spot. Tap the button again to cancel.

  1. set by you - the new point (its height is taken from the default point).
  2. Set on the map - pick again.
  3. Default - back to the point from the data.

Choose a spot outside the siege zone; attackers inside the zone at the start are teleported to town.

#How to plan a fortress siege

  1. Register the clan first (see Registering the clan); the siege time follows from the registration.
  2. Tap the fortress on the map (or its row in the table).
  3. Set Siege time and Regroup in Giran.
  4. Tick the parties. Tick the clan leader's party too, so he can carry the flag.
  5. Check the CC leader, flag carrier, backup carrier and the commander list.
  6. Optional: set your own regroup point and write a note.
  7. Read the warnings, fix the red ones.
  8. Press Save plan. The status line at the bottom says "siege plans saved", and the plan appears under Planned sieges.

At regroup time the plan's main leader starts it by himself (he checks the plan file every 30 seconds). He waits if a raid or Kamaloka is running and starts after it.

#Planned sieges

Every saved plan of this kind (fortress or castle), sorted by time.

  1. Status chip - planned, done, cancelled, or LIVE while the bots run it.
  2. Countdown - "in 2h 40m" (planned plans only). Below the title: the regroup time, the parties in their colours, the CC leader, the flag carrier or engraver, and your notes.
  3. Bots - what the main leader reported in Logs/siege_runs.json: starting, started or done, with the result (for example "WON", "wiped", "time is up", "could not reach the target") and the time.
  4. Edit - loads the plan into the form above (and switches to the right tab).
  5. Start now - sends !siege plan <id> to the plan's main party, after a confirmation. The siege starts at once (the regroup included); a planned start time still in the future is kept as the start time.
  6. Cancel - sets the plan to cancelled after a confirmation. The bots ignore cancelled plans.
  7. Plan again - (shown instead of Cancel on a cancelled or done plan) sets it back to planned, no confirmation.
  8. Delete - removes the plan from the file after a confirmation.

Watch live › appears on the plan that is running now.

Every change to the plan file first copies the old file to Settings/backup/siege_plans_<time>.json.

  1. Save changes - saves over the same plan.
  2. New plan - empties the form for a new plan of the same target.
  3. All values of the plan (time, parties, roles, commanders, regroup point, notes) are in the form.

The confirmations:

Start now uses the standard order confirmation ("Send to the WHOLE party (n characters): ... Busy right now and will change orders: ..."). Cancel and Delete ask "Cancel/Delete the siege plan for ?".

#All fortresses table

  1. Selected row - tap any row to select that fortress (same as tapping the map).
  2. Skills - icons of the owner's skills; hover for name and effect.
  3. Owner - the clan seen winning it last ("?" = unknown).
  4. Can register - "yes" or "clan lvl 4".

Other columns: name, type and size, castle, number of commanders. On a phone the table scrolls sideways.

#Rules + sources

  1. Rules - the main values from the data file: minimum clan level, registration fee, siege length, count-down, maximum attacker clans, the Combat Flag item ...
  2. All config values (L2J defaults) - a fold-out with every other config value.
  3. Sources - where the research is (docs/plan/sieges_research.md), the data date, and the warning that the server may differ.

The Notes list (on the Castles tab) explains how the data was made (castle NPC roles, control and flame towers, siege schedule ...).

#Castles tab (#/castles)

The same page for the 9 castles. #/castles/<id> selects a castle (1 Gludio, 2 Dion, 3 Giran, 4 Oren, 5 Aden, 6 Innadril, 7 Goddard, 8 Rune, 9 Schuttgart).

  1. Eligibility bar - the same as on the Fortresses tab, for clan level 5.
  2. Selected castle - castles are bright here, fortresses dimmed and smaller.
  3. Dashed lines - from each castle to its fortresses.
  4. Detail panel.

  1. Chips - territory, town, owner, planned siege.
  2. Position block - position, nearest landing, regroup point, its fortresses (tap one to open it), the default tax and the lord items (crown and circlet with icons and item ids).
  3. Close-up - gates and walls, Control Towers, Flame Towers, the Holy Artifact.
  4. Can we siege it? - like the fortress checklist; registration is at the castle's Messenger or Chamberlain, and every fighter must be in a registered clan (attacker side). Register sends !siegereg castle <name>; the clan leader talks to the Messenger and sends the "join siege" request. Registration closes 24 hours before the siege (L2J).
  5. Objectives - break the outer and inner gates, destroy the Control Towers (they let defenders respawn; Flame Towers are traps), protect the clan leader while he engraves the Holy Artifact.
  6. Skills for the owning clan.
  7. Territory skills.
  8. Dungeon - the castle dungeon quest.

Below them: Rewards (crown and circlets, tax, castle functions, its fortresses' contracts, the dungeon) and the NPC list.

#Plan a castle siege

  1. Engraves the artifact (must be the clan leader) - the list holds the members of the ticked parties; the default is the clan leader, so tick his party. Any other choice gives a red warning.
  2. Command Channel leader.
  3. Save plan.

All other fields work as for a fortress.

  1. The plan line shows the regroup time, parties, CC leader, engraver and notes.

  1. Fortresses - the castle's fortresses.
  2. Lord items - crown and circlet icons.
  3. Owner.

#What the bots do in a siege

Every ticked party leader runs the siege for his own party; members follow and assist as always. The main (CC) leader also waits for the others, opens the Command Channel and writes the live view.

  1. Regroup in Giran - the normal Giran regroup.
  2. Travel - town first, then the gatekeeper landing nearest the regroup point, then the team walks there.
  3. Regroup outside - each leader waits for his team. The main leader waits up to 15 minutes for every party, invites the other leaders into the Command Channel (if he has the right) and gives GO.
  4. Wait for the start - until the server's start message or the planned time; the party rebuffs (!buff) 4 minutes before.
  5. Siege - fortress: break the nearest closed outer gate, each party kills its commander (focus fire), all commanders must die within 10 minutes of the first or they come back; then the command center opens and the carrier picks up the Combat Flag (item 9819), walks to the flag pole and casts Flag Display (skill 3318, 3 minutes) while every party escorts him. Castle: gates, then Control Towers, then the clan leader casts Seal of Ruler (skill 246) on the Holy Artifact.
  6. End - a win, the siege-end message, the main party dead for 60 seconds, the siege time over, or !siege stop. Everyone stops and waits for the next order, like after a raid.

Rules: nobody escapes while the siege runs; healers raise the dead and Scrolls of Resurrection are allowed (a siege is not a raid). Enemy players are only shown on the live view; the bots do not attack them.

Not built yet: headquarters (Build Headquarters), the large-fortress control room, ballista bombs, the contract choice after a win. Gate and flag-pole ids come from server packets read during the siege; this part is untested.

#Commands

All of these are also in the command center (category "clan") and the command reference.

Command Sent to What it does
!siege plan <id> the plan's main party start a saved plan now (the Start now button)
!siege fort <name> / !siege castle <name> a party quick siege with this party only, starting now
!siege stop a party, or all stop the running siege (all parties)
!siegereg fort <name> / !siegereg castle <name> the clan leader register the clan (the Register button)

#Files

File What
Scripts/data/fortresses.json, castles.json the data shown on these tabs (made by docs/plan/tools/sieges_data.js)
Scripts/data/siege_plans.json the plans (read live by the bots)
Logs/siege_live.json the live view (written by the main leader every 2 seconds)
Logs/siege_runs.json plan id -> what the bots did with it
Logs/siege_registrations.json, Logs/siegereg_*.html registration results and NPC pages
Logs/siege_owners.json the owner of each fortress / castle, as last seen
Logs/siege.log every siege event

#Notes and safety

  • Register, Start now, Cancel and Delete ask for confirmation. Save plan, Plan again, Edit, Set on the map and Default do not.
  • Saving or changing a plan is safe: nothing happens in the game until the regroup time (or Start now).
  • A saved plan will start by itself at regroup time. Cancel or delete plans you no longer want.
  • Times are stored in UTC and shown in the time zone of the device you are using.

#Crystals (soul crystals)

Route: #/crystals

A soul crystal adds a special ability (SA, for example Focus, Acumen or Health) to a weapon. You level a crystal by using it on suitable monsters until it reaches the stage the weapon needs, then a blacksmith puts it into the weapon. (See "soul crystal" and "special ability" in the glossary.)

The bots do the leveling by themselves. This tab shows, per party and per character:

  • which crystal it is working on now and why (the ability its next weapon grade needs),
  • what is in its bag, how many crystals it has finished and stored, and how its tries went,
  • and it lets you change the plan: a party may stop leveling, a party may farm extra crystals for the stock, and you can set a character's target by hand.

How it works in the game (from the bots' code):

  • Crystals start at level 40 (the lowest crystal monsters are level 40). Younger characters show "crystals from lvl 40".
  • !soul get: the leader takes the team to Gideon in Oren, and everyone without a crystal fetches one (free, quest 350).
  • While a monster that accepts the crystal's stage is the target and is at 50 % HP or less, the character uses the crystal on it once (26 MP). Whoever lands the killing blow gets the try.
  • Only one crystal may be in the bag. Two crystals = "resonation": no tries at all.
  • A crystal that reached its target stage is READY. !soul store takes the team to the Giran warehouse and every character stores its finished crystals (the clan warehouse when in a clan, otherwise its own); !soul get fetches the next one.
  • Raid bosses (stage 10 and up) need no crystal use: the party gets the try when the boss dies.

The targets come from the special abilities table (Scripts/data/soul_sa.txt) and the role of each character: destroyers Focus (plus a Health weapon for the HP swap before Frenzy), casters and healers Acumen, tanks Health, daggers Focus, and so on. The dashboard writes the result to Scripts/data/soul_targets.json every minute; the bots read it live. The page refreshes every 8 seconds.

#Overview

  1. Intro - the level rule and where crystals come from. The line under it explains "no report yet" (a character that has not written Logs/soul_<name>.json yet).
  2. Party box - one box per party ("Not in a party" for characters without one).
  3. levels crystals - on/off for the whole party. Off = the party's characters do not use crystals (and a finished crystal is stored). This is a plan change: press Save afterwards.
  4. Get crystals - sends !soul get to the party (confirmation first).
  5. Store finished - sends !soul store to the party (confirmation first).
  6. Status in party chat - sends !soul: everyone writes its crystals and tries into party chat (confirmation first).
  7. Extra for the stock - fold-out list of extra crystals this party farms after its own targets (see below). The number is how many are listed. It opens by itself when the list is not empty.
  8. Save - saves the plan (Scripts/data/soul_plan.json). It turns gold and reads "Save (unsaved changes)" when you have changed something.

#The party table

Columns: Character (tap for its character page), Lvl, Role, In bag, Working towards, Then, Stored, Tries, edit. Characters below level 40 are faded.

  1. READY — store it - the crystal in the bag reached its target stage. Order Store finished.
  2. resonation - more than one crystal in the bag: no tries happen until one is gone.
  3. by hand - the target was set on this page (an override), not computed.
  4. Working towards - the ability, crystal colour and stage, the weapon, and why (for example "Focus · red 8 · Berserker Blade — main weapon C: 2h sword + Focus"). "nothing" = no target; "team stock" = the party's stock list.
  5. Then - the later targets, in order (the next weapon grades).
  6. Stored - how many finished crystals this character has stored; hover for colour, stage, time and place.
  7. Tries - successes ✓ and failures ✗ since the bot started; hover for the details (success, not absorbed, broke, resonation, refused because the monster level is too low).
  8. edit - opens the target editor row for this character.

In bag shows each crystal as a chip (colour icon, colour, stage, ×count), "none", or "no report yet", plus "levelling off" when the party does not level, and how old the report is.

#Changing a character's target

  1. Ability - every special ability in the table.
  2. Weapon - every weapon that has this ability, with grade, type, colour and stage, sorted by grade and stage.
  3. Use this target - saves this weapon's crystal as the character's only target (after a confirmation).
  4. Reset to automatic - (only for a target set by hand) removes the override, after a confirmation.

The confirmation names the change ("Cassius: Focus · red 8 · Berserker Blade") and says that other unsaved plan changes on the page are saved too, and that the bots read the plan live (no deploy). Cancel undoes the change.

#How to set a target by hand

  1. Tap edit on the character's row.
  2. Choose the ability, then the weapon.
  3. Tap Use this target and confirm.
  4. The row shows by hand; within about a minute the bot levels the new colour.

#Extra crystals for the stock

A character that has finished all its own targets levels the first crystal of its party's stock list next.

  1. Colour - red, green or blue.
  2. Stage - 1 to 16.
  3. Note - free text.
  4. ✕ - removes the row.
  5. + Add a crystal - adds a row (red, stage 10).
  6. Save - saves the plan.

Changes here are not saved until you press Save:

  1. unsaved plan changes - next to the title.
  2. Save (unsaved changes) - highlighted.

Save asks "Save the soul crystal plan? Party : levels crystals ON/OFF, n extra crystal(s) for the stock ... The bots read it live (no deploy)". On OK the server copies the old plan to Settings/backup/soul_plan_<time>.json, writes the new one and recomputes every target.

The order buttons use the normal order confirmation:

#Stock

  1. Stored crystals - every finished crystal stored by anyone, counted by colour and stage.
  2. Wanted for the stock - the stock lists of all parties.

#Special abilities table

  1. Filter - type a weapon, ability, grade or type ("acumen", "C blunt", "Focus" ...).
  2. Table - grouped by grade and weapon type: weapon, crystal stage, and the ability a red, green or blue crystal gives.

The table is Scripts/data/soul_sa.txt (one line per weapon: grade|type|name|stage|red|green|blue).

#soul.log

The last 80 lines of Logs/soul.log, newest first: crystals fetched ("got red stage 0"), every try result ("SUCCESS - next stage | now red stage 5", "not absorbed", "BROKE", "resonation") and stores.

#Commands

Command Sent to What
!soul get a party fetch crystals from Gideon in Oren (level 40+)
!soul store a party store finished crystals in the Giran warehouse
!soul a party everyone reports its crystals in party chat
!soul on / !soul off a party crystal use on/off until the next script reload (command center only)

#Notes

  • levels crystals, the stock list and the target editor change Scripts/data/soul_plan.json; all saves ask for confirmation.
  • The three order buttons ask for confirmation.
  • Colour preferences per character can also come from Scripts/data/soul_prefs.json (used only when a character has no target).

#Clan

Route: #/clan

Everything about your clan in one place: the clan leader, the clan level and what the next level needs, the clan level quests (Blood Mark, Q501, Q503) step by step, the clan warehouse, the roster, the reputation quests and their raid bosses, clan skills, the clan level table, new accounts for the Academy, Seven Signs for every character, a clan event (several parties on an epic boss with a Command Channel) and raid team templates.

The data comes from the clan leader's bot (Logs/clan_state.json, written every 30 seconds), from every bot's own clan report (each asks the server for the clan member list every 10 minutes), from Scripts/data/clan_quests.json and clan_data.json (L2J High Five values). The page refreshes every 4 seconds. The clan leader is the leader in Scripts/data/clan_quests.json (clan.leader), else clanLeader in swarm.config.json (in the demo: Quill).

#Overview

  1. Clan tabs - one button per clan the bots are in: clan name, level and leader ("(not ours)" when the leader is not one of your characters). Before your clan exists there is one "(planned)" tab for it. Tap a tab to switch; the configured clan shows the full page below, any other clan a short page (see Another clan).
  2. Look in the clan warehouse now - the clan leader opens the clan warehouse and reports what is in it (!clanwh, confirmation first).
  3. Clan leader card.
  4. Clan box.
  5. Clan level & reputation.

The sections below the cards, in order: Clan level quests, Clan roster, Clan quests, Clan raid bosses, Clan skills, Clan levels, New accounts (Academy), Seven Signs, Clan event, Raid team templates.

#Leader, clan, level, warehouse and help boxes

  1. Clan leader card - name (tap for his character page), class, level, a "dead" chip when dead, HP and MP bars, his current task, where he is, his SP and when he last reported.
  2. Adena - his adena. Rich parties top him up to 12,000,000 adena in Giran, because clan level-ups cost adena.
  3. Clan name - read-only ("fixed (the clan exists)") once the clan exists. See Founding the clan.
  4. Next level table - what the next clan level needs and what he has: SP (clan leader), adena (clan leader), items (with where they come from), clan reputation, clan members. Green ok or orange "missing n".
  5. Increase clan level now - sends !clanlevel to the clan leader (he raises the level at the Giran village master). Greyed out with "Missing: ..." until everything is there. Confirmation first.
  6. Automatic level-up: ON / OFF with Switch on / Switch off - sends !clanlevel auto on|off. When on, the clan leader raises the level by himself (in a town, when everything is there). Confirmation first.
  7. Clan warehouse - the items the clan leader saw the last time he opened the clan warehouse, with count and enchant level, "last seen by ". "never seen yet" until the first look.
  8. Send party X to help - sends !assist <clan leader> to that party: it travels to the clan leader and hunts around him until stopped. Clan quests count kills only near the clan leader, so this is how you bring members to him. Confirmation first.
  9. Stop helping - sends !assist off (back to normal hunting). Confirmation first.

The level box says "No clan data from the clan leader yet" until his bot reports. The top line shows level, reputation and how many members the server listed.

#Clan level quests

Clan levels 1 and 2 only need SP and adena (the Increase clan level now button). Level 3 needs a Blood Mark, level 4 the quest Q501 Proof of Clan Alliance, level 5 Q503 Pursuit of Clan Ambition. Each has a box with its steps. Automated steps run with a button; manual steps need you or several characters together. Progress per step is in Logs/clanquest_<id>.json.

  1. automated - the bots can do this step.
  2. manual - you have to do it (the text says what).
  3. done - with who did it, when, and the bot's message.
  4. running - the step the bot is doing now. The golden frame marks the next step that is not done.
  5. Run - sends !clanquest <quest> <step> to the clan leader (confirmation first).
  6. Reset progress - sends !clanquest <quest> reset: the progress starts over (confirmation first).

The grey line under the title says where the quest comes from, and "Starts at clan level X; the clan is level Y" when the clan is not at the right level for it.

  1. failed - with the reason from the bot.
  2. Hunt step - one button per party ("Party Aldric (49+)" = its lowest level). The party hunts there until someone has the item. Send it to a party whose lowest level matches the step.

#How to raise the clan to level 4

  1. Check Clan level & reputation: SP and adena must be ok, only the Alliance Manifesto is missing.
  2. In the Q501 box, press Run on the golden step and confirm. Repeat for the next automated steps.
  3. Do the manual steps yourself (they need three clan members and the poison run; the text explains each).
  4. The last step is the level-up itself; or turn Automatic level-up on.

#Clan roster and clan quests

  1. Roster count - your characters in the clan / the member limit at this clan level. The table lists name, level, role and party.
  2. ON / OFF - switch a reputation quest (Q508 A Clan's Reputation, Q509 A Clan's Fame, Q510 A Clan's Prestige) on or off, after a confirmation. Saved in Scripts/data/clan_quests.json. A quest the clan is too low for is greyed out and says "needs clan level X, the clan is level Y" (an active one can still be switched off).
  3. Active quest - ON (highlighted).

What "ON" does:

  • Raid hunt puts that quest's bosses first (the level window, raid curse and route checks still apply).
  • Every 10 minutes the dashboard sends one fitting party that is not in a raid to one quest boss that is not known dead (!mission raid <boss>) and sends the clan leader along (!assist <party>), because the kill only counts within 1500 of the clan leader. At most one call per boss every 6 hours. The calls are logged in Logs/clan.log.

#Clan raid bosses

  1. Rule - the clan leader has to be there; it only counts once the quest is active (clan level 5+).
  2. Status - alive, dead or unknown, from the raid status the bots record, and when it was seen.
  3. Reward - the quest item and how much reputation it gives.
  4. Parties - for every party of 3+: a green chip "Party X fits" with a Send button, or a grey chip with the reason ("raid curse: party max 50 > 35+8", "too strong: boss 70 > party min 49+3"). Send sends !mission raid <boss> to that party after a confirmation; send the clan leader along with Send party ... to help (above).

#Clan skills

  1. Focus line - which skill the clan saves reputation for, and what it costs (reputation + items).
  2. Focus ✓ - the chosen skill (its row has a gold frame).
  3. Focus - choose this skill instead (confirmation first). Saved in Scripts/data/clan_quests.json.

The table is grouped by clan level ("(now)" marks the current one): skill and level, effect, reputation, items, kind and minimum rank. Residence skills are faded and say "needs a castle/fortress"; they cannot be focused.

#Clan levels

  1. now - the current level (gold frame).

Per level: leader SP, adena, items (and where they come from), reputation, members needed, member limit after the level-up (main + academy). Hover a row for where to do it and notes.

#New accounts (Academy)

  1. Login - 3-16 letters or digits, starting with a letter.
  2. Password - the game password. It is cleared from the page right after sending and stored only encrypted (L2Swarm's own encryption).
  3. Character name - the character to create at the first login.
  4. Class - the fastest solo class to level 40 with board buffs, or the runner-up (the reasons are under the form).
  5. Create - asks for confirmation, then the dashboard creates the account config, a one-time script that creates the character at the empty character list, and logs the account in. Progress goes to Logs/academy.log.
  6. Academy rules - clan level needed, who may join, graduation.

The label says "(optional)", but the dashboard server refuses an empty character name; always fill it in.

#Seven Signs

The bots always sign up with the Lords of Dawn. They do it by themselves at a Priest of Dawn (at every Giran regroup) in the competition period, after the first class transfer; !dawn does it now.

  1. Period line - competition or seal validation (with last week's winner), the next change (Monday 18:00), and when and by whom the priest was last read.
  2. Dawn - the character is signed up.
  3. not registered - with the reason: needs the 1st class transfer, the priest asked for a fee (see Logs/dawn.log), or the last try failed.
  4. Catacombs / necropolises - "may enter" or "closed", with the rule: in the competition period anyone signed up may enter; in the validation period only the winning side, and only where it owns the seal.

#Clan event: several parties on an epic boss

  1. Boss - Queen Ant, Core, Orfen, Zaken, Baium, Antharas, Valakas, Frintezza (with level). The line under it: zone, entry, weak element, whether it needs a Command Channel.
  2. Command Channel leader - a party leader; "✓ " when he may open a Command Channel, "(no CC right yet)" otherwise. Choosing him also ticks his party.
  3. Party checkboxes - with size, level range and the level check (green = fits, orange = why not).
  4. Start the clan event - asks for confirmation, then sends !jointraid <boss> with <other parties> cc <leader> to the main party. Every party runs its raid mission on the boss, the main leader waits until all are within 2500, the CC leader invites the other party leaders into the Command Channel (they accept by themselves), then GO.

Warnings under the count: a party that does not fit the boss level, fewer than 18 people (a Command Channel only gets the loot right with more), a CC leader without the right, and a CC leader whose party is not ticked.

A Command Channel needs one of: clan leader of a level-5 clan, a Strategy Guide (item 8871) in the bag, or the Clan Imperium skill.

#Raid team templates

  1. Boss - every boss that has a template (★ = epic boss).
  2. Template - level window, weak element, elements to avoid, entry; a table of roles (with suitable classes), the job of each role, the characters proposed from all your characters (any party; orange = why one does not fit) and what is missing; how many places are filled from which parties; and the tactics. Read only: in a raid on this boss the bots use the template by themselves (nukers prefer the weak element, the tank keeps the minions).

Templates live in Scripts/data/raid_templates.json.

#Another clan

When some of your characters are in another clan, it gets its own tab.

  1. Its tab.

  2. Clan card - leader (ours, with party and level, or "not one of our characters"), clan level, reputation, alliance, when seen.

  3. Our members - your characters in it, with level, class, party, CLAN LEADER, whether one may open a Command Channel, offline.

  4. calls other parties - (only when the leader is ours) Send to help (!assist <leader>) and Stop (!assist off) per party.

  5. leader - the member list as the server sent it: name, level, unit (main / academy), online.

#Founding the clan

Before the clan exists, the clan box lets you pick the name and found it.

  1. Clan name - 2 to 16 letters or digits, no spaces.
  2. Save name - stores the name in Scripts/data/clan_quests.json (confirmation first). It cannot be changed here once the clan exists.
  3. Found the clan now - sends !clancreate to the clan leader (confirmation first). The clan is created once, when the clan leader is level 10+ and in no clan; the code never creates a second clan.

#Commands

Command Sent to What
!clanwh clan leader open the clan warehouse and report it
!clanlevel / `!clanlevel auto on off` clan leader
`!clanquest [ reset]` clan leader (hunt steps: a party)
!clancreate clan leader found the clan
!assist <name> / !assist off a party go and hunt around that character / stop
!mission raid <boss> a party raid a boss (Send button)
!jointraid <boss> with <parties> [cc <leader>] main party clan event on an epic boss
!dawn a party sign up with the Lords of Dawn now

#Notes

  • Every button that sends an order or changes a file asks for confirmation (except switching clan tabs and the selects).
  • The roster lists only your own characters; the server's full member list is on another clan's tab and in the level box count.
  • Clan levels, quests and skills follow L2J High Five; your server may differ.

#Zones (#/zones)

The Zones tab is where you define your own hunting zones: places where a party levels up. A zone has a name, a level range, the parties that may use it, how the team gets there (a gatekeeper teleport or a .town command), and either a simple circle (centre + radius) or a drawn hunting area with exclusion zones (places the team must never fight in) and pull routes (a path the tank runs to gather monsters).

All zones live in one file, Scripts/data/custom_zones.json. The same entries appear on the Spots tab (where you tick which party may use which spot and set priorities) and in the full-screen spot editor (waypoints, round exclusions, floors, monsters to avoid). The shape editor can drag the outline of any zone.

How the bots use zones. When a party leader needs a hunting spot (auto-level, see Concepts), he first takes the party's own choice from the Parties tab, if there is one. Otherwise he takes the custom zones that are enabled, whose level range contains the party's lowest level, whose party list contains his party (or "all") and whose Kind fits the team. Of those, the one with the lowest priority number for his party wins (set on the Spots tab, empty = 50); equal priority = the nearest. Only when no zone fits does he use the generated outdoor areas and the built-in spot list. swarm.js reads the file at every spot pick, so every save is live: no deploy and no restart. A party already hunting in a zone keeps the old version until its next spot check (every few minutes).

On this page:

  • The top of the tab
  • Zone editor: fields, the map, drawing modes, layers, zoom, save and delete
  • Simple zone form and the zone table
  • How to ...
  • Notes and safety

#The top of the tab

  1. What the zones are for: a one-line reminder that auto-level uses these zones first and that edits apply live.
  2. ✎ Edit a zone's shape: a filter box, a list of every hunting zone and every field area (grouped "Hunting zones / spots (custom_zones.json)" and "Field areas (field_areas.json)"), and Edit shape. It opens the full-screen shape editor for the picked item. The list shows each item's levels and a mark: ▱ drawn polygon, ○ circle, · rooms hunts inside dungeon rooms, ✎ edited on the dashboard, OFF switched off. Type in the filter to shorten the list.
  3. Open full screen: opens the zone that is open in the editor below in the full-screen spot editor (#/spot/<name>). With no zone open it opens the spot editor's picker (#/spot).
  4. + New spot on the map: starts a new spot in the full-screen spot editor (#/spot/new).
  5. ✎ Drag-edit shape (on a phone the title row is wider than the screen; scroll it sideways to reach this button): opens the zone picked in the zone picker (6) in the shape editor. With nothing picked you get "Pick something to edit first.".
  6. Zone picker ("— pick a zone —"): every zone, sorted by its lowest level, shown as name (min-max, party) and OFF when it is switched off. Picking one opens it in the zone editor.
  7. New zone at…: starts a new zone at the position of the character chosen in (8).
  8. Character: every character the dashboard knows. The list fills once the live data has arrived (open the tab again if it is empty).

#Zone editor

The zone editor works on one zone at a time. Nothing is written until you press Save zone; the summary line says unsaved changes while you have edits that are not saved.

#Fields

  1. Name: the zone's name. It is also its key: saving under a new name renames the zone.
  2. Team: all or one party (a party is named after its leader). Note: once you have ticked parties for this zone on the Spots tab, those ticks decide and this field is ignored; change the parties there.
  3. Levels: lowest and highest party level the zone is meant for. The leader compares the party's lowest level with this range. The map recolours the monsters as soon as you change the numbers.
  4. Kind: which kind of team may use it: any team, mage team (at least half of the party are nukers / necromancers), melee team (the others), small team (3 characters or fewer).
  5. enabled: untick to switch the zone off. The bots never pick a zone that is off.
  6. Get there: gatekeeper teleport (the leader takes the team to the town and uses its gatekeeper) or .town and walk (the leader uses the .townname command and the team walks from the town).
  7. Gatekeeper destination: shown text like Gludin -> Abandoned Camp. Type it (the list suggests every destination the bots have seen on a live gatekeeper menu) or tap a blue square on the map.
  8. Town: for .town and walk: pick the town, or tap a gold square on the map.

#Drawing buttons and layers

  1. Hunting area: drawing mode for the green outline: the area the team fights in. A tap on the map adds a corner. A tap close to an edge inserts the corner into that edge, so the outline stays clean.
  2. Exclusion zone: drawing mode for the red outlines: places inside the hunting area where the team must never fight (a cliff, a spot next to a raid boss). The exclusion that is being edited has a solid outline, the others are dashed.
  3. + new exclusion: starts another exclusion zone and switches to Exclusion mode.
  4. Pull route: drawing mode for the yellow line. Taps add points at the end. The first point is where the team waits ("tank waits here"); the leader runs along the other points, tags monsters and brings them back. While you draw, the points are numbered.
  5. + new pull route: starts another pull route ("pull 2", ...). With several routes the leader uses them in turn.
  6. Move / pan: tapping no longer adds points; drag the map to move the view.
  7. Delete point: deletes the selected point (tap a point first; it turns white).
  8. Delete this shape: in Hunting area mode it clears the whole outline; in Exclusion or Pull route mode it removes the exclusion / route that is being edited. There is no confirmation, but nothing is saved until you press Save zone (open the zone again from the picker to throw your edits away).
  9. teleport landings: show or hide the blue squares (gatekeeper landings) and gold squares (.town landings).
  10. monsters: show or hide the monster spawns (from the game's datapack).
  11. + / − / Fit: zoom in, zoom out, and fit the whole zone. A mouse wheel over the map zooms too.
  12. Summary line: 6 area points · 1 exclusions · 1 pull routes · area 13.2 km² and · unsaved changes after edits.
  13. The map: see below.

#The map, legend, Save and Delete

  1. The map: the game's map art with the zone drawn on it. Green = hunting area, red = exclusion zones, yellow = pull routes (the label at the first point says "(tank waits here)"), blue squares = gatekeeper landings with their name, white square = the landing the zone uses, gold squares = .town landings, coloured dots with names = your characters that are online nearby. Monster dots are coloured against the zone's level range: grey = more than 3 levels below, green = fits, orange = up to 4 above, red = more. A purple dot with a crown is a raid boss.
  2. Legend: the same colours as a list.

The zone editor does not draw a zone's waypoints and round exclusions (circles); open the zone in the full-screen spot editor to see and edit those. 3. Save zone: writes the zone (see Saving). 4. Delete zone: removes the zone after a confirmation.

The points of the shape you are editing are big and draggable; the points of the other shapes are small. Drag any point to move it (also a point of a shape that is not active). Tap a point to select it (white, with its number).

#Exclusion mode and a selected point

  1. The selected point: white and numbered. Delete point removes it.

#Pull route mode

  1. Point 1: the team waits here; the label reads "pull 1 (tank waits here)".
  2. The last point: the far end of the run.

#Adding and dragging points

  1. A corner that was dragged further out.
  2. A corner that was added by tapping next to the east edge (it went into that edge, not at the end of the list).

  1. After any edit the summary line ends with unsaved changes.

#Zoom and layers

  1. Zoomed in far enough, every monster dot shows its level. The white square is the gatekeeper landing this zone starts from; tap any blue square to make it the zone's start (the "Get there" fields follow).

  1. teleport landings off. 2. monsters off. Only the zone's own shapes and your characters stay on the map.

#New zone at a character

  1. Character: the character to start from.
  2. New zone at…: opens a new, unsaved zone: a square hunting area of 4 000 x 4 000 around the character.
  3. Name: New zone <month-day hour:minute>; change it before you save.
  4. Levels: the character's level −3 to +5. The Team is the character's party.

#Saving

  1. Save zone.
  2. The result: "saved — the bots use it on their next spot check", or the error.

What Save zone does:

  • The page checks: a name is needed ("give the zone a name"), and the hunting area needs at least 3 points ("the hunting area needs at least 3 points"). Exclusions with fewer than 3 points and pull routes with fewer than 2 points are dropped.
  • The server writes the zone into Scripts/data/custom_zones.json. A copy of the old file goes to Scripts/data/routes/spots_history/.
  • With a drawn hunting area the server sets the zone's centre (average of the corners) and radius (farthest corner) and writes the outline as an L2Swarm zone map, Settings/zones/<name>.zmap, so L2Swarm's own combat also stays inside it.
  • Fields the zone editor does not show (waypoints, round exclusions, floor, avoided monsters, party ticks and priorities) are kept.
