  1. Here the hunting area was cleared with Delete this shape; Save answers "the hunting area needs at least 3 points" and nothing is written.

Delete zone asks "Delete zone name?". OK removes the zone from the file (the old file is copied to routes/spots_history/ first).

#Simple zone form and the zone table

Under the zone editor is an older, simpler way to make a circle zone: a centre, a radius and the basic fields. Under it, the table lists every zone.

  1. Name: the zone's name (required). Saving with the name of an existing zone replaces that zone.
  2. X / Y / Z: the centre (X and Y required).
  3. Radius: default 2500. The bots hunt in a square around the centre of 3 x the radius, at least 9 000 wide.
  4. Level min / Level max: default 1 and 85.
  5. Party: all or one party.
  6. Teleport: optional gatekeeper destination, for example Gludio -> Ruins of Agony (the part before -> is the town).
  7. Take position from: pick a character to copy its current X, Y and Z into the fields.
  8. Save zone: saves without a confirmation. The message under the page header says "zone saved — auto-level picks it up on its next check".

  1. Columns: Zone, Levels, Party, Center / radius (x, y, z · r), Teleport. Sorted by the lowest level. The Party column shows the zone's single party field; it is empty (or out of date) for zones whose parties were ticked on the Spots tab.
  2. Edit: copies the zone's values into the simple form above (it does not open the zone editor; use the zone picker for that).
  3. Delete: removes the zone after "Delete zone name?".

  1. The message line under the page header.

Warning: the simple form only knows circles. Saving a zone that has a drawn hunting area through the simple form (Edit, then Save zone) removes its drawn hunting area, its exclusion zones and its pull routes, and resets "Get there" to the Teleport text. Use the zone editor or the spot editor for drawn zones.

#How to ...

Draw a new hunting zone around a party that is hunting now

  1. Pick the party leader in the character list next to New zone at… and press New zone at….
  2. Change the Name, the Levels and, if needed, Kind.
  3. With Hunting area on, drag the 4 corners to the edge of the area you want, and tap next to an edge to add corners where the outline must bend.
  4. Tap the blue square of the gatekeeper landing the team should use (or choose .town and walk and a town).
  5. Press Save zone. The leader uses the zone at his next spot check if it fits his party.

Keep the team away from a dangerous corner

  1. Open the zone in the zone picker.
  2. Press + new exclusion and tap around the dangerous place (at least 3 points).
  3. Press Save zone.

Add a pull route

  1. Open the zone, press + new pull route.
  2. Tap the waiting point first (where the team stands), then the points the tank should run along.
  3. Press Save zone.

Delete a single point: tap it (it turns white), then Delete point.

#Notes and safety

  • Every save and delete on this tab is live for the bots (no deploy). Only Delete zone asks for confirmation; Save zone and the simple form's Save do not.
  • Backups: every save or delete through the zone editor or the simple form copies the whole file to Scripts/data/routes/spots_history/.
  • A drawn hunting area becomes Settings/zones/<name>.zmap too; deleting a zone does not delete that file.
  • Who may use a zone and in which order is easier to set on the Spots tab. Waypoints from the landing to the area, round exclusions, a tower floor and monsters to avoid are only in the spot editor.
  • What the bots do inside a zone: the leader only takes monsters inside the hunting area and outside every exclusion zone (and any monster that attacks the team). With a pull route the leader (only a party leader in a party, not a solo character) runs the route, tags up to 4 monsters at each point, turns back below 50 % HP and brings them to the waiting team; melee damage dealers switch to a polearm from their bag for the pack if they carry one.
  • A plain circle zone (no drawn area, no pull route, no waypoints) is hunted as the generated field areas inside its square, rotating between the free ones that fit; see field areas.

#Spots (#/spots) and the full-screen spot editor (#/spot)

The Spots tab decides which party may hunt where, and in which order. Every row is one hunting spot from Scripts/data/custom_zones.json (the same entries as on the Zones tab). For every party you tick whether it may use the spot and give it a priority number. You can switch spots on and off, and add a spot inside a catacomb, a necropolis or a dungeon with rooms.

The full-screen spot editor (#/spot/<name>) draws everything about one spot on a big map that works with a mouse and with fingers: where the team starts (teleport or .town), the waypoints from there to the hunting area, the hunting area, exclusion areas and exclusion circles, a floor for towers and caves, and monsters the team must never attack there.

How a party leader picks his spot (see also Concepts): a spot chosen for the party on the Parties tab always wins. Otherwise he looks at the enabled spots his party is ticked for whose level range contains the party's lowest level, takes the one with the lowest priority number, and of equal numbers the nearest. Every change on this page and in the spot editor is saved at once into the file, and swarm.js reads that file at every spot pick: live, no deploy.

On this page:

  • Spots table
  • Add a dungeon spot
  • Full-screen spot editor
  • How to ...
  • Notes and safety

#Spots table (#/spots)

  1. + New spot on the map: opens the spot editor with a new spot (#/spot/new).
  2. Map editor: opens the spot editor's picker (#/spot).
  3. Filter: shows only rows whose spot name, way in or kind contains the text.
  4. only spots that fit a party: hides rows that fit no party's lowest level.
  5. How the leader picks: the rules above, in short.
  6. ✎ Edit a spot's shape: picker for the shape editor: hunting spots, the datapack spots (the bots' built-in fallback list) and the field areas, with a filter and Edit shape.

#The columns

  1. Spot + map: the spot's name. map opens it in the full-screen spot editor. "✓ saved" appears for 5 seconds after a change to that row.
  2. Kind: outdoor (a circle: centre + radius), drawn area (a drawn hunting area), dungeon (inside a catacomb or necropolis), rooms (the rooms of a dungeon with floors; the leader picks a room that fits the level).
  3. ON / OFF: tap to switch the spot on or off. OFF rows are faded and never picked.
  4. Party ticks: one column per party (named after its leader; under the name the party's lowest and highest level). Tick = this party may use the spot. When every party is ticked the spot is stored as "all" and the cell shows "all".
  5. Priority: shown next to a tick. 1 = first choice; empty = 50 = normal. Any number from 1 to 99. Unticking a party also removes its priority.
  6. ✕: delete. Only for spots that were added with Add a dungeon spot (asks first). Other spots can only be switched OFF.

The other columns: Lvl (the spot's level range), Way in (the gatekeeper destination, .town, "inside dungeon" or "rooms in dungeon"). A green cell means the spot's level range contains that party's lowest level right now. The table reloads every 20 seconds while the tab is open.

#Filter and "only spots that fit"

After you type in the filter or tick "only spots that fit", the ticks and priority boxes of the rows that moved can show the values of the row that was in that place before, until the table reloads (every 20 seconds, or when you open the tab again). Wait for the reload before you change a tick in a filtered table.

  1. Filter text ("route").
  2. only spots that fit a party ticked.
  3. A green cell: the spot fits that party's lowest level.

  1. "all": the spot is open to every party. Untick one party and the others stay ticked by name.

#Saving a change

  1. A priority typed into a party's box (saved when you leave the box or press Enter).
  2. ✓ saved next to the spot name.

Every tick, priority and ON/OFF change is sent at once (no Save button, no confirmation). If the server refuses, the reason appears under the page header and the table reloads. Before every change the server copies the file to Settings/backup/custom_zones_<time>.json.

#Add a dungeon spot

  1. Type: Catacomb / Necropolis (the Seven Signs dungeons, from catacombs.json) or Dungeon with floors / rooms (Cruma Tower, Tower of Insolence, Ant Nest, ... from dungeon_rooms.json).
  2. Dungeon: the dungeon, with its level range.
  3. Level min and 4. Level max: filled with the dungeon's levels when you pick it; change them if you want.
  4. Parties: tick at least one party.
  5. Add spot: adds a spot named <dungeon> (<min>-<max>). No confirmation.

What the new spot does: a Catacomb / Necropolis spot makes the leader take the party inside that dungeon and hunt there; a rooms spot makes him walk into the dungeon and hunt in a room that fits the party's level (see Rooms). The entry is marked "added on the dashboard", so it can be deleted with ✕ later.

  1. The message under the header: "spot added: dungeon".

  1. Without a party ticked: "tick at least one party". Without a dungeon or with min above max: "pick a dungeon and a level range (min ≤ max)".

✕ asks "Delete the spot "name"?". Only spots added on the dashboard can be deleted; the server refuses the others with "only spots added on the dashboard can be deleted (switch others off)".

#Full-screen spot editor (#/spot)

Open it with + New spot on the map, Map editor or a row's map link here, or Open full screen / + New spot on the map on the Zones tab. Addresses:

Address Opens
#/spot the picker panel (no spot open)
#/spot/new a new spot
#/spot/<name> that spot (the name URL-encoded). An unknown name shows "No spot called ... — pick one or start a new one" and the picker.

It covers the whole screen. On a phone use one finger to drag and tap, two fingers to zoom; on a desktop drag with the mouse and zoom with the wheel (Ctrl + wheel zooms faster).

#Picker (#/spot)

  1. ✕: closes the panel (the map stays).
  2. + New spot: starts a new spot.
  3. Filter: shortens the list.
  4. The spots: name, levels, parties, OFF, route (has waypoints), area (has a drawn area). Tap one to open it.
  5. Find a place: search for a dungeon, town, teleport, character or spot and jump there on the map (see Find a place).

#The screen

  1. ◀ Back: back to where you came from. With unsaved changes it asks "Leave without saving the changes to this spot?".
  2. Spot name: type to rename. Saving under a new name renames the spot (if that name is taken it asks "A spot called ... exists already — replace it?").
  3. Floor shown: which height the map shows: All heights, the spot's own floor (★), the floors of the dungeons in view (for example "Cruma Tower: 1st floor"), and height bands found in the monster spawns in view ("height -2900..-2700 (40 spawns)"). For towers and caves the map art of that level is shown and only the monsters, characters and points of that floor are drawn bright. This only changes the view; the spot's hunting floor is set in ☰.
  4. ↶ / ↷: undo and redo (also Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y).
  5. ⤢: fit the whole spot on the screen.
  6. ☰: the settings panel.
  7. Save: saves the spot. It shows Save • while there are unsaved changes. Ctrl+S saves too.
  8. Legend (not shown on phones): waypoints (light blue), hunt area (green), excluded (red), teleport landing (blue square), .town (gold square), monster colours (grey low, green fits, orange above, red too high, purple raid boss).
  9. Hint: what the current tool does, then a summary: start ✓ / no start yet, number of waypoints, area corners and size, exclusions, avoided monsters, floor, and N leg(s) may hit a wall when the wall check failed.
  10. Tools: see below.

What is on the map: the start (a white ring labelled START <teleport>), a dashed line from the start to waypoint 1 and solid lines between the waypoints (a red line with "⚠ wall?" = the straight walk between those two points runs into a wall according to the geodata), the green hunting area, red exclusion areas (solid while you edit them) and circles, pull routes from the Zones tab (dashed yellow, shown but not editable here), your online characters, the monsters (datapack spawns, plus small red squares for the monsters a party leader in view sees right now) and the names of dungeon entrances (⌂). A spot without a drawn area yet shows its old centre and radius as a dashed green circle with "old centre + radius — draw the hunt area".

#Tools

On a phone the row scrolls sideways:

  1. ✋ Move map (key 1): drag to move the map; tap a point to select it. Nothing is added.
  2. ⚑ Start (key 2): tap a blue square (gatekeeper landing) or a gold square (.town landing). That is where the team starts. If several destinations land on the same square, a box asks which one ("Which teleport? 1) ... 2) ..."). Missing the square gives "Tap right on a blue (gatekeeper landing) or gold (.town) square — or pick the start in ☰". After a start the tool switches to Waypoints if there are none yet.
  3. ➜ Waypoints (key 3): each tap adds the next waypoint; a tap on a line inserts one there. The whole team walks every point, member by member, from the start to the area.
  4. ▱ Hunt area (key 4): tap around the hunting area; a tap near an edge inserts a corner. The team only fights inside it. If the map shows a floor and the spot has no floor yet, the first corner sets the hunting floor to that floor (a message says so).
  5. ⛔ Exclude area (key 5): tap around a place the team must never fight in.
  6. ⭘ Exclude circle (key 6): tap to drop a no-fight circle. Drag its centre to move it, drag the small handle on its edge to resize.
  7. ☠ Avoid monster (key 7): tap a monster dot: that monster kind is never attacked in this spot ("name: never fought in this spot"); tap one again to allow it ("allowed again"). Avoided monsters are drawn black with a red ring.
  8. + New: only with Exclude area: starts another exclusion area.

Every new point gets its height (z) from the geodata: the ground under it closest to the floor shown, or to the previous point.

#Selecting a point

  1. The selected point is white and larger. Tap it again to unselect, or press Esc.
  2. The selected point box: its name ("Waypoint 2", "Area corner 3", "Exclusion 1, corner 2", "Exclusion circle 1") and x / y.
  3. z: the height. Type a number, or, where the geodata has several floors at that spot (towers, caves), tap one of the buttons after "floors here:". A single floor shows "ground z".
  4. Delete: removes the point (also the Delete / Backspace key).

Drag any point to move it; when you let go it gets a new height from the geodata and the waypoint legs are checked again.

  1. The circle's centre (drag to move). 2. The radius handle (drag to resize). 3. radius: type the radius (50 or more).

  1. A corner of an exclusion area. 2. Delete this exclusion: removes the whole exclusion area.

#Drawing, step by step pictures

  1. ⚑ Start is on. 2. The hint tells you to tap a blue or gold square.

  1. The new waypoint (number 5). The new leg is checked against the geodata about a second later; a red leg with "⚠ wall?" means the team cannot walk it in a straight line: add a waypoint in between or move the point.
  2. The summary line counts the legs that may hit a wall.

  1. ▱ Hunt area is on. 2. The new corner is selected (its box shows "Area corner N").

  1. + New. 2. A new exclusion area drawn with three taps.

  1. The new circle (its size depends on the zoom; change it with the radius box or the handle). 2. radius.

  1. ☠ Avoid monster is on. 2. The message after tapping a monster dot.

#Settings panel (☰)

  1. Levels: lowest and highest party level.
  2. enabled (the parties may pick it).
  3. Team kind: any, mage, melee, small (as on the Zones tab).
  4. Parties that may use it: all parties or single parties. Ticking "all" clears the others; ticking a party clears "all"; unticking the last one sets "all" again.
  5. Start: — none (walk / automatic) —, gatekeeper teleport or .town and walk.
  6. Gatekeeper destination (a list of every known destination) or the town. Or use the ⚑ Start tool on the map.

  1. Hunting floor (towers, caves): — any height (outdoor) —, the spot's floor, "the floor the map shows", or a floor of a dungeon in view. With a floor the team only fights monsters on that height band, and in towers and caves it never uses L2Swarm's path search (it attacks and lets the server walk to the monster).
  2. Monsters never fought here: the avoided monsters as chips; ✕ on a chip allows it again.
  3. Monster name and 4. Add: avoid a monster by typing its name.
  4. monsters, 6. teleport landings, 7. characters: map layers on/off.

  1. Find a place. 2. Note: free text kept with the spot. 3. Clear all drawing: removes the waypoints, the hunt area and every exclusion after a confirmation (Undo brings them back). 4. Delete spot: deletes the saved spot after a confirmation and goes back to the picker.

Below the danger zone: "Keys: 1-7 tools, Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y undo/redo, Del deletes the selected point, Ctrl+S saves. Every save keeps the old file in Scripts/data/routes/spots_history." If the spot has pull routes from the Zones tab, the panel says they are kept; a rooms or dungeon spot says that way in comes first.

#Find a place

  1. Type at least 2 letters. The list shows dungeons (⌂, with their number of floors), .town landings, teleport landings (⚑), characters (●, with level) and spots (▱). Tap one: the map jumps there and zooms in. For a dungeon the map switches to its first floor. On a phone the panel closes.

#A new spot (#/spot/new)

  1. The message: "New spot: 1) Start — tap where the team teleports in · 2) Waypoints · 3) Hunt area. Use ☰ to find a place."
  2. The ⚑ Start tool is already on.
  3. The settings panel is open (use Find a place to get to the right part of the world).

The new spot is called New spot <month-day hour:minute>, with levels and party taken from the first online character (its level −3 to +5).

#Saving

  1. "Saved — the leaders use it on their next spot pick (within 5 min, no deploy needed)".

Save checks, in this order:

Check What you see
a name "Give the spot a name first"
a hunt area with at least 3 corners "Draw the hunt area first (▱ Hunt area, at least 3 corners)" and the Hunt area tool switches on
a start (not needed for rooms / dungeon spots) confirmation "No start (teleport / .town) is set: the team walks from wherever it is. Save anyway?"
levels "Level min is above level max"
the name is free confirmation "A spot called ... exists already — replace it?"

The spot is written into Scripts/data/custom_zones.json with everything you drew: hunting area, exclusion areas (3+ corners), circles, waypoints, start, floor (its height is stored as the middle of the floor band, else the average height of the area corners), avoided monsters, parties, levels, kind, note. A copy of the old file goes to Scripts/data/routes/spots_history/. A failed save shows "Not saved: reason".

The browser also warns before closing the page while a spot has unsaved changes.

#A spot on one floor of a tower

  1. Floor shown: the spot's floor. The map art is that floor's.
  2. The summary ends with "floor name", and the map writes "hunting floor: name (z ...)" in the middle of the area.

With a hunting floor the bots ignore monsters more than 150 above or below the floor band, and a team member outside the band does not count as "in the area".

#How to ...

Let only one party use a spot, as its first choice

  1. On the Spots tab, untick every other party in that row (or tick only that party if it showed "all").
  2. Type 1 in that party's priority box.

Make a spot for a new hunting ground from scratch

  1. + New spot on the map. In ☰ use Find a place to jump to the area, close the panel.
  2. ⚑ Start: tap the gatekeeper landing (blue) the team should teleport to.
  3. ➜ Waypoints: tap the way from the landing to the hunting ground. Watch for red legs ("⚠ wall?"): add points around the obstacle.
  4. ▱ Hunt area: tap around the area.
  5. Optional: ⛔ / ⭘ for places to avoid, ☠ for monsters to leave alone.
  6. ☰: set the levels, the parties, the name (top bar).
  7. Save.

Hunt on one floor of a tower: pick the floor in the floor menu at the top, draw the hunt area (the first corner sets the spot's hunting floor to the floor shown), check ☰ → Hunting floor, Save.

#Notes and safety

  • Everything here is live for the bots (custom_zones.json is read at every spot pick). The leader picks again every few minutes, so a party that is hunting keeps its spot until then.
  • Confirmations: ✕ on the Spots tab, Save without a start, Save over an existing name, Clear all drawing, Delete spot, leaving with unsaved changes. Ticks, priorities, ON/OFF and Add spot are sent without asking.
  • Backups: Spots tab changes → Settings/backup/custom_zones_<time>.json; spot editor saves and deletes → Scripts/data/routes/spots_history/.
  • What the bots do with the drawing: after the teleport every member walks the waypoints point by point by itself and they all wait at the last one (only when the team landed near the route; otherwise they walk the normal way); then the leader hunts only monsters inside the area and outside every exclusion (a circle or exclusion drawn with a height only counts on that floor, ±400-500); avoided monster kinds are never attacked within the spot's area plus 3 000.
  • To change only the outline of a spot by dragging, the shape editor is quicker; it keeps everything else.

#Rooms (#/rooms)

Inside a dungeon the bots do not hunt "somewhere in the dungeon": they hunt in one room. The Rooms tab shows every dungeon, its floors and its rooms, and lets you draw the walk-in route for a room: the points the party leader walks, in straight lines, from the place where he arrives on the floor (the floor entry) to the room. Without a route of yours he uses the computed route (found with the geodata). From here you also open a room's outline in the shape editor.

Dungeons, floors and rooms (data file Scripts/data/dungeon_rooms.json, made by the tools in docs/plan/tools, about 30 dungeons and 900 rooms, including the catacombs and necropolises):

  • A floor is a height band of a dungeon (Cruma Tower 1st, 2nd, 3rd floor; Tower of Insolence 1st to 12th floor; one floor "Inside" for a catacomb). Floors are reached on foot or with a teleporter NPC in the dungeon; the leader takes the party there by himself.
  • A room is a group of monster spawns close together, with an outline found from the geodata (walls and doorways), its monster levels, the party levels it suits, its monsters, and the side (left / right / straight / behind) as seen from the floor entry.
  • A floor has safe spots (green shields on the maps): places in the corridors away from every room and every aggressive monster, used when a character has to get away from a fight.

How rooms are used: a party hunts in rooms when its spot is a "rooms" spot (see Spots) or when you chose a room (or several) for the party on the Parties tab. The leader takes the party to the floor, walks your saved points in straight hops (if a hop fails he stops following them), then walks to the room centre and hunts only inside the room outline. swarm.js reads a room's saved route every time it walks into that room, so a saved route is used from the next walk in, no deploy.

#Pick a dungeon, floor and room

  1. Dungeon: every dungeon with its monster level range.
  2. Floor: the floors of that dungeon with their level ranges.
  3. Room: the rooms of that floor, with their monster levels. A ✓ in front of a room means it has a saved route.
  4. ✎ Edit this room's outline: opens the room in the shape editor (drag its corners on the floor map, move it, set its levels and centre).
  5. Room facts: the room's name, side, monster levels, the party levels it suits, ✓ saved route or computed route only, and (in grey) its monsters with levels.
  6. Entry, floor height, saved route: how the floor is entered (for example "teleporter via NPC → x, y, z"), the floor's height band, and "Saved: N points, date" or "none". A note about the room follows when there is one.

#The map

  1. Zoom + and 2. Zoom −. The mouse wheel zooms around the pointer.
  2. Fit: the whole route, the room and the floor entry.
  3. Start from the computed route: copies the computed route into your point list (asks first if you already have points).
  4. Floor entry = point 1: puts the floor entry in front of your points (only shown when the floor entry is known).
  5. The floor map: the map art of that floor (towers and caves use the picture of the right level). On it: the room in red with its name, the other rooms of the floor faint blue with their short ids, safe spots as green shields, the floor entry as a blue square, the computed route as a dashed grey line, your points as a yellow line with numbered dots (the selected one red), and your characters on that floor.
  6. Legend, with the controls: tap = new point after the selected one · drag a point = move it · drag the map = pan · wheel = zoom.

The line above the buttons says how many points you have, the length of the walk and unsaved changes after an edit.

#Points, Save and the point table

  1. Character: every character that reported in the last 2 minutes.
  2. Add its position: inserts that character's position (x, y, z) after the selected point. Walk a character to a good spot in game, then press it.
  3. Save: saves the points (at least 2).
  4. Delete saved route: removes the saved route after a confirmation; the leader then uses the computed one. Only shown when a route is saved.
  5. Undo changes: drops your edits and loads the saved route again (no confirmation).
  6. x / y / z: type a number to change a point.
  7. ↑ / ↓ / ✕: move a point earlier or later in the list, or delete it. Tap a row (not a box) to select that point; the selected row is highlighted and new points are added after it.
  8. Paste coordinates: opens the paste box.

The step column shows the distance from the previous point ("start" for the first).

#Paste coordinates

  1. One point per line: x y z, or a line copied from the game's /loc output. Every line with three numbers becomes a point.
  2. Add after the selected point. Without any usable line you get "No x y z found".

#A room without a saved route

  1. computed route only.
  2. "No saved route: the leader uses the computed one (grey). Tap the map to add points, or start from the computed route."

#Editing, step by step pictures

  1. "added point 9": a tap on the map adds a point after the selected one, at the floor's middle height.
  2. The count line now says unsaved changes.

Picking another dungeon, floor or room with unsaved points asks "Drop the unsaved changes of room id?". Cancel keeps you on the room.

"Replace your N points with the computed route (M points)?"

  1. saved ✓. The room now has a ✓ in the room list.

"A route needs at least 2 points". Errors from the server (for example an unknown room) appear the same way.

"Delete the saved route for room? The leader then uses the computed one."

#How to ...

Draw a walk-in route for a room

  1. Pick the dungeon, floor and room.
  2. Press Floor entry = point 1 (or Start from the computed route to start from the computed line and fix it).
  3. Tap the map along the corridors to the room. Each tap adds a point after the selected (red) one. Keep the legs straight through open corridor: the leader walks them in straight lines.
  4. Drag points to fine-tune; use ↑ / ↓ / ✕ in the table.
  5. Press Save.

Record a route by walking a character there in game: put the character at each corner of the way and press Add its position each time (or paste /loc lines into Paste coordinates).

#Notes and safety

  • Files: Scripts/data/routes/rooms/<room id>.json ({ id, dungeon, floor, room, points: [{x, y, z}], by, updated }). Every save or delete first copies the old file to Scripts/data/routes/rooms/history/.
  • Confirmations: Delete saved route, Start from the computed route (when you have points), switching rooms with unsaved changes. Save and Undo changes do not ask.
  • A new point gets the floor's middle height. Points you add from a character or paste keep their own z; a point saved without a z gets the room centre's height.
  • To change a room's outline, levels or centre, use ✎ Edit this room's outline (shape editor). The walk-in route always ends at the room centre, so after moving a room far, draw its route again.
  • Which room a party hunts in is chosen on the Parties tab (one room, several rooms in rotation, or any free room).

#Shape editor (#/edit/<room|zone|spot|area>/<id>)

The shape editor is a full-screen map for changing the outline of one thing the bots hunt in, by dragging its points with a finger or the mouse. It edits four kinds of shapes:

Kind What it is File Opened from
Dungeon room (#/edit/room/<room id>) a room inside a dungeon floor Scripts/data/dungeon_rooms.json Rooms: ✎ Edit this room's outline
Hunting zone (#/edit/zone/<name>) a zone / spot of the Zones and Spots tabs Scripts/data/custom_zones.json Zones: ✎ Drag-edit shape or ✎ Edit a zone's shape; Spots: ✎ Edit a spot's shape
Datapack spot (#/edit/spot/<number>) a spot of the built-in fallback list (made from the game's spawn list) Scripts/data/hunting_spots_h5.json Spots: ✎ Edit a spot's shape
Field area (#/edit/area/<id>) one generated outdoor hunting area (see Field areas) Scripts/data/field_areas.json Zones and Spots pickers

It only changes the shape and a few simple fields (name, levels, on/off, centre, radius, height band, notes). Waypoints, exclusions, pull routes and floors of a zone stay as they are (they are edited in the spot editor and the zone editor).

The pickers on the Zones and Spots tabs (box "✎ Edit a zone's shape" / "✎ Edit a spot's shape"): type in the filter, pick an item and press Edit shape. Items are grouped by file and sorted by level; the marks are ▱ polygon, ○ circle, · rooms (hunts inside dungeon rooms), ✎ edited on the dashboard, OFF. If the dashboard server is older than the shape editor, the list says "The dashboard server does not know the shape editor yet — it needs a restart".

#The screen

  1. ◀ Back: back to the tab you came from (Esc too). With unsaved changes it asks "Leave without saving? Your changes to this shape are lost.".
  2. Title: the kind ("Dungeon room", "Hunting zone", "Datapack spot", "Field area"), the name, and where it is (dungeon · floor, the file, or the field region), plus "· edited on the dashboard" when it was saved here before.
  3. ↶ / ↷: undo / redo (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z). Up to 200 steps.
  4. ⤢: show the whole shape.
  5. ☰: the fields panel.
  6. Save: greyed out until there is a change, and while the outline has an error.
  7. Legend (not shown on phones): this room / zone (red-orange for rooms, green otherwise), others, safe spot (rooms) or "square today" (circles), and the monster colours: grey = more than 3 levels below the item's levels, green = fits, orange = up to 4 above, red = more; "white ring = its own" monsters.
  8. Live numbers: points (or "circle r n"), the area as an equal square ("area ≈ 1721 × 1721"), the monsters inside by level, the share of the item's own monsters that are inside ("own 100 %"), "unsaved", and lines with ✕ errors (cannot save) and ⚠ warnings (can save).
  9. Hint: what you can do now.

What the map shows around the shape:

  • Other rooms / zones / spots / field areas nearby, faint, with name and levels (dashed when they are circles or monster outlines).
  • Monsters from the game's spawn list: bright inside the shape, faded outside, white ring = the item's own monsters, purple crown = raid boss.
  • Safe spots (green shields; yellow = "tight") of the floor or region.
  • Lines: the room's walk-in route (grey, dashed), a field area's walk from its landing (grey), a zone's pull routes (yellow) and waypoints (light blue). Points: the floor entry / landings (blue squares).
  • For zones: its exclusion areas and circles (red), and its sub-areas (dashed light-blue circles "sub-area n").
  • For a circle: the dashed yellow "hunting square today": the square the bots really hunt in now (3 x the radius, at least 9 000 wide).
  • For a datapack spot: its monster outline (dotted purple).

#The tool row

  1. ✎ Points: the normal mode: drag points, add and delete them.
  2. ✥ Move shape: drag anywhere to move the whole shape (a room's centre moves along).
  3. ✕ Point: deletes the selected point (Delete / Backspace key too). At least 3 points stay ("A shape needs at least 3 points.").
  4. ☠ Fit to monsters: replaces the outline with one around the item's own monsters (or, when it has fewer than 3, the monsters of its level range ±3 inside), pushed out a little. It asks first and warns that it ignores walls.
  5. ⌖ Snap: when on, every edit is checked against the geodata, and a point you drag onto rock or a wall is moved to the nearest walkable ground (up to about 320 away), with a message "Point n snapped onto walkable ground (d away).".
  6. Check walls: checks every point and edge against the geodata once.
  7. ☠ monsters, 8. ▱ others, 9. ⛨ safe spots: show or hide those layers.

▱ Make polygon appears instead of the point tools when the item is a circle.

select a point tap it (white, numbered) click it
unselect tap the empty map click the empty map, or Esc
move the view drag the empty map drag the empty map
zoom two fingers (pinch) mouse wheel
move the whole shape ✥ Move shape, then drag the same

The + handles are only drawn on edges that are long enough on screen; zoom in to get more.

  1. The selected point: white, a bit bigger, with its number. 2. ✕ Point can now delete it.

  1. A + handle on an edge. 2. The live numbers show one more point and "unsaved". 3. Undo is active.

  1. ✕ the outline crosses itself (red edges): the crossing edges are drawn red. 2. Save stays greyed out until it is fixed.

  1. ✥ Move shape is on. 2. The hint: "Move shape: drag anywhere to move the whole shape. Two fingers / wheel = zoom."

      1. Monsters, other shapes and safe spots switched off.

#Geodata: Check walls and Snap

  1. Check walls. 2. The result, for example "Geodata: every point is on walkable ground, no edge crosses a wall.", or which points are not on walkable ground (drawn with an orange ring) and which edges cross a wall (drawn orange, dashed). "fine where the outline follows a wall": an outline may touch a wall; an edge that cuts through rock into the next corridor is the problem. Points where the map has no geodata are counted separately.

The check uses the item's height band (a room: its height ±300; a floor zone: its floor; a field area: its height band), so on a tower floor it looks at that floor only. A point counts as walkable when walkable ground is within 48 units; an edge "crosses a wall" when 128 units or more of it in a row have no walkable ground near it.

  1. ⌖ Snap is on (gold). 2. The geodata message. Here point 4 was dragged out of the room: it still stands on walkable ground (so it was not moved), but two of its edges now cut through the wall: they are drawn orange and dashed, and the live numbers warn "2 edges cross a wall".

#The fields panel (☰)

  1. Name (up to 100 characters). For a zone this is its key: renaming is allowed when the new name is free, but a party that chose this spot by name on the Parties tab has to choose it again (the save says so).
  2. Monster levels (rooms) / Levels (the others): 1 - 99, min ≤ max.
  3. Suits party lvl (rooms, field areas): the party levels this place is good for.
  4. Enabled: off = the bots never pick it.
  5. Centre x / y / z (rooms and circles). A room's centre is where the leader walks to and what "is someone in this room" measures; you can also drag the red cross on the map.
  6. Radius (rooms and circles): 100 - 20 000. For a room it is used for "is someone in this room"; for a circle the bots hunt in a square of max(3 x radius, 9 000).
  7. Height band (rooms, field areas): monsters and members outside it do not count. At most 4 000 between the two numbers.
  8. Notes.
  9. ✕: close the panel.

  1. update the room's monster list from the spawns inside the new outline on save (rooms only).
  2. Apply: puts the typed values on the map (changing a field and leaving it does the same).
  3. Levels from monsters inside: sets the levels to the lowest and highest monster inside the shape ("No monsters inside." if none).
  4. ☠ Fit to monsters (as in the tool row). ▱ Make polygon is here too for circles.
  5. Undo all changes: back to the shape as it was when you opened it (asks first when there are changes).
  6. When the bots use it: a note about when the bots pick up a change, then the file name, the id, and "every save keeps a copy in Scripts/data/history/". When the item was saved here before, Reset to generated is shown with the date (see below); otherwise "generated / original shape — your first save marks it manual, so the generator tools keep it".

The "when the bots use it" note in the panel and in the save question can be older than the scripts: current swarm.js versions re-read dungeon_rooms.json, hunting_spots_h5.json and field_areas.json within about a minute after a save, and skip rooms, datapack spots and field areas that are switched off. A party that is hunting there now uses the new shape the next time it picks its spot.

#Saving

Save (or Ctrl+S) first asks, with a summary: "Save dungeon room "name"? — 24 points, area ≈ ..., 11 monsters inside (lvl 47-49), levels 47-49 — Used by every party (the leader hunts only inside this room outline). Marked as edited by hand, so the generator tools keep it. A copy of the file goes to Scripts/data/history/." plus the note about when the bots use it.

  1. ✓ Saved (poly, ...): the list of what changed, warnings after ⚠, and "Recomputing: safe spots of this floor…" when a background job was started. 2. The title now says "edited on the dashboard".

What a save does on the server:

  1. Checks (an error = nothing is written): 3 to 400 points, inside the world, no two neighbouring points on top of each other, no crossing edges, at least 200 x 200 in size, at most 40 000 wide for a room and 80 000 for the others; levels 1 - 99 with min ≤ max; radius 100 - 20 000; height band at most 4 000; a zone name that is not used by another zone; a spot that hunts inside dungeon rooms cannot get an outline ("this spot hunts inside dungeon rooms — edit the rooms on the Rooms tab instead").
  2. Warnings (saved anyway): "the room centre is outside the outline — the leader walks to the centre first"; "the outline moved more than 6000 from the old room centre — the saved walk-in route still ends at the old place"; a renamed zone.
  3. Changed on disk: if the file changed since you opened the shape (a tool, or the same shape saved in another window), you get "changed on disk since you opened it ... — reload and edit again" and the question "Reload the shape from the file now? (Your changes are lost; Cancel keeps them on screen.)".
  4. Writes only that one item, safely (lock, temporary file, rename), in the file's own format. A copy of the whole file goes to Scripts/data/history/<file>_<time>.json (the last 50 are kept).
  5. Marks the item as edited by hand (manual), keeping its original generated values, so the generator tools never overwrite it and Reset to generated can bring the original back.
  6. Derived values: a polygon zone / spot / area gets its centre (average of the corners) and radius (farthest corner); a zone also gets its L2Swarm zone map Settings/zones/<name>.zmap. A room gets its new area and outline quality "manual".
  7. Background jobs: a room whose outline, centre or height band changed gets the safe spots of its floor recomputed (a message reports when it is done); a circle zone that moved or changed size, or got an outline, gets its sub-areas recomputed. A field area's region is only marked; its safe spots are recomputed by the field-area tool.

  1. "Not saved: levels: 1-99, min <= max": the server's reason (red message, stays 15 seconds; ✕ closes it).

Reset to generated (☰ panel, only for items saved here before) asks "Reset "name" to the generated shape and values? The manual mark is removed, so the generator tools may change it again. A history copy is kept." and answers "✓ Reset to the generated shape.".

#Each kind

#Dungeon room

The screenshots above show a room: the room in red-orange, its red cross centre (drag it), the other rooms of the floor, safe spots, the walk-in route and the floor entry. Rooms have Suits party lvl, a Height band and the monster-list option in ☰. Warnings to watch: "n of its own monsters are outside" and "n monsters of other rooms inside" (the outline swallows part of the next room), and "centre is outside the outline".

#Hunting zone: a circle

  1. Centre: drag the red cross to move the zone. 2. Radius handle: drag the yellow handle; its label shows the radius.
  2. ▱ Make polygon: turns the circle into a 12-corner outline the size of today's hunting square.
  3. The hint: "Circle: drag the red centre or the yellow radius handle, or "Make polygon" to draw the exact area."

The dashed circles are the zone's sub-areas: when two of your parties use the same circle zone, each takes one sub-area so they do not hunt on top of each other (made by docs/plan/tools/zone_subareas.js, recomputed after a save here).

  1. "Now a polygon: drag the points to fit. Saving makes the bots hunt only inside it." 2. 12 points.

#Hunting zone: drawn

  1. The title says "Hunting zone (custom_zones.json)". 2. The live numbers.

The zone's exclusion areas and circle (red), pull route (yellow) and waypoints (light blue) are drawn for orientation; edit them in the spot editor or zone editor.

#A spot that hunts inside dungeon rooms

  1. "This spot hunts inside the rooms of dungeon — edit the rooms on the Rooms tab. Here: levels, on/off, notes (☰)."

#Datapack spot

  1. The title: "Datapack spot · region (hunting_spots_h5.json)". 2. ▱ Make polygon.

For a datapack spot Make polygon asks "Start from the monster area of this spot (dotted purple outline)? Cancel = start from the square the bots hunt in today."

#Field area

  1. The title: "Field area · region". 2. The legend. 3. The live numbers (monsters inside, own %).

  1. Levels. 2. Suits party lvl. 3. Height band. 4. Enabled.

"Replace the outline with one around n monster spawns (its own monsters), m points? It ignores walls — check the edges afterwards."

#A wrong link

  1. "not found: id" (or "Nothing to edit: the link needs #/edit/<room|zone|spot|area>/"). The map stays empty; press ◀ to go back (the buttons are shown but do nothing useful).

#Field areas

Field areas are the outdoor version of dungeon rooms. A tool (docs/plan/tools/field_areas.js, run by hand; a full run takes about an hour) splits every outdoor hunting ground into regions (one per gatekeeper landing that leads to a field, for example "Abandoned Camp", "Windy Hill"; plus " outskirts" and "(far)" regions) and each region into areas: groups of monsters of similar level on one piece of walkable ground, with an outline that follows walls, cliffs and water edges from the geodata. The result, Scripts/data/field_areas.json, has about 120 regions and 1 700 areas, each with its levels, the party levels it suits, its monsters (aggressive ones marked), raid bosses nearby, the landing to use and the walk from it, its neighbours and the nearest safe spot.

How the bots use them:

  • You choose them on the Parties tab: open a hunting ground's region map and tap one or more areas; the leader hunts the first and moves on to the next when an area has had no monster for a while (nearest first, or in your order).
  • Automatically: when no custom zone fits, the leader picks the best free field area for the party's level (reachable from a live gatekeeper landing, not too dangerous, not taken by another of your parties) plus its fitting neighbours to rotate through.
  • Plain circle zones: a zone without a drawn area, pull route, waypoints or .town start is hunted as the field areas inside its square.
  • Inside an area the leader only takes monsters inside the outline (and anything that attacks the team); members walk back inside.

You edit an area's outline, levels, height band or on/off state here (#/edit/area/<id>); the field-area tool keeps areas you saved (it never regenerates an item marked as edited by hand). After changing an outline, the region's safe spots are recomputed the next time the tool runs for that region (node docs/plan/tools/field_areas.js --only <region id>).

#Notes and safety

  • Every save asks first and keeps a history copy of the whole file in Scripts/data/history/ (last 50 per file). Reset to generated asks first too.
  • Nothing on this screen sends anything to the game; it only changes data files that the bots read.
  • Keys (desktop): Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y undo / redo, Ctrl+S save, Delete / Backspace delete the selected point, Esc closes the panel, then unselects, then goes back.
  • The background jobs and the server part need a dashboard server that knows the shape editor (Dashboard/server.js with the "POLYEDIT" block); after updating the dashboard files, restart the dashboard server once.

#Gear planner (#/gear)

The Gear tab is the gear planner. For every class (base, 1st, 2nd and 3rd class, Kamael included) and every grade (No-grade, D, C, B, A, S, S80, S84) you choose the item each slot should hold: weapon, shield or sigil, helmet, upper and lower armor (or a full armor), gloves, boots, necklace, two earrings, two rings, belt, bracelet, talisman and cloak. You can choose any item of that grade, including the ones no shop in town sells. The bots read your choices live: they use them on their next gear upgrade, with no restart and no deploy.

New to the words used here (grade, Common item, S.A., set bonus, supply run)? See the glossary. The old per-role Gear tab (2026-10-06) is what you see until the dashboard server has been restarted once; its choices keep working (they show up in the planner as "from the old role choice").

#The page

  1. Class button (phone / tablet) or class list (desktop, left column): every class grouped by race, each class line indented base → 1st → 2nd → 3rd. Next to a class: which of our characters play it now, and a green number = how many grades already have a plan. Type in find a class… to filter by class or character name.

  2. Grade tabs: No-grade, D (20+), C (40+), B (52+), A (61+), S (76+), S80, S84. A green dot = this class has choices at that grade.

  3. Plan box: the paper doll (same as the character page's Equipment box) and one row per slot. Tap a doll cell or a row to choose. Each row shows the chosen item, its grade, its key stats (P.Atk / M.Atk / crit / speed, P.Def / M.Def / shield / MP) and a chip that says how the bots get it:

    Chip Meaning
    Giran 449k · Radia (gold) Sold in Giran (live shop scan): the bots buy it on the next supply run. "(Common)" = the cheap Common twin. "(sword + Change Weapon)" = a Kamael buys the sword and turns it.
    manual · drop … / craft … (grey) No Giran shop sells it: get it by hand (drop, craft, exchange). The chip says where it comes from.
    manual · bots do not buy belts Belts, bracelets, talismans and cloaks are never bought by the bots.
    from Shillien Knight / from the old "sk" role choice (blue) Nothing chosen for this class: it uses its parent class (then the old per-role choice). Choosing here makes it the class's own.
    auto: Full Plate Helmet / automatic Nothing chosen anywhere: the bots' automatic pick.
    real only / Common only The buy rule of that slot (see below).
    +1 alt. Alternatives, tried in order when the first item cannot be bought.

    Greyed rows: no shield for this class, two-handed weapon, full armor: no lower part, nothing at this grade.

  4. if not for sale: what the bots do while a chosen item cannot be bought: buy the auto pick (default) or keep what they wear.

  5. Copy to N similar: copies this class's plan at this grade to every class of the same kind (e.g. Destroyer → Orc Raider + Titan; all healers; all daggers). It asks first and lists the classes. Items a class cannot wear are skipped (it says which).

  6. Clear: removes every choice of this class at this grade (asks first). Choices inherited from the parent class stay.

  7. Our characters: every character of this class (and, dimmed, of its class line) with one small cell per slot: green = wears the planned item (or its Common twin), gold = the bots will buy it, grey = manual, dark = nothing chosen. Tap the name for the character page. "wears C now" = the character's level is in another grade band (the bots buy for their own grade).

#Recommended plan (pre-filled)

Every class has a recommended item for every slot at every grade, worked out from the datapack and the live Giran shop scan (Dashboard/gear_recommend.js). It is shown pre-filled with a teal recommended chip and one line saying why, e.g. "Karmian Tunic set (magic): set bonus cast speed +15%, P.Def +5.3%; sold in Giran 659k for the set (real pieces, for the bonus)".

  • Weapon: the highest damage the class line can use (P.Atk x attack speed x crit; mystics M.Atk). Destroyers two-handed, tanks one-handed + shield, daggers, bows, Kamael ancient sword / rapier / crossbow (bought as the sword and changed). The best S.A. for the role (Acumen / Empower / Mana Up for casters and healers, Focus / Haste / Health for fighters, Cheap Shot for archers ...) is added as an alternative.
  • Armor: the complete SET with the best score for the role: the pieces' P.Def / M.Def / MP plus the set bonus (P.Atk / attack speed / crit for damage dealers, P.Def / CON / shield for tanks, M.Atk / cast speed / INT / WIT / MP for casters and healers). Slots the set does not cover get the best single piece.
  • Jewellery: best M.Def of the grade. Epic boss jewels (Queen Ant, Core, Orfen, Zaken ...) are only an alternative. Belt / bracelet: the best of the grade (manual: the bots never buy them). Talisman / cloak: no recommendation.
  • Availability: what Giran sells wins; a better piece that Giran does not sell becomes the first alternative ("better if you craft / drop it"). Fighters buy the Common twin (1/20 price) unless the set bonus is worth it (C-grade and up); casters and healers buy the real set. Above C nothing is sold in Giran, so B+ recommendations are manual.

Your own choice always wins (gold your choice chip; a different recommendation shows next to it as "rec.: …"). Order the bots use: your choice for the class → its parent classes → the old per-role choice → recommended → their automatic pick. A recommended piece is only bought when it really beats what the character wears, and an unsold recommendation never adds a "needs manual" note.

Buttons: Use recommended (in the picker: removes your choice for that slot), Reset grade to recommended, … all grades (every grade of this class), … all classes (every class; the old per-role choices stay). All of them ask first; the old file is kept in Scripts/data/gear_prefs_history/.

The bots read the recommendations from Scripts/data/gear_rec/<classId>.json; the dashboard rewrites them whenever the item catalog or the Giran shop scan changes (or run node docs/plan/tools/gear_recommend.js).

#Choosing an item (the picker)

A bottom sheet on phones, a side panel on wide screens.

  • Chosen line at the top: the first choice and the alternatives. ↑ = try earlier, ✕ = remove (removing the first choice of a slot without alternatives = back to the automatic pick).
  • find an item… search; sort: best stats (P.Atk with crit and speed for fighters, M.Atk for mystics, P.Def / M.Def for armor and jewellery), Giran price, name.
  • fits / all items: by default only what the class line uses (its weapon types, one- or two-handed, robe / light / heavy armor, shield or sigil). Tap it to see everything the class can equip (race limits and Kamael rules always apply).
  • sold in Giran: only items the bots can buy.
  • S.A. versions (weapons): shows "Berserker Blade - Focus" etc. Normally they are folded under the base weapon ("3 S.A.").
  • buy as: auto (the Common twin for fighters, the real piece for a caster's armor because of the set bonus), real only (e.g. for an S.A. weapon or a set bonus), Common only.
  • Each item row: icon, name, grade, type, stats, and source chips: Giran Common 78k, Giran 1.42M, shop Aden, craft, exchange, drop / boss drop, spoil, S.A. by soul crystal.
  • Tap a row for the details: every Giran offer, other shops with prices, the craft recipe (craft level, success rate, materials, where the recipe drops), exchanges, the monsters that drop or are spoiled for it (level and chance), how to put an S.A. on it, the armor set with its bonus (+ shield bonus and the +6 bonus), Kamael Change Weapon, race limits. Then Choose or Add as alternative. The S.A. buttons choose that S.A. version directly.

#Rules the bots follow

  • A character uses the plan of its own class at the grade of its level; empty slots use the parent class, then the old per-role choice, then the automatic pick.
  • The bots buy only in Giran (supply run / !upgrade). Anything else is manual: !gearplan lists it ("needs manual: Necklace of Seal (craft: …, drop …)") and writes Logs/gear_plan_<name>.json → planned (slot, wanted item, wearing / buy / manual).
  • Wearing any of the chosen items (or the alternatives, or their Common twin, or a Kamael's changed weapon) counts as done.
  • A worn S.A. weapon is never replaced by one of the same grade; enchanted pieces of the same grade stay; the destroyer weapon rule (_weapon, real weapon once the soul crystal is ready) still applies.
  • One earring / ring choice = two of it; a second earring / ring choice = one of each.

#Where it is saved

Scripts/data/gear_prefs.json → "_class": { "<class id>": { "<grade>": { "<slot>": { "id", "alt", "buy", "name", "src" }, "_fallback" } } } plus "_parents" (class tree for the bots). The old { role: { grade: { slot: id, _weapon } } } entries stay untouched. Every save copies the old file to Scripts/data/gear_prefs_history/ (last 200) and writes the new one atomically. Item data: Dashboard/data/gear_catalog.json, rebuilt with node docs/plan/tools/gear_catalog.js (L2J High Five datapack: items, shops, multisells, recipes, monster drops and spoils, armor sets); Giran prices come live from Scripts/data/shopscan_giran.json (re-scan with !shopscan).

#Maps on every page

Scrolling the page over a map scrolls the page (since 2026-10-09). To zoom or move a map, click / tap into it first (gold outline), or use Ctrl + scroll (⌘ + scroll on a Mac) or two fingers. Click / tap outside the map to give the scroll back to the page.

#Accounts (#/accounts)

The Accounts tab lists every account config of the install, lets you create a new character (on a new or an existing account) and move adena and items from one character to another, including old characters that are not in any party.

#Accounts table (#/accounts)

  1. Accounts tab: opens this page.
  2. Login: the account's login name (from the account config Settings/<Login>.xml).
  3. Character: the character the account plays (SelectedCharacter in the config). Tap the gold name to open its character page. "none" = the config has no character yet.
  4. Level / class: from the character's live report. Empty when it has not reported recently. After it the short next level estimate (lvl in 1h25, no exp).
  5. Online: green online when its script reported within the last 30 seconds, grey offline otherwise.
  6. AutoStart: yes when the config is an enabled entry in L2Swarm's AutoStart list (Settings/settings.xml). The staggered login of the PC tab (Start / Restart) opens these accounts one by one.

The whole page, with the two forms under the table:

  1. Accounts table 2. Create a character 3. Transfer adena / items

The table refreshes every 4 seconds. Every .xml in Settings/ is listed except settings.xml itself (and one old duplicate config the install skips). Passwords are never shown anywhere on the dashboard.

#Create a character

  1. Login: the account to use. 3 - 16 letters or digits, starting with a letter.
  2. Password (only for a brand-new account; stored encrypted): fill it in only when no config for this login exists yet. It is stored encrypted in the new config (L2Swarm's own password encryption) and the field is emptied right after you press Create. For an existing account leave it empty.
  3. Start class: Human Fighter, Human Mystic, Elf Fighter, Elf Mystic, Dark Elf Fighter, Dark Elf Mystic, Orc Fighter, Orc Mystic, Dwarf Fighter, Kamael Soldier (male), Kamael Soldier (female).
  4. Sex: Male or Female (for Kamael the start class already decides it).
  5. Name (empty = random): the character name. Empty gives a random fantasy name.
  6. Create: starts it. There is no confirmation.

What happens after Create:

  1. If Settings/<Login>.xml does not exist, the dashboard creates the account config with the password (tool docs/plan/tools/new_account.ps1). Without a password you get "new account: password needed once (it is stored encrypted)".
  2. The account is opened (logged in) in L2Swarm.
  3. A small one-off script is attached to the account. At character select it creates the character with the start class's base stats and keeps trying every 5 seconds (up to 30 minutes) until the account is in game.
  4. Progress lines go to Logs/create_chars.txt ("waiting for character select ...", "CharacterCreate sent", "in game as ...").

  1. The message line: "Name is being created on login - it appears here when logged in", or the error.

The new character is not in a party yet. Add it to swarm.config.json (login, character, party, role) to make it part of the swarm; see Getting started.

#Transfer adena / items

Use it to empty an old character into an active one: everything it carries (or only the adena) goes to a character that is online.

  1. From (any character, also old ones on the accounts): the giver. The suggestions list every character known on the accounts, with its login. Old characters are known once their account has logged in with the current swarm.js (it saves the account's character list to Logs/chars_<login>.json at every login).
  2. To (online character): the receiver. Must be online, and on another account than the giver.
  3. What: everything (adena + every item not worn) or adena only. Worn items and quest items are never given.
  4. Transfer: asks first, then starts.
  5. Log box: the current or last transfer (see below).

The confirmation: "Transfer EVERYTHING (adena + every item not worn) from X to Y? If X is not its account's active character, that account logs out and back in twice." Cancel changes nothing.

#What a transfer does

  1. If the giver is not in game, its account must be logged in with another character. That account's scripts and bot are paused and the running session goes back to character select and picks the giver (the account config is not changed, and the account is never closed or reopened). A dead giver respawns in the nearest village first.
  2. The receiver goes to Giran by its own safe trip (!town giran), the giver with .giran, repeated every 20 seconds. Both must be near the .giran landing within 5 minutes.
  3. Both scripts and bots are paused; the giver walks next to the receiver (they must be within 150).
  4. Trades of up to 10 item stacks each, then one last trade with the adena. Each trade is checked afterwards ("trade 2/5: 10/10 moved").
  5. At the end the receiver's bot and swarm.js are switched back on. A switched account goes back to its normal character, and its bot and swarm.js come back on. If that switch back fails, the log says so in a WARNING line and the account is left with the bot off: retry the transfer or switch by hand, but do not close and reopen the account.

Only one transfer runs at a time (a second one answers "a transfer is already running").

#The log box

  1. The first line is the job: "From -> To (all | adena) - running..." and later "done" or "failed: reason". Below it every step with its time. The step times are UTC (they can differ from the clock in the header by your time zone). "no transfer yet" when nothing ran since the dashboard started.

The same lines are appended to Logs/transfer.log (kept across dashboard restarts).

Typical failures: "To is not online", "From is not in the character index ...", "account ... is not logged in in L2Swarm", "From and To are on the same account", "both did not get to Giran within 5 min", "could not meet".

#How to ...

Add a character to a new account

  1. Fill in Login with the new login and the Password.
  2. Pick Start class, Sex and a Name (or leave the name empty).
  3. Press Create and watch the message line, then Logs/create_chars.txt.
  4. When it appears online in the table, add it to swarm.config.json.

Empty an old character into the party leader

  1. Make sure the old character's account is logged in (with any character) and the leader is online.
  2. Type the old character in From, the leader in To, choose everything.
  3. Press Transfer, read the question, press OK.
  4. Follow the log box. It takes a few minutes (Giran trip + trades).

#Notes

  • Create a character has no confirmation; Transfer asks first.
  • A transfer pauses both characters' scripts and, for an old character, switches the account's character for a while.
  • The password field is only sent once to create the config. It is never stored in plain text, logged or shown.

#Plan (#/plan)

The Plan tab is a reader for the project's own documents: every Markdown file (*.md) in docs/plan/ and its sub-folders (except the tools and zones folders). Use it to read the background documents on a phone, for example the install guide, the Kamael weapon list, the raid log or the dashboard command list.

#Plan documents (#/plan)

  1. Plan tab: opens this page.
  2. Document chips: one chip per document, sorted by name. Sub-folder files show their folder (folder/file.md).
  3. PLAN.md is always the first chip.

Tap a chip to open the document under the chips:

  1. The document, rendered as formatted text (headings, tables, lists, code). If the Markdown renderer could not load (it comes from a public CDN), the plain text is shown instead.

#Every control

Control What it does
Document chip Loads that file from the server (/api/plan?f=<file>) and shows it under the chips. Read only.

There is nothing to save or confirm on this page. The list of chips is read once when the page loads; a new file appears after a reload of the dashboard page.

#Useful documents

File What it is

dashboard_commands.md Every dashboard command.
