#Notes

  • Only .md files inside docs/plan/ can be opened; anything else answers "not found".
  • To change a document, edit the file on the PC; the tab shows the new text the next time you open it.

#PC (#/pc)

The PC tab watches and controls the L2Swarm program on the bot PC: is it running, how much memory it uses, and buttons to start, restart or stop it and to put a new version of swarm.js live. Use it from your phone when the bots stop reporting, when the PC is low on memory, or after you edited the script.

L2Swarm needs administrator rights. The buttons do not start it themselves: they run the scheduled tasks L2Swarm Start, L2Swarm Stop and L2Swarm Restart, which run elevated without a UAC prompt. The tasks are created once by SETUP_PC_ALWAYS_ON.cmd (run as admin, see Getting started). Without them a button answers "... - run SETUP_PC_ALWAYS_ON.cmd once (as admin) to create the L2Swarm tasks".

#L2Swarm program (#/pc)

  1. PC tab: opens this page.
  2. Status: is L2Swarm running, its memory, threads and handles, the PC's free RAM and CPU threads, and whether a newer swarm.js is waiting to be deployed (see Status line).
  3. Start L2Swarm
  4. Restart L2Swarm
  5. Stop L2Swarm
  6. Deploy swarm.js
  7. The limits line: a reminder that every script reload costs memory (see Memory and the limits).
  8. Memory watch: the last 5 lines of Logs/memwatch.log, newest first.
  9. Start/stop + deploys: the last 5 lines of Logs/l2swarm_ctl.log and the last 5 of Logs/deploy_swarm.log, mixed by time, newest first.

The page refreshes every 15 seconds while it is open. The process numbers (memory, threads, handles) are measured by the dashboard server once a minute, so they can be up to a minute old.

#Status line

Look Meaning
L2Swarm running in green: memory is normal. The line shows the memory in GB, "(auto-restart at 4.5 GB)", threads and handles; then "PC RAM free x / total GB · n CPU threads". The orange line under it says Scripts_dev/swarm.js has changes that are not deployed yet.
Orange: L2Swarm uses more than 3 GB.
Red: L2Swarm uses more than 4.5 GB.
L2Swarm is not running (red). "No Scripts_dev copy yet" = there is no Scripts_dev/swarm.js to deploy from.

The same on a phone:

#The buttons

Button Asks first? What it does
Start L2Swarm No Runs the task L2Swarm Start: starts L2Swarm and logs the accounts in one by one (the AutoStart list of L2Swarm is switched off on purpose, because many logins at once are refused by the login server for minutes). Gap between logins: login.gapSeconds in swarm.config.json (8 s if not set; Settings/login_gap.txt wins when present). It closes L2Swarm's empty default account, then checks that everyone got in game and retries the ones that did not. Nothing happens if L2Swarm already runs or another start is busy.
Restart L2Swarm Yes: "Restart L2Swarm? All characters log out and back in (about 1 min)." Runs L2Swarm Restart: Stop, then Start (staggered login again). With many accounts the full login takes longer than a minute.
Stop L2Swarm Yes: "Stop L2Swarm? All characters log out." Runs L2Swarm Stop: ends L2Swarm at once (a hard stop, so no "are you sure?" window waits on the PC), closes the game clients L2Swarm started for in-game characters, and leaves a "stopped on purpose" mark (Logs/l2swarm_stopped.flag) so the memory watch does not start it again by itself. The next Start removes the mark.
Deploy swarm.js Only when it is too soon (see below) Runs docs/plan/tools/deploy_swarm.ps1: copies Scripts_dev/swarm.js over the live Scripts/swarm.js. L2Swarm notices the change and reloads the script on every account.

After a button, the message line under the header shows the answer, and the status is read again after 2 and 17 seconds.

  1. "start sent - status updates in about 15 s".

Before a planned Stop or Restart, send the parties to a town first. Characters left in a hunting ground stay in the world for a while after the program stops, and can die there. Never stop or restart during a raid or Kamaloka.

#Deploy swarm.js

You edit Scripts_dev/swarm.js, never the live Scripts/swarm.js (every write to the live file reloads the script on all accounts at once). When your edits are done, press Deploy swarm.js. The deploy script:

  1. SKIP: no changes when both files are the same.
  2. Checks the syntax (node --check). A syntax error: ABORT: syntax error in Scripts_dev\swarm.js, nothing is copied.
  3. Refuses when the last deploy was less than 15 minutes ago: "ABORT: last deploy n min ago (min gap 15). Batch more edits, or use -Force." The page then asks Deploy anyway? (OK = deploy with -Force).
  4. Refuses during a live raid or Kamaloka ("ABORT: a fight is live (raid_live.json, ...)"), because the reload would end the fight routine.
  5. Refuses while accounts are still logging in after a start ("ABORT: accounts are still logging in ...").
  6. Copies the file: DEPLOYED (force=False) L2Swarm MB=n (the memory at that moment). It is always a live reload; the deploy never restarts L2Swarm.

  1. The deploy script's answer in the message line.

The question shows the deploy script's line, then "Deploy anyway?". OK deploys with -Force, which skips the 15-minute gap and the live-fight and login checks. Cancel deploys nothing.

  1. Refused: a fight is live. Wait until the raid or Kamaloka is over and press the button again.

Every deploy attempt is a line in Logs/deploy_swarm.log, so it also shows in the Start/stop + deploys box.

#Memory and the limits

Every reload of swarm.js costs L2Swarm some memory that it does not give back, so the memory slowly grows while it runs, faster with many deploys. That is why deploys are spaced out and batched.

The memory watch (scheduled task L2Swarm MemWatch, every 2 minutes, docs/plan/tools/l2swarm_ctl.ps1 -Action watch) writes one line per check to Logs/memwatch.log:

2026-10-09 08:11:02 ok   L2Swarm private=2380MB threads=212 handles=5120 pcFree=4100MB commitFree=50300MB

private = L2Swarm's memory, pcFree = free RAM of the PC, commitFree = free memory including the page file. The line starts with WARN above 4.5 GB. Other lines you may see: RESTART ... (it restarted L2Swarm), HIGH ... (live fight ... - no restart), and DEADLOCK ... (L2Swarm stopped answering and was restarted).

What the watch does by itself:

  • It does not restart L2Swarm just because it is big. It restarts only when the PC is about to run out of memory (free commit memory below 3 GB), at most once per 30 minutes, and never during a live raid or Kamaloka unless memory is nearly gone (below 1.5 GB).
  • It starts L2Swarm again when it is not running (after a crash), unless you stopped it with Stop or a start is already running.
  • It restarts L2Swarm when its user interface hangs (MCP stops answering and the scripts stop reporting).

The status colours and the limits line on the page use fixed numbers built into the dashboard: orange above 3 GB, red above 4.5 GB, "(auto-restart at 4.5 GB)", "deploys are refused above 3 GB", and a 20-minute gap in the button's tooltip. The tools themselves use the rules described above (warning line above 4.5 GB, restart only on low PC memory, 15-minute deploy gap, no memory limit on deploys). Read the colours as "how big is it", and the memory watch log as "what will happen".

#How to ...

Put your swarm.js edits live

  1. Save your edits in Scripts_dev/swarm.js (several edits together).
  2. Make sure no raid or Kamaloka is running and the accounts finished logging in.
  3. Open PC, check the orange "changes that are not deployed yet" line, press Deploy swarm.js.
  4. Read the answer: DEPLOYED, SKIP or ABORT with the reason.

Bring everything back after the bots stopped reporting

  1. Open PC. If the status says not running, press Start L2Swarm.
  2. If it runs but the characters do not report, send the parties to town if you can, then Restart L2Swarm and confirm.
  3. Watch Start/stop + deploys: "start: opened ..." lines, then "start: all accounts opened" and "login check round 1: everyone is in game".

#Notes

  • Restart and Stop log every character out. Start and Deploy do not ask.
  • The buttons work from any device that can open the dashboard (on the LAN with the dashboard key).
  • Logs: Logs/memwatch.log, Logs/l2swarm_ctl.log, Logs/deploy_swarm.log.

#Live views

Most dashboard pages show the state of the bots every few seconds. A live view goes further: while something important happens (a raid, a Kamaloka run, a siege, an escape from a fight), the party leader's script writes a small live file every one or two seconds, and the dashboard turns it into a moving picture of the fight. You never have to open a live view yourself: when one starts, a coloured LIVE banner appears under the header on every page, and the matching tab switches to its live layout. Tap Watch on the banner to open it.

Live views only show things. Orders are still given from the normal pages and the command center.

#Which live views exist

Live view When it appears Where Written by Guide page
Raid live view (raid HUD) the party leader is in a raid fight #/live, the Raid bosses tab, the boss page, the red banner the leader, Logs/raid_live.json, every second Raid live view, older layout: live/raid-live.md
Kamaloka live view from the moment a Kamaloka run starts until 15 minutes after it ended the Kamaloka tab, the Parties tab, the banner the leader, Logs/kamaloka_live.json, every second Kamaloka live view
Siege live view a planned fortress or castle siege is running (from the regroup until the result) #/siege/live, the Fortresses / Castles tabs, the banner the main leader, Logs/siege_live.json, every 2 seconds Siege live view
Live party view always (any party, any time) #/live/<leader>, the green Live button on a party card every member's own state file Live party view
Party live states escape from a fight, long casts (Scroll of Escape, .town, resurrection), rescue trips, rotating hunting areas, other players at the spot, the chosen-spot status, hunting pairs inside each party card on the Parties tab each character's Logs/swarm_state_<name>.json, every few seconds Party live states

#How "live" is decided

  • A live file counts as running while it is fresh. The raid and Kamaloka views treat a file older than about 30 seconds as finished (the leader stopped writing it). The Kamaloka view keeps showing a finished run, with its result, for 15 minutes.
  • If the leader's game window freezes, the view stops moving and its "updated" time grows. That is the first sign that something is wrong with the leader's window (see Troubleshooting).
  • The banners and live blocks need no setting: they appear and disappear by themselves.

#A first look at each

Raid live view: the boss with its HP, what it casts and whom it targets, the debuffs on it with the time left, every team member's HP / MP and current action, the minions with the focus target, a map, damage totals and a time-stamped event feed.

Kamaloka live view: the phase steps (travel, entering, rebuff, fighting, loot, done), the boss bar, the team table, the instance map with monsters, the focus target and the path walked, damage and events.

Siege live view: the objectives and their status, the flag or Holy Artifact, enemies seen, every party's members on a close-up map, the countdown to the end of the siege, and the events.

Escape box (party live state): when a character is alone in a fight it cannot win, its row on the Parties tab gets an escape box with a mini map: the monsters on it, which ones are put to sleep or held, the safe spot it runs to, and whether the leader is coming to rescue it.

#Live party view (#/live/<leader>)

The live party view shows one party on a big live map with one live card per member: who has aggro, what each member casts or fights, who is stuck or walking a route, who is selling or buying, and the experience each kill gives. Use it when you want to watch a party closely, for example in a dungeon, during a long walk, or when something looks wrong on the Parties tab. The page only shows things. It never sends an order.

#/live without a leader name is a different page: the raid live view.

#Opening it

  1. Live - the button with the green dot in the header of every party card on the Parties tab. It opens #/live/<leader> for that party. The same button is on the character page (it opens the character's party).

You can also type the address yourself, for example #/live/Aldric. The page updates every 1.5 seconds while it is open and visible. It pauses when the browser tab is hidden or the phone screen is off, and catches up at once when you come back.

#The whole page

  1. Party name - "Live · Party Aldric".
  2. Party menu - switch to another party's live view.
  3. Back - back to the page you came from (the Parties tab when there is none). The Esc key does the same.
  4. Summary line - see Top line.
  5. Live map - see The map.
  6. Zoom and follow - + and − zoom in and out, ◎ follows the party.
  7. Member cards - one per member, the leader first, then the others A to Z. See Member cards.

Layout per device:

Width Layout
Phone (under 700 px) The map on top (about half the screen high), the cards in one column under it.
Tablet (700-1279 px) The map on top, the cards in a grid under it (two or more columns, each card at least 280 px wide).
Desktop (1280 px and wider) A big map on the left (as high as the window; it stays in view while you scroll), the cards on the right in a grid: 2 columns at 1280-1599 px, 3 at 1920 px. On a 1920x1080 screen all 9 cards of a full party fit without scrolling.

There is no separate scroll box for the cards: the whole page scrolls. Tablet and full HD sizes are described here but not shown in a screenshot.

#Top line

The grey line under the title reads, from left to right:

Part Means
7/9 online members that reported in the last 30 seconds / all members
lvl 49–51 lowest and highest level in the party
5 fighting members in combat or with a monster target
5 monsters on the party (red) how many monsters have aggro on a member (shown only when there are some)
1 dead (red) dead members
1 stuck / not moving (red) members that are stuck or should be walking but do not move
updated 10:43:52 the time of the last answer from the dashboard server
monsters: mcp where the monster dots come from: mcp = the leader's game window through L2Swarm. (8 s old) is added when that list has not been refreshed for more than 6 seconds; none = no list

If the dashboard server does not answer, the line says so in red ("dashboard server not reachable ..."). A wrong party name shows "unknown party ...".

#The map

The map uses the same map art as the party map on the Parties tab: the outdoor map, or the dungeon floor the party is on. When you select a member, the floor of that member is shown (useful when members are on different floors).

The whole party (with ◎ on, the map shows everyone):

  1. Pulsing red ring with "Darian stuck 41 s" - the member's walker reports that it is stuck. It re-plans the way by itself.
  2. Green line - the planned walk (route) of a member, from the member to its goal. Small green dots are the waypoints; the part already walked is drawn faint.
  3. Green ring - the next waypoint of that route.
  4. Gold dashed outline - the leader's hunting room, field area or hunting square, with its name ("room: ...", "area: ...", "hunting: ...").
  5. Scale bar - top left, in game units (1.0k = 1,000).

Zoomed in (tap + a few times):

  1. Member dot - a dot in the party colour. The leader's dot is a little bigger and has a ★. A red ring around a dot = fighting.
  2. Gold arc - a cast in progress, drawn on top of the dot. It fills up clockwise until the cast lands.
  3. Orange line - from a monster to a member: that monster has aggro on that member (it targets or hits it).
  4. Yellow dotted line - from a member to its current target.
  5. Dark dot with ✕ - a dead member.
  6. Blue dot - a resting member (sitting to get HP / MP back), label "zZ".
  7. Monster with aggro - a bigger red dot with an orange ring.
  8. Monster - a small red dot. Names, levels and HP % show when you zoom in, and always for monsters with aggro.
  9. Green flag - the goal of a route, with its name (here "Liangma room").

More symbols you may see:

Symbol Means
Pulsing orange ring "not moving 25 s" the member should be walking (a route or a walk order) but has not moved for 20 seconds or more. The dashboard notices this itself, so it also works when the walker does not report "stuck".
Grey dot "(offline)" the member has not reported for more than 30 seconds
Purple monster dot a monster that is held by crowd control (sleep, root ...)
White dashed outline "chosen: ... · travelling" a room or area you chose for the party on the dashboard, which the party has not reached yet
Thin dashed circle in the party colour the leader's combat range
Thin dashed line to a small ring a plain walk to a point (no route)
Yellow dashed line "escape: ..." the way a member runs while it escapes from a fight
Gold dashed circle "♛ " the spawn of the raid boss the party is hunting (raid hunt)
Name labels next to each dot. Close members share one label ("Aldric, Cassius", "Cassius +2"). A label can end with ⚔ (fighting), ⌛ (casting), zZ (resting). Stuck, dead, escaping and selected members always get their own label.
far away: ... (bottom of the map) members more than 20,000 game units from the leader, with the distance

  1. Orange ring - not moving (noticed by the dashboard).
  2. Red ring - stuck (reported by the walker).

Moving around the map:

  • The map is idle until you click or tap into it. While idle, the mouse wheel and a one-finger swipe scroll the page as usual (a short hint says "Ctrl + scroll or click the map to zoom it"; on a Mac "⌘ + scroll"). Ctrl / ⌘ + wheel and a two-finger pinch zoom it even while idle.
  • Click or tap the map to make it active (gold outline; on a phone a hint says "Map active: drag to move, two fingers to zoom. Tap outside the map to scroll the page."). Now drag moves it and the wheel zooms. Clicking outside the map, the mouse leaving it or scrolling elsewhere makes it idle again.
  • + / − zoom in and out at any time.
  • ◎ (green when on) = follow the party: the map keeps every member (within 20,000 of the leader), their next waypoints, the monsters with aggro and the hunting area in view. Moving or zooming by hand turns it off; tap ◎ to turn it on again.
  • Tap a member dot to select it (tap again to unselect). Its card gets a white frame and scrolls into view, and a line at the bottom of the map says what it does, for example "Darian: stuck for 41 s — re-planning (try 2) on the way to Liangma room".
  • Tap a monster to see its name, level, HP, who it has aggro on and whether it is aggressive. Tap empty ground to clear.

  1. Monster info - "Liangma lvl 49 · 88% HP · aggro on Aldric · aggressive".

  1. Selected card - white frame (tapping a card selects the member too; on screens narrower than 1280 px the map scrolls into view).
  2. Highlight on the map - a white circle around the dot.

Legend and help: under the map is a small legend of the symbols, and What does this mean? opens a short explanation of every symbol.

  1. What does this mean? - tap to open or close the help text.

The monsters come from the leader's game window (everything within 12,000 game units, on his floor only, so monsters on the floor above or below are not mixed in). Each member also reports the monsters that target or hit it, so aggro lines show even when the leader's list is missing.

#Member cards

The cards are animated, in the same style as the member cards of the raid live view. From top to bottom (rows that have nothing to show are left out):

  1. Header - class icon, level, name, ★ for the leader, class (or the exp pop-up), exp % in the current level (2 decimals) with the next level estimate under it (lvl in 3h09, no exp 22m), and open › (the member's full character page).
  2. Bars - CP, HP and MP ("CP ?" until the member reports it). They slide smoothly to the new value. The card flashes red when the member lost 3 % HP or more since the last update and green when it was healed. The frame turns orange below 60 % HP and red below 30 %.
  3. What it does right now - the icon of the skill it casts, with a sweep that fills the icon until the cast lands; the icon of a skill it just used (with a short gold glow); otherwise a small activity icon. Next to it one line in plain words (list below, at most 2 lines).
  4. Target - "⚔ monster" with the monster's HP bar and distance (♛ in gold for a raid boss). When it has no target but walks a route: "➜ goal", a green progress bar (point 3/6) and the distance left.
  5. Key skills - up to 7 skills it used or has on cooldown lately (potions and scrolls left out), with the game's dark cooldown sweep and the seconds left. Hover for the name.
  6. Buffs and debuffs - small icons, debuffs first (red frame), then the buffs that run out first, each with a thin time bar (orange and blinking in the last minute); up to 14 icons, then "+n", then "8 buffs · 2 debuffs". An older script only sends the count and the debuff names (chips).
  7. Chips - see the table below.
  8. Last 3 things it tried - time, what, and ✓ done, ✗ failed, … still running. Hover a line (desktop) for the whole text and what the member was doing at the time.

A cast bar appears between rows 3 and 4 while it casts: the skill (or "Teleport .giran"), its target and a bar with the time left; afterwards it stays a few seconds in green (landed) or red (interrupted, refused). Rows that have nothing to show are left out.

With reduce motion on in the device settings, nothing pulses, blinks or slides; the sweeps and bars still show the progress.

  1. Exp pop-up - three kills in a row, summed (see Exp pop-ups).
  2. Cast bar - Bryndis heals Cassius; the bar shows the time left.
  3. Debuff icons - red-framed icons first (here poison and slow), then the buffs.
  4. "2 monsters on me" - red, pulsing chip; hover it for the monster names and levels ("(hits)" = it hits, not only targets).
  5. Stuck chip - "stuck 41 s · re-plan 2"; the card also gets a red frame.
  6. Lost exp - red pop-up "−32,150 exp (−0.25%) died".
  7. Route progress - "➜ Liangma room", point 3/6, 3.6k left.
  8. LEVEL UP! - gold pop-up.

Chips:

Chip Means
3 monsters on me (red, pulsing) monsters with aggro on this member; brighter when one of them hits it
stuck 41 s · re-plan 2 (red) / not moving 25 s (orange) the walker reports stuck / the dashboard sees no movement while it should walk
Buff icon + number (older script only) long buffs on the member (red below 10); hover for the time left on the longest buff
Purple chips (older script only) debuffs on the member (poison, slow ...)
SoE 1 (red) fewer than 2 Scrolls of Escape
shots 80 (red) 100 soulshots / spiritshots or fewer
≈+1.3 %/h · 131 kills/h experience per hour and kills per hour, over the last hour (or since the script started, at least 3 minutes); hover for the exp points. This one counts deaths in; the next level estimate leaves them out

Card colours: the left edge has the party colour (red when 2 or more monsters are on the member). Dead = grey. Not reporting = faded. Stuck = red frame. Selected = white frame. Tap a card (not its link) to select that member on the map; on a phone the map scrolls into view.

What it does right now - the first that fits, in this order:

Line When
not reporting for 5 min — offline or its script stopped no report for more than 30 seconds
dead — waiting for a resurrection / dead — no healer alive dead (the second when no healer of the party is alive and reporting)

"(fund round)" for an adena round. An older script only shows trading with X (giving / receiving).

#Exp pop-ups

Every member reports each change of its experience. The dashboard turns that into a small pop-up next to the exp %:

  1. Gain - green "+3 kills: +3,702 exp (+0.029%)". Kills less than 6 seconds apart are added up ("+3 kills: ...").
  2. Loss - red "−32,150 exp (−0.25%) died". Exp was lost (by death; "died" is added when a death caused it).
  3. Level up - gold "LEVEL UP! +1,410 exp (lvl 51 +0.42%)". The % is then the part of the new level.

Details:

  • The % is the share of the current level: 2 decimals from 0.1 %, 3 or 4 decimals for smaller amounts.
  • A gain right after a resurrection ends in "res" (exp given back by the resurrection).
  • The pop-up shows for about 6 seconds after your browser first sees the change, floats up and fades. A change older than 15 seconds when your browser first sees it is not shown (so opening the page does not replay old kills). Nothing shows for a member that is not reporting.
  • Hover the pop-up with the mouse to see each single change with its time and the monster names.
  • With reduce motion switched on in your phone or computer settings, the pop-up does not move, it only fades.
  • Where it shows: on the live cards (it takes the place of the class name, so the name stays readable), on the Parties tab member rows (it floats to the left of the exp %) and on the character page.

The ≈ %/h chip on the cards adds all gains and losses of the last hour.

#How to ...

Watch what a party does in a dungeon

  1. Open the Parties tab and tap Live on the party card.
  2. Leave ◎ on (green): the map follows the party.
  3. Read the cards from the top: the leader first. Red chips and red frames need attention.

Find out why a member does not come

  1. Look for a red ring ("stuck") or an orange ring ("not moving") on the map, or a red line in the summary.
  2. Tap the member's dot. The line under the map and its card say where it is going and for how long it is stuck.
  3. Check Last 3 things it tried on its card for a failed step (✗).
  4. To act, open its full page with open › and use the orders there (see the character page and the override menu).

See which monster is on whom

  1. Find the orange lines on the map: each goes from a monster to the member it is on.
  2. Tap a monster: the line under the map lists everyone it has aggro on.
  3. The red chip "n monsters on me" on a card lists the names.

#Notes

  • The page reads one batch per refresh from the dashboard server (/api/live?party=<leader>): every member's live state file (Logs/swarm_state_<name>.json, written by swarm.js every 2 seconds), the last steps of its intent log (Logs/intent_<name>.log) and the monsters around the leader from L2Swarm (cached for 3 seconds). Buff icons and key-skill cooldowns come from the same state files (fields buffList and ov).
  • Exp pop-ups, aggro lists, CP, debuffs, "healing X" and target lines need a swarm.js that reports them. Routes and "stuck" need a walker that publishes its route. With an older script the page still works; those parts are just empty.
  • The plain-words activity line comes from Dashboard/activity.js, which the Parties tab member rows and the character page use too, so all three say the same thing.
  • Nothing on this page sends anything to the game.

#Raid live view (raid HUD) (#/live)

The raid live view shows a raid fight while it runs: the boss and its HP over time, the debuffs on it, every team member's skills, cooldowns and buffs, a map, the minions, the boss's drop list, an event feed and the damage numbers. Use it to watch a raid as it happens and, when needed, to give one member a one-time order with Act (the override menu).

It shows up by itself while a raid runs:

Where What
Live banner at the top of every page a red bar "LIVE raid: boss · HP · alive · clock · Watch ›". Tap it to open #/live.
#/live the full view (this page). Without a running raid it says "No raid is running right now. This page shows the fight as soon as one starts."
Raid bosses tab the same view above the boss table (inside the raid hunt box while a raid hunt is fighting)
Boss page #/raid/<id> the same view at the top of the page
Parties tab the live block at the top

A raid counts as running while the leader's live file is younger than 30 seconds. When the fight ends, the view disappears by itself (an open Act panel closes too). The rules the bots follow in a raid are described in Raid bosses; the older description of the live raid block is in the live raid page. Words such as focus, minion and aggro are in the glossary.

The view refreshes every second. The information is the same on every device; only the layout changes.

#The whole view

  1. LIVE raid: - with a pulsing red dot.
  2. Clock, phase, age, leader - "⏱ 4:06 · killing minions (3 left) · 1s ago · leader Aldric": time since the raid started, the phase the leader reports (for example waiting for the tank, killing minions, on the boss), how old the data is and the party leader.
  3. Totals chips - see Top line.
  4. Boss - see Boss.
  5. Debuffs on the boss - see Debuffs on the boss.
  6. Map - see Map.
  7. Team - one card per member, see Team cards.

The whole page, top to bottom:

  1. Boss 2. Debuffs 3. Map 4. Team 5. Minions 6. Drops 7. Event feed 8. Damage 9. Damage log (folded until you open it).

#Layout per device

The layout follows the width of the view itself (not of the screen), so the same view also fits inside the boss page and the Raid bosses tab.

Width of the view Layout
Phone (under 720 px) One column: Boss, Debuffs, Team, Map, Minions, Drops, Event feed, Damage, Damage log.
Tablet (720-1149 px) Two columns: Boss over the full width; Debuffs + Minions; the Team over the full width; Map + Event feed; Drops; Damage + Damage log.
Desktop (1150 px and up) The raid HUD: Boss over two columns + Debuffs; Map and Minions on the left, the Team (cards side by side) on the right; then Drops, Event feed, Damage; the Damage log at the bottom.
Full HD (1560 px and up) Four columns: as desktop, and the Event feed runs down the right edge the whole height.

Every section folds: tap its title (the small ▸ turns). Your choice is remembered in this browser (the Damage log starts folded).

  1. Folded section - only the title shows.
  2. Open section.

#Top line

Chip Means
8/9 alive living members / all; green when everyone is alive, red otherwise
✝ 2 deaths / 0 deaths deaths this fight (from the leader's event list)

UD ×1 the tank's Ultimate Defense uses
0 potions potions used by the team (only when the members report their skill / item use)
⚔ 225k · 913/s damage the team logged and damage per second
clearing: 3 left before the pull: monsters still to kill inside the clear area (see Raid fight area)

#Boss

  1. Boss name - gold when the boss is the team's current focus target. Red chips after it are boss states the leader reports.
  2. HP bar.
  3. HP line - the boss's HP since the raid started. "HP line: collecting…" until there are two points.
  4. On the boss - time since the raid started.
  5. Kill in ≈ - time left at the speed of the last 60 seconds ("—" while the HP does not drop).
  6. Party DPS - all damage the team logged ÷ fight time.
  7. Aggro on - who the boss attacks. Green name + "tank ✓" = the tank holds it; red name + "NOT the tank" = it is on someone else; "nobody (idle)" = no target. "· from its hits" = known from the boss's attacks (the game does not tell us its target directly).
  8. Boss now - the skill it is casting right now; a red AoE 150 chip = it hits an area (radius in game units). "not casting" otherwise.
  9. Boss skills - its last 8 skills, newest first: time, icon, name and target.

#Debuffs on the boss

  1. One debuff card - icon, name, level, who cast it, its type (for example Defense ↓, Poison, Death Mark, Melee res. ↓), what it does in numbers ("P.Def −23%") and a bar with the seconds left.
  2. n active - debuffs on the boss now (not counting resisted ones).
  3. Debuff casts this fight - every debuff each member cast at the boss, with counts.

More:

  • Debuffs of the same type replace each other on the boss. The older one is shown faded: "replaced by ... — same type".
  • ✕ resisted: (red) lists casts the boss resisted, with the caster.
  • When the members do not report counts, the line reads "Recent debuff casts" (icon, skill, caster, seconds ago).
  • The game server does not send the effects on a monster, so a debuff only shows when the caster reports it. "Nobody in this party has put a debuff on the boss" means none of them cast one (for example a party without a necromancer or a Shillien Saint).

#Team cards

Every card has the same rows in the same place, so the bars line up across the grid:

  1. Number - the same number as on the map, in the role colour (blue tank, green healer, gold melee, white caster, grey dead). Next to it: class icon, name, level and class.
  2. SS and DMG - SS = soulshots / spiritshots in the bag (● green = auto-use on and some left, ○ red = off or empty, "shots ?" = unknown). DMG = damage dealt this fight; hover for hits, critical hits, the biggest hit and the damage taken.
  3. Act - opens the override menu for this member.
  4. HP / MP / CP bars - CP shows "CP ?" until the member reports it. The bars glide to new values. The card flashes red when the member lost 3 % HP or more since the last refresh, green when it was healed by 3 % or more.
  5. Doing now - the skill it casts (the icon gets a progress ring while the cast runs, and the seconds left), the target (green when it is a teammate), "hits " for melee hits (⚔), or "✝ dead". "◀ 3 monsters" / "◀ " (red) = monsters attacking this member.
  6. Key skills - its most used skills this fight (up to 6, potions left out) with a cooldown sweep like the game's skill bar: a dark sector and the seconds until the skill is ready. The small number in the corner = how often it was cast. Hover for the reuse time.
  7. Buffs / debuffs - buff icons (a red frame = a debuff on the member) and the count ("8 · 1 deb"). Without a buff list: debuff chips and a chip "12 buffs · 650 min" (green from 10 buffs).
  8. Role line - depends on the role:
    • tank: "✓ holds the boss" or "✗ boss is on " or "boss idle" · monsters on him · Ultimate Defense uses
    • destroyer: "↓ draining HP for Frenzy" / "Frenzy / Zealot up" / "Frenzy not up"
    • healer: number of heals and the last one (skill → target at its HP %, time), or "no heal yet this fight"
    • doomcryer: chants cast with counts, or the last chant, or "no chant seen this fight"
    • everyone else: the 3 most used skills with counts
    • "✝ died ×n" and "res ×n" come first when they happened.
  9. Damage bar - its share of the best damage dealer, the damage and the damage per second.
  10. A dead member - grey, "✝ dead", HP bar empty.

The member that holds the boss's aggro has a pulsing red frame. The HP colours: orange below 60 %, red below 30 %.

One card close up:

  1. SS - shots in the bag, green dot = auto-use on.
  2. DMG - damage dealt.
  3. Cast icon - with the progress ring while casting.
  4. Cooldown sweep - seconds until ready.
  5. Healer role line - heals and the last heal.

How the cooldowns are known: from the datapack's reuse time of each skill and the last time the dashboard saw the member cast it. When the member reports its own skill timers (the same data the override menu uses), those win.

#Map

Centred on the boss, on the game's own map art (underground maps for deep dungeons). The map only grows during a fight, it never jumps back.

  1. Boss - big circle with a red HP ring and its HP %.
  2. Yellow ring - the team's focus target.
  3. Minion - orange dot with "HP% name" above it.
  4. Other monster - purple dot (a monster that is not the boss's minion but fights us).
  5. Red line - a monster hits that member.
  6. Green dashed line - a heal or buff on a teammate.
  7. Purple dashed line - a debuff cast.
  8. Dead member - grey dot with ✝.
  9. Scale bar - 500 game units.
  10. Numbered names - member number, colour and name (dead members struck through).
  11. Key - the line and dot colours.

More lines: blue = a member hits (melee), dashed orange = a damage spell. Dashed circles = an area skill landing, with its real radius (red when the boss casts it). Member dots are numbered in their role colour; an orange outline = HP under 60 %, red = under 30 %. Names are placed so they never overlap.

#Raid fight area on the map

When a raid fight area is set for the boss (or the leader reports one), the map also shows it and grows to fit it:

  1. Fight area - orange outline: where the team fights; the tank pulls the boss into it.
  2. Clear area - a yellow band around the fight area (the automatic margin), or a yellow dashed outline when a clear area was drawn by hand: only monsters inside it are killed before the pull.
  3. Stage point - blue flag: where the team waits before the pull.
  4. Key - "fight area", "clear area" and "stage" are added to the line key.

Before the pull, monsters still to clear show as yellow rings (red for aggressive ones), and the top line shows "clearing: N left".

#Minions

  1. ▶ focus - the minion the team kills now (gold). Each row: name, HP bar, its target ("→ Aldric" in red, or "idle") and the skill it casts.
  2. Dead minions - "✕ name ×2".
  3. Other monsters on us - monsters that are not minions but hit the team (purple names).

The section title says "3 alive · 2 dead".

#Drops

  1. Rate line - the datapack chances are multiplied by the server's drop rate (×1.5). Full boss page › opens the boss page with the complete table.
  2. Group - Equipment, Recipes, Scrolls / books, Materials / other, Adena.
  3. Chance bar - the chance after the rate, with the count range left of it. Hover a row for the drop group, "one item of the group drops", spoil, the datapack chance and what the item is useful for.
  4. Gold ×n - we already got this item from this boss (that many in total).
  5. Our last kill - what each character got at our last kill of this boss (right after a kill this is the fight that just ended), and how many kills are recorded.

The section title shows the boss level. Bosses that are not in the datapack list say "This boss is not in the datapack list (no drop table)". The drop list is loaded once per boss; our own loot (Logs/raid_loot.log) is re-read every minute.

#Event feed

  1. Filter buttons - Events, Heals, Skills, Boss: each switches one kind on or off (remembered in this browser).
  2. Death (red) - "DIED: ".
  3. Heal (green) - healer, skill → target (target HP % at the time), from the heal log.
  4. Boss skill - the boss's casts with their target.

Newest first, up to 80 lines, each with its time. Other colours: resurrections ("back up: "), minion kills (gold), the final result, and warnings such as "RESISTED" or "interrupted" (orange). A heal shows once (from the heal log), not again as a skill.

#Damage and damage log

  1. Damage per member - name, bar (share of the best), damage, share of the team in % and damage per second.
  2. 🛡 damage taken.
  3. Damage log - the last 40 hits, newest first: who hit whom, the damage, and CRIT for critical hits. Folded by default; tap the title to open it.

#Act (override)

Act on any team card opens the override menu for that member: cast one of its skills, use a potion or scroll, target, attack, stop, move to the tank or boss, or resurrect a dead teammate, once, even in the middle of the fight.

#Kamaloka

The Kamaloka live view uses the same team cards (with the same Act menu) for its Team section.

#How to ...

Check that the tank holds the boss

  1. Look at Aggro on in the Boss panel: green "tank ✓" is good.
  2. On the team cards, the member with the pulsing red frame has the boss's aggro.
  3. The map shows a red line from the boss to that member.

Make a healer heal someone right now

  1. Tap Act on the healer's card.
  2. Pick the target in on (a teammate), tap the heal skill, then Do it.
  3. Watch the toast at the bottom for the answer. See override menu.

See what the boss can drop

  1. Open the Drops section.
  2. Gold ×n chips mark items the team already got from this boss.
  3. Tap Full boss page › for the full table.

#Notes

  • Everything comes from Logs/raid_live.json (written by the party leader's window every second during a raid), the members' own Logs/swarm_state_<name>.json, Logs/raid_heals.log, Logs/raid_loot.log and the datapack. The dashboard adds them together in /api/raidlive.
  • Skill casts per member, potions, CP and the HP line need a swarm.js that writes them. Without them the view still works: it builds a short skill history from what it sees every second, and samples the boss HP itself.
  • The only thing on this page that sends anything is Act (it always asks with Do it first).

#Raid live view

The current raid live view (raid HUD, every section explained) is described in Raid live view (raid HUD).

This page explains where the live raid view appears and how to get to it. What every part of the view shows (boss, debuffs, map, minions, drops, team cards, event feed, damage, the Act button) is explained section by section in Raid live view (raid HUD).

While a party fights a raid boss, its leader writes Logs/raid_live.json every second: the boss, its minions, the team, the debuffs on the boss, the boss's casts, damage numbers and a running list of events. The dashboard turns that into the live raid view. It counts as running while the file is younger than 30 seconds; when the fight ends the view disappears by itself. Words such as focus, minion, aggro and raid curse are in the glossary. The raid rules the bots follow are described in Raid bosses.

Where you see it:

Where What
Live banner at the top of every page a red bar "LIVE raid: boss · HP · alive · clock · Watch ›"
#/live (tap the banner) the full live page
Raid bosses board a red LIVE strip pinned on top (Watch / Party view buttons)
Parties tab the live view at the top, under the raidhunt line
Boss page #/raid/<id> of that boss a LIVE fight box with the live view at the top of the page

The live page, the Parties tab and the boss page show the same view, refreshed every second.

#The banner and the Parties tab

  1. Live banner - pulsing red dot, LIVE raid: , boss HP %, members alive / party size, fight clock, Watch ›. Tap it to open #/live. It is shown on every page except the live page itself (a Kamaloka run has its own banner next to it).
  2. Live view on the Parties tab - the same view as on #/live, above the party list.

#The live page (#/live)

The tab bar keeps Raid bosses highlighted.

  1. LIVE raid: .
  2. Clock, phase, age, leader - fight time since the raid started, the phase ("waiting for the tank / destroyers", "killing minions (3 left)", "on the boss"), how many seconds ago the leader wrote the file, and the party leader.
  3. Totals chips - alive / party size, deaths, resurrections, heals, Ultimate Defense, potions, total damage.
  4. Boss - HP, target, casts.
  5. Debuffs on the boss - one card per debuff our casters put on it, with time left; resisted ones listed apart.
  6. Map - the fight around the boss.

Further down: minions, drops, team cards, event feed, damage and damage log. Each part is explained in Raid live view (raid HUD).

Without a running raid the page says "No raid is running right now. This page shows the fight as soon as one starts." - leave it open and the fight appears by itself:

#On the Raid bosses board and the boss page

  • Raid bosses board: a red LIVE strip is pinned on top with the boss HP, Watch and Party view (picture).
  • Boss page of the boss being fought: a LIVE fight box at the top of the page (picture).

#How to follow a raid from your phone

  1. Open the dashboard; when a fight starts, the red LIVE raid banner appears on every page.
  2. Tap Watch ›.
  3. Watch the boss HP and the phase; check that the boss targets the tank, that the healers heal, and that no member runs out of shots.
  4. The event feed tells you about deaths and resurrections. You do not need to do anything: the party fights until the boss or the last member dies (no escape in raids), then loots. The result ends up in the fight reports.

#Notes

  • To stop a raid, send !stop to the party from the Command center. One member can be given a one-time order with Act in the live view (override menu).
  • HP and MP of the other members come from each member's own report (every few seconds), so they can lag a little behind the leader's view.
  • If the raid view script (Dashboard/raidlive.js) cannot load, the dashboard falls back to a simpler, older live block with the same data.
  • A Kamaloka run uses the same kind of live view on the Kamaloka tab: see Kamaloka live view.

#Kamaloka live view

While a party runs a Kamaloka, the dashboard shows the run live: which step the run is at, every character's HP, MP and what it is doing, a map of the instance with the team and the monsters, who deals and takes how much damage, and a running list of events. It appears by itself as soon as a leader starts a Kamaloka (from the Run button, a command, or the daily switch). You do not have to do anything. For the list of Kamalokas, Run buttons and the daily switch, see the Kamaloka tab.

Where you see it:

Where What
Kamaloka tab (#/kamaloka) The full live block at the top of the tab. The running Kamaloka is selected in the list and gets a LIVE chip.
Every other page A red LIVE Kamaloka banner under the header. Tap it to go to the Kamaloka tab.
Parties tab (#/parties) The same full live block, above the parties, plus the banner.
After the run (15 minutes) A short "Run over" summary on the Kamaloka tab.

How it works: during the run the party leader writes Logs/kamaloka_live.json every second. The dashboard reads it every second while the Kamaloka tab is open or a run is on (every 3 seconds otherwise, to notice a new run). A run counts as live while the file is less than 30 seconds old; the summary stays for 15 minutes after the end. The words anchor, focus and aggro are explained in the glossary.

#The live block on the Kamaloka tab

#Header, steps, boss and team

  1. LIVE Kamaloka: - the instance being run (the red dot pulses).
  2. Time, alive, killed, age - time since the leader started (travel included), how many characters are alive out of the team, how many monsters died inside, and how old the last update is ("1s ago"; it should stay at a few seconds).
  3. Phase steps - Travel -> Enter -> Rebuff -> Fight -> Loot -> Done. Past steps are green, the current one is gold. Right after entering, Rebuff lights up (the instance removes every buff, the team rebuffs from the Community Board).
  4. Leader task - what the leader's script is doing right now, in its own words (for example "instance: focus Lost Captain (3 on us)").
  5. Boss bar - appears when the boss is in view: name, who it attacks (red arrow), what it casts ("casting NPC Mortal Blow") and its HP. It gets a gold frame while it is the team's focus target.
  6. Low HP row - the team table puts the lowest HP first. A red left edge = under 30 % HP, orange = under 60 %.
  7. Dead row - dead characters sit at the bottom, dimmed, with "dead" in the Doing column.
  8. hit by - which monster is hitting this character ("hit by Lost Watcher"; "3 monsters on them" when there are more than two).
  9. From spot - how far the character stands from the team's spot (the anchor). Over 700 it turns red with "away!": that character has strayed and may pull more monsters.

The team table has one row per character: role colour dot (blue tank, green healer, white damage dealer, grey dead), name and role, HP and MP bars, Doing now (the last attack or skill and its target, for example "Greater Heal -> Cassius", "hits Lost Captain"), and From spot. On a phone the table is wider than the screen; swipe it sideways for the last two columns:

  1. Doing now - attack or skill and its target.
  2. From spot - distance from the anchor.
  3. hit by - monsters on this character.
  4. away! - too far from the team's spot.

#Map and monsters

  1. Live map - the instance's own map art, zoomed on the team. It grows at once when someone or something comes into view (up to 3500 from the team's spot) and shrinks back slowly, so it does not jump. Dots move smoothly.
  2. Team spot (anchor) - the dashed gold circle is the spot the team holds while the tank pulls.
  3. Focus target - the monster with the gold ring is the one every damage dealer is told to hit.
  4. Team path - the solid gold line is where the leader walked since he entered.
  5. Overview (Labyrinths only) - a second, small map of the whole Labyrinth under the live map: entry, rooms, mini-boss, boss, and the team's position and path on it.
  6. Legend - red line = a monster attacks this character, blue dashed line = we attack that monster, orange dot = monster, gold = team path and spot.
  7. Focus monster - in the monster list the focus target is first, gold, with a triangle.
  8. Dead monsters - names of the monsters that died in view, with a count ("Lost Beholder x5").

Symbols on the live map:

Symbol Meaning
Blue / green / white dot with a name Tank / healer / damage dealer. A thick orange ring = under 60 % HP, red ring = under 30 %.
Grey dot with a cross before the name Dead character.
Orange dot with a percentage Monster and its HP.
Big red dot with name and percentage The boss.
Small grey dot A monster that died.
Gold ring around a monster Focus target.
Red line A monster is attacking that character.
Blue dashed line That character is attacking that monster.
Dashed gold circle The team's spot (anchor).
Solid gold line The leader's path in this run.

The monster list (right of the map on a desktop, under it on a phone) shows up to 14 living monsters: focus first, then the boss, then monsters that attack someone. Each row: name, HP bar, who it attacks and what it casts.

  1. Monsters - how many are alive in view and how many died.
  2. Focus monster - first in the list.
  3. Casting - the skill a monster is casting right now.
  4. Dead monsters - with counts.

#Damage, damage log, events

  1. Damage - damage dealt per character since the run started, biggest first, as a bar and a number (k = thousands).
  2. Damage taken - the number with the shield.
  3. Damage log - the last 12 hits: time, who hit whom, how much. Yellow numbers are damage we dealt, red numbers damage we took.
  4. CRIT - a critical hit.
  5. Events - the last 14 events, newest first: start, travel, "talking to Captain ...", "inside the instance", rebuff, "goes in first", "FULL AGGRO", "room clear", "killed: ...", "boss in sight", "focus: ...", "DIED: ", "back up: ", "BOSS DOWN" and the final "RESULT".

The whole block at once (desktop):

#The running Kamaloka in the list

  1. LIVE - the red chip next to the Kamaloka being run. When a run starts, the tab selects it, so the detail panel below shows its map and facts.

#Before the team is inside

#Travelling

From the start until the leader talks to the captain the step is Travel. The map shows the whole instance (nobody is inside yet), and a line says where the team is.

  1. Current phase - Travel.
  2. Not inside yet - "Not inside yet - (, ). The map shows the instance." This is also where you see "kamaloka: waiting for the team at Captain ...: " when the leader waits for teammates at the captain.
  3. Whole instance map - the layout with entry, rooms, mini-boss and boss, without the team.
  4. Monsters - "0 in view" until the team is inside.

#Entering

The step Enter lights up when the leader talks to the captain.

  1. Enter - the current phase.
  2. Leader task - "kamaloka: talking to Captain Gosta".
  3. Events - start, travel, "team in Heine - walking to Captain Gosta", "talking to Captain Gosta".

If entry fails the run ends at once and the summary shows why (for example "not entered: could not enter - server said: #2100 ...", "team not with the leader - not entered", "could not get to ", "the team did not come in - leader left").

#Run over: the summary

When the run ends (cleared, wiped, timeout, stopped, or not entered), the live block turns into a short summary for 15 minutes. It never shows the old inside picture as if the team were still there.

  1. Result - "Run over: - cleared" (green frame and chip when cleared, red otherwise).
  2. Ended, lasted, killed - end time and how many minutes ago, how long the run took (travel included), monsters killed.
  3. Not in the instance - "The team is not in the instance any more." If the boss was still alive, its last HP is added ("The boss Lost Captain was at 37 % when it ended").
  4. Deaths - who died during the run, with the time.
  5. Team at the end, the path and the last events - tap to open the details.

  1. Team at the end - the team table as it was when the run stopped ("At the end" column).
  2. The path - the whole instance with the path the leader walked.
  3. Last events - the event list of the run, newest first, ending with "RESULT: ...".

A run that did not clear looks like this:

  1. wiped - red chip and red frame (any result other than "cleared").
  2. Boss HP - "The boss Lost Captain was at 37 % when it ended."
  3. Deaths - everybody, in the order they died.

A wipe does not use up the day: the server only locks a Kamaloka when its boss dies (the daily switch still allows only two tries per Kamaloka per day).

After the run, the list's Today column and the run history update by themselves (a new result appears in Run history).

#The live banner on other pages

On every other page a red banner sits under the header while a run is on.

  1. Banner - "LIVE Kamaloka: ", the current step (Travel, Enter, Rebuff, Fight, Loot), alive out of the team, run time.
  2. Watch > - tap the banner to open the Kamaloka tab with the live block.

If a raid fight is live at the same time, the raid banner is shown above it (see Raid live view).

#The Parties tab during a run

The Parties tab shows the whole Kamaloka live block above the party cards, so you see the run without switching tabs.

  1. Banner - as on every page.
  2. Live block - the same as on the Kamaloka tab (header, steps, boss, team, map, monsters, damage, events).

#Notes

  • Read only: the live view has no buttons that send anything. To stop a run, send !mission stop (or !stop) to the leader; the view closes with the result "stopped" about 15 seconds later.
  • Only the leader writes the file. If the leader's script stops, the view stops updating; after 30 seconds without an update it disappears (the "age" in the header tells you how fresh it is).
  • Learning the map: at the end of every run the leader adds the monster positions he saw inside to Logs/kamaloka_map.json, and keeps the run's path. The detail panel then shows them for that Kamaloka.
  • Damage numbers come from each character's own system messages ("You hit for ..."), collected by the leader. A character whose script is not running reports nothing.

#Siege live view

Route: #/siege/live. Also: the red LIVE siege banner on every page, and a compact live box on the Fortresses / Castles tabs.

While a siege mission runs, its main leader (the plan's Command Channel leader) writes what he and the other party leaders see to Logs/siege_live.json every 2 seconds. This page draws it, a bit like the raid live view: the phases, the objectives with their status, who has the flag, where everyone stands, the enemy players seen, and an event log. It starts showing at the very first phase (the regroup in Giran), not only when the fighting starts.

The page asks the dashboard for new data every 2 seconds. A siege counts as running while its phase is not "done" and the file is at most 30 seconds old. A finished siege stays visible as Last siege for 30 minutes.

Like everything about sieges, the live view has not been seen in a real siege yet. The screenshots use a demo siege.

#The banner (every page)

While a siege runs, a red banner appears under the header on every page except the live page itself.

  1. LIVE siege: .
  2. Phase - for example "Siege: objectives".
  3. Objectives done - "1/10 objectives" (gates, commanders, command center, flag; other NPCs are not counted).
  4. Alive - our characters alive / in the siege. A ⚑ item appears when one of us holds the flag, and ⏱ shows how long the mission has been running.
  5. Watch › - tap the banner to open the live view.

The banner check runs every 2 seconds on the siege pages and while a siege runs, otherwise every 8 seconds.

#Compact box on the Fortresses / Castles tabs

  1. Phase timeline (see below).
  2. Flag box (fortress) or Holy Artifact box (castle).
  3. Summary - objectives done, alive count, time left (or "siege starts in ...").
  4. Watch › - opens the live view.

#No siege running

  1. "No siege is running right now. This page shows it as soon as a siege mission starts (the regroup in Giran included)."

#A fortress siege in progress

  1. Title - "LIVE fortress siege: " (or castle siege).
  2. Status line - ⏱ time since the mission started, the main leader's current step, the time left of the siege ("ends in 51:20") or the countdown before it ("siege starts in 12m"), how old the data is ("1s ago"), and RESULT at the end.
  3. Phase timeline - Regroup in Giran · Travel · Regroup outside · Waiting for the start · Siege: objectives · Flag / artifact · Done. Green = done, gold = now, grey = still to come.
  4. Flag box - who holds the Combat Flag, the carrier and backup from the plan, and whether the command center is open.
  5. Live close-up map.
  6. Objectives + Enemies seen.
  7. Parties - one box per party.
  8. Events - the last 14 events, newest first.

#Phases

Phase What happens
Regroup in Giran every chosen party goes to Giran (the normal regroup)
Travel town, gatekeeper landing nearest the regroup point, then walking there
Regroup outside each leader waits for his team; the main leader waits up to 15 minutes for the other parties and opens the Command Channel
Waiting for the start until the server's start message or the planned time; a rebuff 4 minutes before
Siege: objectives gates, commanders (fortress) or gates and Control Towers (castle)
Flag / artifact the carrier takes the flag to the pole, or the clan leader engraves the Holy Artifact; everyone escorts him
Done the result is written; everyone stops and waits for orders

#The live map

The close-up of the target (see Close-up map) with the live state on top:

Marker Meaning
Red circle C1 ... a commander; grey with ✕ = dead. "→ party X" under it = the party assigned to it
Blue / green bar a gate: blue = closed, green = open or destroyed
Orange dot another fortress NPC seen within 4000 (guard, archer, healer ...); dark = dead
Purple dot an enemy player; dark = dead
Dot in a party colour one of our characters (grey = dead). Hover for name, party and HP
Pulsing yellow ring "⚑ " the Combat Flag and who holds it
Green ✚ the regroup point

#Objectives and enemies

  1. ▶ focus row - an objective a party is attacking now, with an HP bar and the party it is assigned to.
  2. Done - green "✓ dead", "✓ destroyed" or "open".
  3. Closed - an orange "closed" gate. A red alive = a commander or tower still standing; grey "unknown" = not seen yet (too far away or behind a wall).
  4. Enemies seen - red chips with each enemy clan and its head count, then the names (✝ = dead). Only players near the target who are not in our clan are listed. The bots never attack them.

The list has: every outer gate (with its HP when known), every commander C1-C4 (fortress) or Control Tower (castle), the command center, "Raise the Combat Flag" (waiting / held / raised) or the Holy Artifact (waiting / engraving / done). The title counts how many are done.

#Parties

  1. Party header - "Party " in its colour, alive count, its current focus target ("on C2 Guard Captain") and task ("kill: ...", "escorting ", "waiting for Aldric's GO").
  2. Dead member - ✝ and faded, with an empty HP bar. Each living member shows HP and MP bars; ⚑ marks the flag holder.

#Events

Time (the leader's PC clock) and message. Typical events: the phase changes, "party X: attacking C2 Guard Captain", "server: a barracks has been seized", "all commanders dead — the command center opens", "server: has acquired the flag", the carrier's own reports ("casting Flag Display on the flag pole (1/4, 3 min ...)") and "RESULT: ...". The full log is Logs/siege.log.

#Waiting for the start

  1. Status line - the countdown "siege starts in 12m".
  2. Current phase - "Waiting for the start".
  3. Map - all parties stand at the green regroup point outside the walls. Objectives show "unknown" until the bots are close.

#The flag carrier

  1. Flag box - gold frame: "held by Quill (party Quill)", command center OPEN. If an enemy picks up the flag it says ENEMY in red.
  2. Phase - "Flag / artifact".
  3. Map - the pulsing yellow ring follows the carrier to the flag pole; every party walks with him.

#A castle siege

  1. Holy Artifact box - "not yet", " is engraving…" (gold frame) or ENGRAVED, and the engraver from the plan.
  2. Objectives - the gates (walls are left out), Control Tower 1-3 and the Holy Artifact.
  3. Map - the castle close-up with gates, towers and the artifact.

#After the siege

  1. Last siege - the title changes when the phase is "Done".
  2. RESULT - for example WON, "siege over", "wiped", "time is up", "stopped", "could not regroup in Giran", "could not reach the target".
  3. Flag box - "RAISED — fortress taken" after a fortress win.

The same result goes to the plan list ("bots: done — WON") and to party chat ("[siege] : WON — waiting for orders"). After a siege every leader stays put until you give the next order.

#How to watch and stop a siege

  1. Tap the red banner (or Live view on the Fortresses / Castles tab).
  2. Follow the phase timeline and the events.
  3. To stop: give !siege stop to the main party from the command center ("Stop the siege"). Every party stops; the result becomes "stopped".

#Notes

  • The live view only reads; it has no buttons that change anything.
  • Only the main leader writes the file. The other party leaders send him what they see every 2 seconds, so objectives far from him can still show a status.
  • Gate HP and the flag pole come from server packets read only during the siege (untested); if they are missing, gates show "unknown".

#Party live states

Most of the time a party card on the Parties tab looks calm: member rows, a map, the hunting spot line. When something happens, the card shows it live: a character that escapes from a fight gets an escape box with its own mini map, a long cast gets a cast bar, a leader on a rescue trip says where he is going, the hunting-spot status follows the trip, rotations and occupied spots appear, and hunting pairs show which group fights which monster.

All of it comes from the bots' live state files (Logs/swarm_state_<name>.json, written every few seconds by swarm.js) and is drawn only while it is fresh (a character that has not reported for 30 seconds shows none of it). While somebody escapes or casts, the tab refreshes every 1.5 seconds instead of every 4. Nothing here needs a button: you only watch. Words like CC, escape, SoE and .townname are in the glossary.

#Escape box

A character that is alone in a fight (no living teammate within 2500 on its floor, outside towns, raids and instances) escapes by itself: healers after 6 seconds, others below 50 % HP, with 3 or more attackers, or after 45 seconds. It puts attackers to sleep or roots them (CC), runs to a safe spot, waits until nothing hits it, and as the last step uses .townname (a Scroll of Escape only as a fallback). At most 5 rounds. Meanwhile the party leader may come to help (see Rescue trip).

While it runs, a red-bordered box opens under the member's row:

  1. Status line - Escape (why · dungeon — floor) round n/5 · HP n % · then the steps so far: each CC that worked (CC: Sleep on Death Knight ✓ 24s = seconds left), the current phase in bold, the monsters on the character (on me: Liangma, Death Knight (sleep)) and the leader (Aldric 2.8k away — coming).
  2. Step text - the bot's own words for this round.
  3. Mini map - a square map around the character:
    • the character (party colour, white ring) with its name,
    • monsters within 1600: red dots; a big dot with an orange ring and its name + level = it targets or hits the character; purple = crowd-controlled, with a mark (zZ sleep, ⚓ root, ✶ hold / stun, ! fear, ~ slow, ☮ peace, … silence),
    • target: the yellow circle with its label (safe spot: corridor between …) and the yellow dashed path to it,
    • safe spots: green diamonds with their names,
    • rooms nearby (in a dungeon): red dashed outlines,
    • the leader: a blue dot ★ Aldric (coming); when he is outside the map, a blue dashed line points to him with his distance.

The phase in the status line is one of:

Phase Text Meaning
cc crowd control casting a sleep / root / fear … on an attacker
run running to <safe spot> (n left) walking to the target on the map
wait waiting — no hits for n s standing still until nothing hits it for a while
rescue waiting for <leader> the leader is coming; the character holds at a safe spot instead of leaving
town .townname the .townname command is sent (a cast bar shows the wait)
soe Scroll of Escape fallback when .townname did not work

For two minutes after the end, a thin box stays with the result:

  1. Escape OK (green) - used .townname, Scroll of Escape, the leader came, or the fight ended - and the time.
  2. Escape FAILED (red) - died or gave up (still stuck after 5 rounds and a 5-minute wait).

The second picture also shows an escape in the .townname phase with its cast bar:

The same escape is written to the character's notes, its intent log (What they do) and Logs/escape.log.

#Cast bar

A long cast (1.5 seconds or more, or any resurrection / return / escape / summon skill), a Scroll of Escape, a .townname wait or a crowd-control skill shows as a bar under the member row:

  1. Casting Resurrection → Cassius - skill icon, skill name and target; the bar fills from the cast's start, the number is the time left (finishing… at the end).
  2. CC Sleep → Death Knight - a crowd-control skill.
  3. Casting Scroll of Escape - the scroll's icon.
  4. Interrupted - a red bar with the reason (interrupted, refused, resisted, no teleport). A finished cast turns green. Both stay for 20 seconds.

A .townname wait reads Waiting for .giran → giran with the map icon; the bar runs for the 20 seconds the bot waits for the server's answer.

#Rescue trip

When a teammate escapes alone, the leader goes to help (whatever he was doing), if the way takes less than 15 minutes. In a dungeon he plans the way across floors: walk to the floor teleporter, take it, walk to the teammate. The team comes along.

  1. The leader's task line - rescue Bryndis: Ponti: down to the 1st floor (2/4, ETA 2 min): the step he is on, out of how many, and the time left.
  2. The teammate's escape box - phase waiting for Aldric, and Aldric 4.1k away — coming. The mini map points to the leader with a blue dashed line when he is outside it. The teammate holds at a safe spot instead of leaving with .townname.

If the leader cannot come (no way found, or the way is too long) he writes it into party chat and his notes, and the teammate escapes by itself. Every rescue step is also written to Logs/dungeon.log.

#Hunting-spot status

When you choose a hunting spot on the dashboard, the spot line of the party card follows the leader's trip live: chosen 06:54 · travelling · ETA 1:20, then in the room ✓. If other players hunt there: occupied by others → auto · retry in 4:10; if the trip fails: not reachable now → auto; if the Seven Signs close a catacomb: closed (Seven Signs) → auto until …; above the safe level: needs your OK with an Override… button. Every state is shown and explained on the Parties page: Live status of your choice.

While the party walks to the chosen room, the party map draws it as a white dashed outline with the status, and inside a dungeon the leader's live route along the hallway centrelines (green, next waypoint ringed) and a red stuck ring on anyone who does not move (see Party map):

#Occupied spots (other players)

The leader watches who else is near the hunting spot. The bots leave a spot to other players when 2 or more players hunt there for 20 seconds, 1 player with a summon for 20 seconds, or 1 player alone in a small area for 120 seconds (they never fight over a spot), and keep away from it for a few minutes. You see this in three places:

  • the spot line: occupied by others → auto · retry in … when it was your chosen spot (picture above);
  • the party map: an orange note left, occupied: <spot> by <players> (n min) at the top left;
  • the hunting-spot picker: a red chip occupied by … (n min) on the place, and red rooms / areas on its maps.

Tick stay even if occupied in the picker to keep a party there anyway. The data is shared between your parties through Logs/spot_claims.json (each party's claim and the spots its leader saw occupied). The leader's last check (who is near the spot, under which rule) is also kept in his state file as spotWatch and written to his notes and Logs/dungeon.log when it changes; the dashboard does not draw it separately.

#Rotation

With several rooms or field areas chosen, the spot line shows a rotation chip (rotating 4 rooms (in order): now 1 · 6 here) and the party map numbers the next rooms with the monsters expected there. The party moves on when its room or area is empty (about 35 seconds without a monster), occupied, or taken by another of your parties.

Details: Rotation between rooms or areas.

#Hunting pairs live

With tactics On (or Auto and the party strong enough), the leader splits the damage dealers into groups. The tactics box of the party card shows them live, and each member's task line names its group and monster:

  1. pairs ON and the reason.
  2. One chip per group - Corwin + Delphine → Giggling Wind 48%; looking = no monster yet; gold (helping Corwin) = this group helps another group.
  3. Member task lines - pair Corwin+Delphine → Giggling Wind 48%, pair …: back toward Valerius (leash 900).

In Auto mode the summary shows pairs off and why (auto: team HP average 62 % (needs 70 % for a minute)). Settings and rules: Tactics box.

#Command reference

This chapter lists every command the dashboard can send: 133 commands in 13 categories. 91 are swarm commands (!, 66 different first words), 34 are L2Swarm chat-box commands (/, 32 different first words) and 8 are dashboard actions. Safety: 20 safe, 99 confirm, 14 destructive.

The list is generated from the command catalog Dashboard/commands.js. That one file feeds both the command center on the page and the server-side checks, so this reference always matches what the dashboard really sends. Words in the glossary are explained there.

#How to send a command

You have four ways. They all end up as the same chat line or action:

  1. Command center (best): click the search field at the top of the dashboard (or press Ctrl K / / on a PC), type a few letters of the command, fill in the form, pick who gets it and press Send. You see exactly what is sent before you confirm. See Command center.
  2. Commands sheet: the Commands button on a party card (Parties tab) or All commands for <name>... on a character page opens every command that fits that party or character, sorted by category.
  3. Quick buttons: the party card has Status, Level, Supply, Collect, Class, Buff and Stop; the character page has Class change, Rebuff and Escape. They send the matching ! command after one confirmation.
  4. By hand in L2Swarm: type the swarm command in the chat box of the party leader's L2Swarm window with a # in front, for example #!level. # makes it a party chat line, which every window of the party reads. Do not type a bare !level: in the game a leading ! means shout, and the line would go to everyone in the region. A character without a party gets the line as normal chat (the dashboard does that by itself). L2Swarm's own / commands are typed in that character's chat box as they are.

#The three kinds of command

Starts with Kind Who receives it
! Swarm command, handled by our script swarm.js Party target: once, as party chat from the party leader; the whole party hears it. Character target: party chat from that character; only its own window obeys (a party leader's own line is heard by his whole party). All parties: once per party leader. Clan: every clan member.
/ L2Swarm chat-box command (built into L2Swarm) Sent to every chosen character one by one. A party target means each member.
@ Account action (@login, @logout) Opens or closes the account in L2Swarm for each chosen character.

A few entries have no character at all (client mode switches and the PC buttons): the dashboard does those itself.

#Who acts

Many swarm commands are heard by the whole party, but only some of the characters act on them:

  • leader: The party leader acts; the other members follow him (party target = the party leader hears it in party chat and leads).
  • each: Every window that hears it acts (party target = every member of that party).
  • self: Each character acts for itself; an optional name argument limits it to that one character.
  • clanleader: Only the clan leader's window acts; the target is always the clan leader.
  • L2Swarm (/) commands and dashboard actions: each chosen character does it.

#Safety classes

  • safe - only reports or a dry run; still asks once.
  • confirm - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy).
  • destructive - asks once, then you must type YES; the server refuses it without that.

Every order shows a confirmation first (who gets it, how many characters, who is busy and will drop what they are doing). Passwords can never be read or set from the dashboard, and /config save never takes a file name (saving to another file would re-point the account).

#Templates

The Sends line shows the exact text. {name} is replaced by what you fill in. A part in [ ... ] is left out when the argument inside it is empty, for example !sell[ {name}] becomes !sell or !sell Bryndis.

#Free text

In the search field you can also type a plain phrase and choose Tell them "...". The dashboard server turns it into a command when you send it; the result line (and the message line under the header) shows what it became. It understands (case does not matter, "please", "now", "the", "team", "all" are ignored):

You type Becomes
restock, supply, supplies, buy supplies, shop scrolls !supply
collect, collect adena !collect
park, wait at grocer (optional: grocer, warehouse, weapons, start) !park grocer (or the place you named)
class change, change class, profession !classchange
forward drop on / forward drop off !cabinet Forward Drop on / off
level, autolevel, grind, farm xp, lvl !level
kill raid boss Bifrons, do raid boss Bifrons, raid Bifrons !mission raid Bifrons
kill / attack <monster> !kill <monster>
kamaloka 39, hall 33, labyrinth 56 (any two-digit level) !mission kamaloka 39
kamaloka, dungeon, instance !mission kamaloka
stop mission, abort mission !mission stop
stop, halt, pause !stop
status, report !status
regroup, go home, home !level
buff, rebuff !buff
escape, soe !soe
giran (or .giran, any of the 11 towns) !town giran
town aden, .town aden !town aden
teleport to Ruins of Agony, gk Ruins of Agony !gk Ruins of Agony
go to Helvetia, walk to Helvetia !goto Helvetia
mark Giran square, save place Giran square !mark Giran square

Anything else is refused with a hint. A typed !, / or @ command is checked against the catalog below.

#Town teleport (.town)

The leader stops hunting, fights off / steps away, regroups and uses .<town> (the server takes the party along). Giran = the safe regroup trip. A member alone ports itself only when the leader is gone.

  • Sends: !town {town}
  • Kind: ! swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
  • Arguments:
    • town - Town: town list (Giran, Gludin, Gludio, Dion, Oren, Aden, Hunters, Heine, Goddard, Rune, Schuttgart); default Giran
  • Who acts: The party leader acts; the other members follow him (party target = the party leader hears it in party chat and leads).
  • Targets: a party, one character, all parties, the clan, several characters; the form starts with a party.
  • Safety: confirm - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy).
  • Where: search field (command center) · party Commands sheet · character Commands sheet
  • Search words: teleport giran gludio dion aden oren heine rune goddard schuttgart hunters gludin
  • Example: !town Giran

#Go to an NPC (anywhere)…

NPC atlas (Scripts/data/npc_atlas.json): the leader takes the party to the best matching NPC — .town to its town, the dungeon way in + room by room (floor teleporters on the way), or teleport near + walk — and opens its dialog. By id (#30487), name (Penelope), role (grocer, gatekeeper, warehouse, priest of dawn, class master, blacksmith … + optional town: "grocer dion") or what it offers ("teleport:Cruma Tower 2nd floor"). Add a character name at the end for that character alone.

#STOP everything

Everyone idle + stop combat. The leader stays stopped (no auto-leveling) until the next order.

  • Sends: !stop
  • Kind: ! swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
  • Arguments: none
  • Who acts: Every window that hears it acts (party target = every member of that party).
  • Targets: a party, one character, all parties, the clan, several characters; the form starts with a party.
  • Safety: confirm - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy).
  • Where: search field (command center) · party Commands sheet · character Commands sheet
  • Search words: halt pause idle
  • Example: !stop

#Kill a monster by name

Everyone who hears it attacks the nearest monster with that name (within 4000).

  • Sends: !kill {name}
  • Kind: ! swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
  • Arguments:
    • name - Monster name: free text; example Bifrons
  • Who acts: Every window that hears it acts (party target = every member of that party).
  • Targets: a party, one character, all parties, the clan, several characters; the form starts with a party.
  • Safety: confirm - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy).
  • Where: search field (command center) · party Commands sheet · character Commands sheet
  • Search words: attack
  • Example: !kill Bifrons

#Help a character (party goes there)

The leader takes the team to that character and hunts around him until "!assist off".

  • Arguments:
    • who - Character to help: character list (grouped by party)
  • Who acts: The party leader acts; the other members follow him (party target = the party leader hears it in party chat and leads).

  • Safety: confirm - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy).
  • Where: search field (command center) · party Commands sheet · character Commands sheet
  • Search words: help follow
  • Example: !assist Bryndis

#Override: cast a skill

That character casts the skill once (skill id), on: boss | focus | self | <teammate> (default: its target / the boss).

  • Sends: !ov {name} cast {skill}[ {on}]
  • Kind: ! swarm command (our script; sent as party chat)
  • Arguments:
    • name - Character: character list (grouped by party)
    • skill - Skill id: a number; example 1015
    • on - On (boss / focus / self / name): free text; example boss; optional
  • Who acts: Each character acts for itself; an optional name argument limits it to that one character.
  • Targets: one character; the form starts with one character.
  • Safety: confirm - changes what they do; asks once (who, how many, who is busy). (This safety applies only to this exact form of the command.)
  • Where: search field (command center) · character Commands sheet
  • Search words: override skill cast heal nuke
  • Example: !ov Bryndis cast 1015 boss
